6.67.d: विश्वेषां वः सतां ज्येष्ठतमा गीर्भिर्मित्रावरुणा वावृधध्यै । सं या रश्मेव यमतुर्यमिष्ठा द्वा जनाँ असमा बाहुभिः स्वैः ॥
6.67.e: NOW Mitra-Varuṇa shall be exalted high by your songs, noblest of all existing;  They who, as ’twere with reins are best Controllers, unequalled with their arms to check the people.

6.67.d: इयं मद्वां प्र स्तृणीते मनीषोप प्रिया नमसा बर्हिरच्छ । यन्तं नो मित्रावरुणावधृष्टं छर्दिर्यद्वां वरूथ्यं सुदानू ॥
6.67.e: To you Two Gods is this my thought extended, turned to the sacred grass with loving homage.  Give us, O Mitra-Varuṇa, a dwelling safe from attack, which ye shall guard, Boon-Givers!

6.67.d: आ यातं मित्रावरुणा सुशस्त्युप प्रिया नमसा हूयमाना । सं यावप्नःस्थो अपसेव जनाञ्छ्रुधीयतश्चिद्यतथो महित्वा ॥
6.67.e: Come hither, Mitra-Varuṇa, invited with eulogies and loving adoration,  Ye who with your might, as Work-Controllers, urge even men who quickly hear to labour.

6.67.d: अश्वा न या वाजिना पूतबन्धू ऋता यद्गर्भमदितिर्भरध्यै । प्र या महि महान्ता जायमाना घोरा मर्ताय रिपवे नि दीधः ॥
6.67.e: Whom, of pure origin, like two strong horses, Aditi bore as babes in proper season,  Whom, Mighty at your birth, the Mighty Goddess brought forth as terrors to the mortal foeman.

6.67.d: विश्वे यद्वां मंहना मन्दमानाः क्षत्रं देवासो अदधुः सजोषाः । परि यद्भूथो रोदसी चिदुर्वी सन्ति स्पशो अदब्धासो अमूराः ॥
6.67.e: As all the Gods in their great joy and gladness gave you with one accord your high dominion,  As ye surround both worlds, though wide and spacious your spies are ever true and never bewildered.

6.67.d: ता हि क्षत्रं धारयेथे अनु द्यून्दृंहेथे सानुमुपमादिव द्योः । दृळ्हो नक्षत्र उत विश्वदेवो भूमिमातान्द्यां धासिनायोः ॥
6.67.e: So, through the days maintaining princely power. ye prop the height as ’twere from loftiest heaven.  The Star of all the Gods, established, filleth the heaven and earth with food of man who liveth.

6.67.d: ता विग्रं धैथे जठरं पृणध्या आ यत्सद्म सभृतयः पृणन्ति । न मृष्यन्ते युवतयोऽवाता वि यत्पयो विश्वजिन्वा भरन्ते ॥
6.67.e: Take the strong drink, to quaff till ye are sated, when he and his attendants fill the chamber.  The young Maids brook not that none seeks to win them, when, Quickeners of all! they scatter moisture.

6.67.d: ता जिह्वया सदमेदं सुमेधा आ यद्वां सत्यो अरतिर्ऋते भूत् । तद्वां महित्वं घृतान्नावस्तु युवं दाशुषे वि चयिष्टमंहः ॥
6.67.e: So with your tongue come ever, when your envoy, faithful and very wise, attends our worship.  Nourished by holy oil! he this yGur glory: annihilate the sacrificer's trouble.

6.67.d: प्र यद्वां मित्रावरुणा स्पूर्धन्प्रिया धाम युवधिता मिनन्ति । न ये देवास ओहसा न मर्ता अयज्ञसाचो अप्यो न पुत्राः ॥
6.67.e: When, Mitra-Varuṇa, they strive against you and break tlie friendly laws ye have established,  They, neither Gods nor men in estimation, like Api's sons have godless sacrifices.

6.67.d: वि यद्वाचं कीस्तासो भरन्ते शंसन्ति के चिन्निविदो मनानाः । आद्वां ब्रवाम सत्यान्युक्था नकिर्देवेभिर्यतथो महित्वा ॥
6.67.e: When singers in their song uplift their voices, some chant the Nivid texts with steady purpose.  Then may we sing you lauds that shall be fruitful: dp ye not rival all the Gods in greatness?

6.67.d: अवोरित्था वां छर्दिषो अभिष्टौ युवोर्मित्रावरुणावस्कृधोयु । अनु यद्गावः स्फुरानृजिप्यं धृष्णुं यद्रणे वृषणं युनजन् ॥
6.67.e: O Mitra-Varuṇa, may your large bounty come to us hither, near to this our dwelling,  When the kine haste to us, and when they harness the fleet-foot mettled stallion for the battle.

6.68.d: श्रुष्टी वां यज्ञ उद्यतः सजोषा मनुष्वद्वृक्तबर्हिषो यजध्यै । आ य इन्द्रावरुणाविषे अद्य महे सुम्नाय मह आववर्तत् ॥
6.68.e: HIS honouring rite whose grass is trimmed is offered swiftly to you, in Manu's wise, accordant,  The rite which Indra-Varuṇa shall carry this day to high success and glorious issue.

6.68.d: ता हि श्रेष्ठा देवताता तुजा शूराणां शविष्ठा ता हि भूतम् । मघोनां मंहिष्ठा तुविशुष्म ऋतेन वृत्रतुरा सर्वसेना ॥
6.68.e: For at Gods’ worship they are best through vigour; they have become the strongest of the Heroes;  With mighty strength, most liberal of the Princes, Chiefs of the host, by Law made Vṛtra's slayers.

6.68.d: ता गृणीहि नमस्येभिः शूषैः सुम्नेभिरिन्द्रावरुणा चकाना । वज्रेणान्यः शवसा हन्ति वृत्रं सिषक्त्यन्यो वृजनेषु विप्रः ॥
6.68.e: Praise those Twain Gods for powers that merit worship, Indra and Varuṇa, for bliss, the joyous.  One with his might and thunderbolt slays Vṛtra; the other as a Sage stands near in troubles.

6.68.d: ग्नाश्च यन्नरश्च वावृधन्त विश्वे देवासो नरां स्वगूर्ताः । प्रैभ्य इन्द्रावरुणा महित्वा द्यौश्च पृथिवि भूतमुर्वी ॥
6.68.e: Though dames and men have waxen strong and mighty, and all the Gods selfpraised among the Heroes,  Ye, Indra-Varuṇa, have in might surpassed them, and thus were ye spread wide, O Earth and Heaven.

6.68.d: स इत्सुदानुः स्ववाँ ऋतावेन्द्रा यो वां वरुण दाशति त्मन् । इषा स द्विषस्तरेद्दास्वान्वंसद्रयिं रयिवतश्च जनान् ॥
6.68.e: Righteous is he, and liberal and helpful who, Indra-Varuṇa, brings you gifts with gladness.  That bounteous man through food shall conquer faemen, and win him opulence and wealthy people.

6.68.d: यं युवं दाश्वध्वराय देवा रयिं धत्थो वसुमन्तं पुरुक्षुम् । अस्मे स इन्द्रावरुणावपि ष्यात्प्र यो भनक्ति वनुषामशस्तीः ॥
6.68.e: May wealth which ye bestow in food and treasure on him who brings you gifts and sacrifices,  Wealth, Gods! which breaks the curse of those who vex us, be, Indra-Varuṇa, e’en our own possession.

6.68.d: उत नः सुत्रात्रो देवगोपाः सूरिभ्य इन्द्रावरुणा रयिः ष्यात् । येषां शुष्मः पृतनासु साह्वान्प्र सद्यो द्युम्ना तिरते ततुरिः ॥
6.68.e: So also, Indra-Varuṇa, may our princes have riches swift to save, with Gods to guard them-  They whose great might gives victory in battles, and their triumphant glory spreads with swiftness.

6.68.d: नू न इन्द्रावरुणा गृणाना पृङ्क्तं रयिं सौश्रवसाय देवा । इत्था गृणन्तो महिनस्य शर्धोऽपो न नावा दुरिता तरेम ॥
6.68.e: Indra. and Varuṇa, Gods whom we are lauding, mingle ye wealth with our heroic glory.  May we, who praise the strength of what is mighty, pass dangers, as with boats we cross the waters.

6.68.d: प्र सम्राजे बृहते मन्म नु प्रियमर्च देवाय वरुणाय सप्रथः । अयं य उर्वी महिना महिव्रतः क्रत्वा विभात्यजरो न शोचिषा ॥
6.68.e: Now will I sing a dear and far-extending hymn to Varuṇa the God, sublime, imperial Lord,  Who, mighty Governor, Eternal, as with flame, illumines both wide worlds with majesty and power.

6.68.d: इन्द्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतं सोमं पिबतं मद्यं धृतव्रता । युवो रथो अध्वरं देववीतये प्रति स्वसरमुप याति पीतये ॥
6.68.e: True to Law, Indra-Varuṇa, drinkers of the juice, drink this pressed Soma which shall give you rapturous joy.  Your chariot cometh to the banquet of the Gods, to sacrifice, as it were home, that ye may drink.

6.68.d: इन्द्रावरुणा मधुमत्तमस्य वृष्णः सोमस्य वृषणा वृषेथाम् । इदं वामन्धः परिषिक्तमस्मे आसद्यास्मिन्बर्हिषि मादयेथाम् ॥
6.68.e: Indra and Varuṇa, drink your fill, ye Heroes, of this invigorating sweetest Soma.  This juice is shed by us that ye may quaff it: on this trimmed grass be seated, and rejoice you

6.69.d: सं वां कर्मणा समिषा हिनोमीन्द्राविष्णू अपसस्पारे अस्य । जुषेथां यज्ञं द्रविणं च धत्तमरिष्टैर्नः पथिभिः पारयन्ता ॥
6.69.e: INDRA and Viṣṇu, at my task's completion I urge you on with food and sacred service.  Accept the sacrifice and grant us riches, leading us on by unobstructed pathways.

6.69.d: या विश्वासां जनितारा मतीनामिन्द्राविष्णू कलशा सोमधाना । प्र वां गिरः शस्यमाना अवन्तु प्र स्तोमासो गीयमानासो अर्कैः ॥
6.69.e: Ye who inspire all hymns, Indra and Viṣṇu, ye vessels who contain the Soma juices,  May hymns of praise that now are sung address you, the lauds that are recited by the singers.

6.69.d: इन्द्राविष्णू मदपती मदानामा सोमं यातं द्रविणो दधाना । सं वामञ्जन्त्वक्तुभिर्मतीनां सं स्तोमासः शस्यमानास उक्थैः ॥
6.69.e: Lords of joy-giving draughts, Indra and Viṣṇu, come, giving gifts of treasure, to the Soma.  With brilliant rays of hymns let chanted praises, repeated with the lauds, adorn and deck you.

6.69.d: आ वामश्वासो अभिमातिषाह इन्द्राविष्णू सधमादो वहन्तु । जुषेथां विश्वा हवना मतीनामुप ब्रह्माणि शृणुतं गिरो मे ॥
6.69.e: May your foe-conquering horses bring you hither, Indra and Viṣṇu, sharers of the banquet.  Of all our hymns accept the invocations list to my prayers and hear the songs I sing you.

6.69.d: इन्द्राविष्णू तत्पनयाय्यं वां सोमस्य मद उरु चक्रमाथे । अकृणुतमन्तरिक्षं वरीयोऽप्रथतं जीवसे नो रजांसि ॥
6.69.e: This your deed, Indra-Viṣṇu, must be lauded: widely ye strode in the wild joy of Soma.  Ye made the firmament of larger compass, and made the regions broad for our existence.

6.69.d: इन्द्राविष्णू हविषा वावृधानाग्राद्वाना नमसा रातहव्या । घृतासुती द्रविणं धत्तमस्मे समुद्रः स्थः कलशः सोमधानः ॥
6.69.e: Strengthened with sacred offerings, IndraViṣṇu, first eaters, served with worship ana oblation,  Fed with the holy oil, vouchsafe us riches ye are the lake, the vat that holds the Soma.

6.69.d: इन्द्राविष्णू पिबतं मध्वो अस्य सोमस्य दस्रा जठरं पृणेथाम् । आ वामन्धांसि मदिराण्यग्मन्नुप ब्रह्माणि शृणुतं हवं मे ॥
6.69.e: Drink of this meath, O Indra, thou, and Viṣṇu; drink ye your fill of Soma, Wonder-Workers.  The sweet exhilarating juice hath reached you. Hear ye my prayers, give ear unto my calling.

6.69.d: उभा जिग्यथुर्न परा जयेथे न परा जिग्ये कतरश्चनैनोः । इन्द्रश्च विष्णो यदपस्पृधेथां त्रेधा सहस्रं वि तदैरयेथाम् ॥
6.69.e: Ye Twain have conquered, ne’er have yc been conquered: never hath either of the Twain been vanquished.  Ye, Indra-Viṣṇu, when ye fought the battle, produced this infinite with three divisions.

6.70.d: घृतवती भुवनानामभिश्रियोर्वी पृथ्वी मधुदुघे सुपेशसा । द्यावापृथिवी वरुणस्य धर्मणा विष्कभिते अजरे भूरिरेतसा ॥
6.70.e: FILLED full of fatness, compassing all things that be, wide, spacious, dropping meath, beautiful in their form,  The Heaven and the Earth by Varuṇa's decree, unwasting, rich in germs, stand parted each from each.

6.70.d: असश्चन्ती भूरिधारे पयस्वती घृतं दुहाते सुकृते शुचिव्रते । राजन्ती अस्य भुवनस्य रोदसी अस्मे रेतः सिञ्चतं यन्मनुर्हितम् ॥
6.70.e: The Everlasting Pair, with full streams, rich in milk, in their pure rule pour fatness for the pious man.  Ye who are Regents of this world, O Earth and Heaven, pour into us the genial flow that prospers meit.

6.70.d: यो वामृजवे क्रमणाय रोदसी मर्तो ददाश धिषणे स साधति । प्र प्रजाभिर्जायते धर्मणस्परि युवोः सिक्ता विषुरूपाणि सव्रता ॥
6.70.e: Whoso, for righteous life, pours offerings to you, O Heaven and Earth, ye Hemispheres, that man succeeds.  He in his seed is born again and spreads by Law: from you flow things diverse in form, but ruled alike.

6.70.d: घृतेन द्यावापृथिवी अभीवृते घृतश्रिया घृतपृचा घृतावृधा । उर्वी पृथ्वी होतृवूर्ये पुरोहिते ते इद्विप्रा ईळते सुम्नमिष्टये ॥
6.70.e: Enclosed in fatness, Heaven and Earth are bright therewith: they mingle with the fatness which they still increase.  Wide, broad, set foremost at election of the priest, to them the singers pray for bliss to further them.

6.70.d: मधु नो द्यावापृथिवी मिमिक्षतां मधुश्चुता मधुदुघे मधुव्रते । दधाने यज्ञं द्रविणं च देवता महि श्रवो वाजमस्मे सुवीर्यम् ॥
6.70.e: May Heaven and Earth pour down the balmy rain for us, balm-dropping, yielding balm, with balm upon your path,  Bestowing by your Godhead sacrifice and wealth, great fame and strength for us and good heroic might.

6.70.d: ऊर्जं नो द्यौश्च पृथिवी च पिन्वतां पिता माता विश्वविदा सुदंससा । संरराणे रोदसी विश्वशम्भुवा सनिं वाजं रयिमस्मे समिन्वताम् ॥
6.70.e: May Heaven and Earth make food swell plenteously for us, all-knowing Father, jother, wondrous in their works.  Pouring out bounties, may, in union, both the Worlds, all beneficial, send us gain, and power, and wealth.

6.71.d: उदु ष्य देवः सविता हिरण्यया बाहू अयंस्त सवनाय सुक्रतुः । घृतेन पाणी अभि प्रुष्णुते मखो युवा सुदक्षो रजसो विधर्मणि ॥
6.71.e: FULL of effectual wisdom Savitar the God hath stretched out golden arms that he may bring forth life.  Young and most skilful, while he holds the region up, the Warrior sprinkles fatness over both his hands.

6.71.d: देवस्य वयं सवितुः सवीमनि श्रेष्ठे स्याम वसुनश्च दावने । यो विश्वस्य द्विपदो यश्चतुष्पदो निवेशने प्रसवे चासि भूमनः ॥
6.71.e: May we enjoy the noblest vivifying force of Savitar the God, that he may give us wealth:  For thou art mighty to produce and lull to rest the world of life that moves on two feet and on four.

6.71.d: अदब्धेभिः सवितः पायुभिष्ट्वं शिवेभिरद्य परि पाहि नो गयम् । हिरण्यजिह्वः सुविताय नव्यसे रक्षा माकिर्नो अघशंस ईशत ॥
6.71.e: Protect our habitation, Savitar, this day, with guardian aids around, auspicious, firm and true.  God of the golden tongue, keep us for newest bliss: let not the evil-wisher have us in his power.

6.71.d: उदु ष्य देवः सविता दमूना हिरण्यपाणिः प्रतिदोषमस्थात् । अयोहनुर्यजतो मन्द्रजिह्व आ दाशुषे सुवति भूरि वामम् ॥
6.71.e: This Savitar the God, the golden-handed, Friend of the home, hath risen to meet the twilight.  With cheeks of brass, with pleasant tongue, the Holy, he sends the worshipper rich gifts in plenty.

6.71.d: उदू अयाँ उपवक्तेव बाहू हिरण्यया सविता सुप्रतीका । दिवो रोहांस्यरुहत्पृथिव्या अरीरमत्पतयत्कच्चिदभ्वम् ॥
6.71.e: Like a Director, Savitar hath extended his golden arms, exceeding fair to look on.  He hath gone up the heights of earth and heaven, and made each monster fall and cease from troubling.

6.71.d: वाममद्य सवितर्वाममु श्वो दिवेदिवे वाममस्मभ्यं सावीः । वामस्य हि क्षयस्य देव भूरेरया धिया वामभाजः स्याम ॥
6.71.e: Fair wealth, O Savitar, to-day, to-morrow, fair wealth produce for us each day that passes.  May we through this our song be happy gainers, God, of a fair and spacious habitation.

6.72.d: इन्द्रासोमा महि तद्वां महित्वं युवं महानि प्रथमानि चक्रथुः । युवं सूर्यं विविदथुर्युवं स्व१र्विश्वा तमांस्यहतं निदश्च ॥
6.72.e: GREAT is this might of yours, Indra and Soma: the first high exploits were your own achievements.  Ye found the Sun ye found the light of heaven: ye killed all darkness and the Gods’ blasphemers.

6.72.d: इन्द्रासोमा वासयथ उषासमुत्सूर्यं नयथो ज्योतिषा सह । उप द्यां स्कम्भथुः स्कम्भनेनाप्रथतं पृथिवीं मातरं वि ॥
6.72.e: Ye, Indra-Soma, gave her light to Morning, and led the Sun on high with all his splendour.  Ye stayed the heaven with a supporting pillar, and spread abroad apart, the Earth, the Mother.

6.72.d: इन्द्रासोमावहिमपः परिष्ठां हथो वृत्रमनु वां द्यौरमन्यत । प्रार्णांस्यैरयतं नदीनामा समुद्राणि पप्रथुः पुरूणि ॥
6.72.e: Ye slew the flood -obstructing serpent Vṛtra, Indra and Soma: Heaven approved your exploit.  Ye urged to speed the currents of the rivers, and many seas have ye filled full with waters.

6.72.d: इन्द्रासोमा पक्वमामास्वन्तर्नि गवामिद्दधथुर्वक्षणासु । जगृभथुरनपिनद्धमासु रुशच्चित्रासु जगतीष्वन्तः ॥
6.72.e: Ye in the unripe udders of the milch-kine have set the ripe milk, Indra, thou, and Soma.  Ye have held fast the unimpeded whiteness within these many-coloured moving creatures.

6.72.d: इन्द्रासोमा युवमङ्ग तरुत्रमपत्यसाचं श्रुत्यं रराथे । युवं शुष्मं नर्यं चर्षणिभ्यः सं विव्यथुः पृतनाषाहमुग्रा ॥
6.72.e: Verily ye bestow, Indra and Soma, wealth, famed, victorious, passing to our children.  Ye have invested men, ye Mighty Beings, with manly strength that conquers in the battle.

6.73.d: यो अद्रिभित्प्रथमजा ऋतावा बृहस्पतिराङ्गिरसो हविष्मान् । द्विबर्हज्मा प्राघर्मसत्पिता न आ रोदसी वृषभो रोरवीति ॥
6.73.e: SERVED with oblations, first-born, mountain-render, Aṅgiras' son, Bṛhaspati, the Holy,  With twice-firm path, dwelling in light, our Father, roars loudly, as a bull, to Earth and Heaven.

6.73.d: जनाय चिद्य ईवत उ लोकं बृहस्पतिर्देवहूतौ चकार । घ्नन्वृत्राणि वि पुरो दर्दरीति जयञ्छत्रूँरमित्रान्पृत्सु साहन् ॥
6.73.e: Bṛhaspati, who made for such a people wide room and verge when Gods were invocated,  Slaying his enemies, breaks down their castles, quelling his foes and conquering those who hate him.

6.73.d: बृहस्पतिः समजयद्वसूनि महो व्रजान्गोमतो देव एषः । अपः सिषासन्त्स्व१रप्रतीतो बृहस्पतिर्हन्त्यमित्रमर्कैः ॥
6.73.e: Bṛhaspati in war hath won rich treasures, hath won, this God, the great stalls filled with cattle.  Striving to win waters and light, resistless, Bṛhaspati with lightning smites the foeman.

6.74.d: सोमारुद्रा धारयेथामसुर्यं१ प्र वामिष्टयोऽरमश्नुवन्तु । दमेदमे सप्त रत्ना दधाना शं नो भूतं द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे ॥
6.74.e: HOLD fast your Godlike sway, O Soma-Rudra: let these our sacrifices quickly reach you.  Placing in every house your seven great treasures, bring blessing to our quadrupeds and bipeds.

6.74.d: सोमारुद्रा वि वृहतं विषूचीममीवा या नो गयमाविवेश । आरे बाधेथां निर्ऋतिं पराचैरस्मे भद्रा सौश्रवसानि सन्तु ॥
6.74.e: Soma and Rudra, chase to every quarter the sickness that hath visited our dwelling.  Drive Nirrti away into the distance, and give us excellent and happy glories.

6.74.d: सोमारुद्रा युवमेतान्यस्मे विश्वा तनूषु भेषजानि धत्तम् । अव स्यतं मुञ्चतं यन्नो अस्ति तनूषु बद्धं कृतमेनो अस्मत् ॥
6.74.e: Provide, O Soma-Rudra, for our bodies all needful medicines to heal and cure us.  Set free and draw away the sin committed which we have still inherent in our persons.

6.74.d: तिग्मायुधौ तिग्महेती सुशेवौ सोमारुद्राविह सु मृळतं नः । प्र नो मुञ्चतं वरुणस्य पाशाद्गोपायतं नः सुमनस्यमाना ॥
6.74.e: Armed with keen shafts and weapons, kind and loving, be gracious unto us, Soma and Rudra.  Release us from the noose of Varuṇa; keep us from sorrow, in your tender loving-kindness.

6.75.d: जीमूतस्येव भवति प्रतीकं यद्वर्मी याति समदामुपस्थे । अनाविद्धया तन्वा जय त्वं स त्वा वर्मणो महिमा पिपर्तु ॥
6.75.e: THE warrior's look is like a thunderous rain-cloud's, when, armed with mail, he seeks the lap of battle.  Be thou victorious with unwounded body: so let the thickness of thy mail protect thee.

6.75.d: धन्वना गा धन्वनाजिं जयेम धन्वना तीव्राः समदो जयेम । धनुः शत्रोरपकामं कृणोति धन्वना सर्वाः प्रदिशो जयेम ॥
6.75.e: With Bow let us win kine, with Bow the battle, with Bow be victors in our hot encounters.  The Bow brings grief and sorrow to the foeman: armed with the Bow may we subdue all regions.

6.75.d: वक्ष्यन्तीवेदा गनीगन्ति कर्णं प्रियं सखायं परिषस्वजाना । योषेव शिङ्क्ते वितताधि धन्वञ्ज्या इयं समने पारयन्ती ॥
6.75.e: Close to his car, as fain to speak, She presses, holding her well-loved Friend in her embraces.  Strained on the Bow, She whispers like a woman-this Bowstring that preserves us in the combat.

6.75.d: ते आचरन्ती समनेव योषा मातेव पुत्रं बिभृतामुपस्थे । अप शत्रून्विध्यतां संविदाने आर्त्नी इमे विष्फुरन्ती अमित्रान् ॥
6.75.e: These, meeting like a woman and her lover, bear, mother-like, their child upon their bosom.  May the two Bow-ends, starting swift asunder, scatter, in unison, the foes who hate us.

6.75.d: बह्वीनां पिता बहुरस्य पुत्रश्चिश्चा कृणोति समनावगत्य । इषुधिः सङ्काः पृतनाश्च सर्वाः पृष्ठे निनद्धो जयति प्रसूतः ॥
6.75.e: With many a son, father of many daughters, He clangs and clashes as he goes to battle.  Slung on the back, pouring his brood, the Quiver vanquishes all opposing bands and armies.

6.75.d: रथे तिष्ठन्नयति वाजिनः पुरो यत्रयत्र कामयते सुषारथिः । अभीशूनां महिमानं पनायत मनः पश्चादनु यच्छन्ति रश्मयः ॥
6.75.e: Upstanding in the Car the skilful Charioteer guides his strong Horses on whithersoe’er he will.  See and admire the strength of those controlling Reins which from behind declare the will of him who drives.

6.75.d: तीव्रान्घोषान्कृण्वते वृषपाणयोऽश्वा रथेभिः सह वाजयन्तः । अवक्रामन्तः प्रपदैरमित्रान्क्षिणन्ति शत्रूँरनपव्ययन्तः ॥
6.75.e: Horses whose hoofs rain dust are neighing loudly, yoked to the Chariots, showing forth their vigour,  With their forefeet descending on the foemen, they, never flinching, trample and destroy them.

6.75.d: रथवाहनं हविरस्य नाम यत्रायुधं निहितमस्य वर्म । तत्रा रथमुप शग्मं सदेम विश्वाहा वयं सुमनस्यमानाः ॥
6.75.e: Car-bearer is the name of his oblation, whercon are laid his Weapons and his Armour.  So let us here, each day that passes, honour the helpful Car with hearts exceeding joyful.

6.75.d: स्वादुषंसदः पितरो वयोधाः कृच्छ्रेश्रितः शक्तीवन्तो गभीराः । चित्रसेना इषुबला अमृध्राः सतोवीरा उरवो व्रातसाहाः ॥
6.75.e: In sweet association lived the fathers who gave us life, profound and strong in trouble,  Unwearied, armed with shafts and wondrous weapons, free, real heroes, conquerors of armies.

6.75.d: ब्राह्मणासः पितरः सोम्यासः शिवे नो द्यावापृथिवी अनेहसा । पूषा नः पातु दुरितादृतावृधो रक्षा माकिर्नो अघशंस ईशत ॥
6.75.e: The Brahmans, and the Fathers meet for Soma-draughts, and, graciously inclined, unequalled Heaven and Earth.  Guard us trom evil, Pūṣan, guard us strengtheners of Law: let not the evil-wisher master us.

6.75.d: सुपर्णं वस्ते मृगो अस्या दन्तो गोभिः संनद्धा पतति प्रसूता । यत्रा नरः सं च वि च द्रवन्ति तत्रास्मभ्यमिषवः शर्म यंसन् ॥
6.75.e: Her tooth a deer, dressed in an eagle's feathers, bound with cow-hide, launched forth, She flieth onward.  There where the heroes speed hither and thither, there may the Arrows shelter and protect us.

6.75.d: ऋजीते परि वृङ्धि नोऽश्मा भवतु नस्तनूः । सोमो अधि ब्रवीतु नोऽदितिः शर्म यच्छतु ॥
6.75.e: Avoid us thou whose flight is straight, and let our bodies be as stone.  May Soma kindly speak to us, and Aditi protect us well.

6.75.d: आ जङ्घन्ति सान्वेषां जघनाँ उप जिघ्नते । अश्वाजनि प्रचेतसोऽश्वान्त्समत्सु चोदय ॥
6.75.e: He lays his blows upon their backs, he deals his blows upon their thighs.  Thou, Whip, who urgest horses, drive sagacious horses in the fray.

6.75.d: अहिरिव भोगैः पर्येति बाहुं ज्याया हेतिं परिबाधमानः । हस्तघ्नो विश्वा वयुनानि विद्वान्पुमान्पुमांसं परि पातु विश्वतः ॥
6.75.e: It compasses the arm with serpent windings, fending away the friction of the bowstring:  So may the Brace, well-skilled in all its duties, guard manfully the man from every quarter.

6.75.d: आलाक्ता या रुरुशीर्ष्ण्यथो यस्या अयो मुखम् । इदं पर्जन्यरेतस इष्वै देव्यै बृहन्नमः ॥
6.75.e: Now to the Shaft with venom smeared, tipped with deer-horn, with iron mouth,  Celestial, of Parjanya's seed, be this great adoration paid.

6.75.d: अवसृष्टा परा पत शरव्ये ब्रह्मसंशिते । गच्छामित्रान्प्र पद्यस्व मामीषां कं चनोच्छिषः ॥
6.75.e: Loosed from the Bowstring fly away, thou Arrow, sharpened by our prayer.  Go to the foemen, strike them home, and let not one be left alive.

6.75.d: यत्र बाणाः सम्पतन्ति कुमारा विशिखा इव । तत्रा नो ब्रह्मणस्पतिरदितिः शर्म यच्छतु विश्वाहा शर्म यच्छतु ॥
6.75.e: There where the flights of Arrows fall like boys whose locks are yet unshorn.  Even there may Brahmaṇaspati, and Aditi protect us well, protect us well through all our days.

6.75.d: मर्माणि ते वर्मणा छादयामि सोमस्त्वा राजामृतेनानु वस्ताम् । उरोर्वरीयो वरुणस्ते कृणोतु जयन्तं त्वानु देवा मदन्तु ॥
6.75.e: Thy vital parts I cover with thine Armour: with immortality King Soma clothe thee.  Varuṇa give thee what is more than ample, and in thy triumph may the Gods be joyful.

6.75.d: यो नः स्वो अरणो यश्च निष्ट्यो जिघांसति । देवास्तं सर्वे धूर्वन्तु ब्रह्म वर्म ममान्तरम् ॥
6.75.e: Whoso would kill us, whether he be a strange foe or one of us, May all the Gods discomfit him. My nearest, closest Mail is prayer.

7.1.d: अग्निं नरो दीधितिभिररण्योर्हस्तच्युती जनयन्त प्रशस्तम् । दूरेदृशं गृहपतिमथर्युम् ॥
7.1.e: THE men from fire-sticks, with their hands' swift movement, have, in deep thought, engendered glorious Agni,  Far-seen, with pointed flame, Lord of the homestead.

7.1.d: तमग्निमस्ते वसवो न्यृण्वन्त्सुप्रतिचक्षमवसे कुतश्चित् । दक्षाय्यो यो दम आस नित्यः ॥
7.1.e: The Vasus set that Agni in the dwelling, fair to behold, for help from every quarter:  Who, in the home for ever, must be honoured.

7.1.d: प्रेद्धो अग्ने दीदिहि पुरो नोऽजस्रया सूर्म्या यविष्ठ । त्वां शश्वन्त उप यन्ति वाजाः ॥
7.1.e: Shine thou before us, Agni, well-enkindled, with flame, Most Youthful God, that never fadeth.  To thee come all our sacrificial viands.

7.1.d: प्र ते अग्नयोऽग्निभ्यो वरं निः सुवीरासः शोशुचन्त द्युमन्तः । यत्रा नरः समासते सुजाताः ॥
7.1.e: Among all fires these fires have shone most brightly, splendid with light, begirt by noble heroes,  Where men of lofty birth sit down together.

7.1.d: दा नो अग्ने धिया रयिं सुवीरं स्वपत्यं सहस्य प्रशस्तम् । न यं यावा तरति यातुमावान् ॥
7.1.e: Victorious Agni, grant us wealth with wisdom, wealth with brave sons, famous and independent,  Which not a foe who deals in magic conquers.

7.1.d: उप यमेति युवतिः सुदक्षं दोषा वस्तोर्हविष्मती घृताची । उप स्वैनमरमतिर्वसूयुः ॥
7.1.e: To whom, the Strong, at morn and eve comes, maid-like, the ladle dropping oil, with its oblation.  Wealth-seeking comes to him his own devotion.

7.1.d: विश्वा अग्नेऽप दहारातीर्येभिस्तपोभिरदहो जरूथम् । प्र निस्वरं चातयस्वामीवाम् ॥
7.1.e: Burn up all malice with those flames, O Agni, wherewith of old thou burntest up Jarutha,  And drive away in silence pain and sickness.

7.1.d: आ यस्ते अग्न इधते अनीकं वसिष्ठ शुक्र दीदिवः पावक । उतो न एभिः स्तवथैरिह स्याः ॥
7.1.e: With him who lighteth up thy splendour, Agni, excellent, pure, refulgent, Purifier,  Be present, and with us through these our praises.

7.1.d: वि ये ते अग्ने भेजिरे अनीकं मर्ता नरः पित्र्यासः पुरुत्रा । उतो न एभिः सुमना इह स्याः ॥
7.1.e: Agni, the patriarchal men, the mortals who have in many places spread thy lustre,—  Be gracious to us here for their sake also.

7.1.d: इमे नरो वृत्रहत्येषु शूरा विश्वा अदेवीरभि सन्तु मायाः । ये मे धियं पनयन्त प्रशस्ताम् ॥
7.1.e: Let these men, heroes in the fight with foemen, prevail against all godless arts of 4magic,—  These who ipprove the noble song I sing thee.

7.1.d: मा शूने अग्ने नि षदाम नृणां माशेषसोऽवीरता परि त्वा । प्रजावतीषु दुर्यासु दुर्य ॥
7.1.e: Let us not sit in want of men, O Agni, without descendants, heroleu, about thee:  But, O House-Friend, in houses full of children.

7.1.d: यमश्वी नित्यमुपयाति यज्ञं प्रजावन्तं स्वपत्यं क्षयं नः । स्वजन्मना शेषसा वावृधानम् ॥
7.1.e: By sacrifice which the Steeds' Lord ever visits, there make our dwelling rich in seed and offspring,  Increasing still with lineal successors.

7.1.d: पाहि नो अग्ने रक्षसो अजुष्टात्पाहि धूर्तेरररुषो अघायोः । त्वा युजा पृतनायूँरभि ष्याम् ॥
7.1.e: Guard us, O Agni, from the hated demon, guard us from malice of the churlish sinner:  Allied with thee may I subdue assailants.

7.1.d: सेदग्निरग्नीँरत्यस्त्वन्यान्यत्र वाजी तनयो वीळुपाणिः । सहस्रपाथा अक्षरा समेति ॥
7.1.e: May this same fire of mine surpass all others, this fire where offspring, vigorous and firm-handed,  Wins, on a thousand paths, what ne’er shall perish.

7.1.d: सेदग्निर्यो वनुष्यतो निपाति समेद्धारमंहस उरुष्यात् । सुजातासः परि चरन्ति वीराः ॥
7.1.e: This is that Agni, saviour from the foeman, who guards the kindler of the flame from sorrow:  Heroes of noble lineage serve and tend him.

7.1.d: अयं सो अग्निराहुतः पुरुत्रा यमीशानः समिदिन्धे हविष्मान् । परि यमेत्यध्वरेषु होता ॥
7.1.e: This is that Agni, served in many places, whom the rich lord who brings oblation kindles,  And round him goes the priest at sacrifices.

7.1.d: त्वे अग्न आहवनानि भूरीशानास आ जुहुयाम नित्या । उभा कृण्वन्तो वहतू मियेधे ॥
7.1.e: Agni, may we with riches in possession bring thee continual ofierings in abundance,  Using both means to draw thee to our worship.

7.1.d: इमो अग्ने वीततमानि हव्याजस्रो वक्षि देवतातिमच्छ । प्रति न ईं सुरभीणि व्यन्तु ॥
7.1.e: Agni, bear thou, Eternal, these most welcome oblations to the Deities' assembly:  Let them enjoy our very fragrant presents.

7.1.d: मा नो अग्नेऽवीरते परा दा दुर्वाससेऽमतये मा नो अस्यै । मा नः क्षुधे मा रक्षस ऋतावो मा नो दमे मा वन आ जुहूर्थाः ॥
7.1.e: Give us not up, Agni, to want of heroes, to wretched clothes, to need, to destitution.  Yield us not, Holy One, to fiend or hunger; injure us not at home or in the forest.

7.1.d: नू मे ब्रह्माण्यग्न उच्छशाधि त्वं देव मघवद्भ्यः सुषूदः । रातौ स्यामोभयास आ ते यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.1.e: Give strength and power to these my prayers, O Agni; O God, pour blessings on our chiefs and nobles.  Grant that both we and they may share thy bounty. Ye Gods, protect us evermore with blessings.

7.1.d: त्वमग्ने सुहवो रण्वसंदृक्सुदीती सूनो सहसो दिदीहि । मा त्वे सचा तनये नित्य आ धङ्मा वीरो अस्मन्नर्यो वि दासीत् ॥
7.1.e: Thou Agni, swift to hear, art fair of aspect: beam forth, O Son of Strength, in full effulgence.  Let me not want, with thee, a son for ever: let not a manly hero ever fail us.

7.1.d: मा नो अग्ने दुर्भृतये सचैषु देवेद्धेष्वग्निषु प्र वोचः । मा ते अस्मान्दुर्मतयो भृमाच्चिद्देवस्य सूनो सहसो नशन्त ॥
7.1.e: Condemn us not to indigence, O Agni, beside these flaming fires which Gods have kindled;  Nor, even after fault, let thy displeasure, thine as a God, O Son of Strength, o’ertake us.

7.1.d: स मर्तो अग्ने स्वनीक रेवानमर्त्ये य आजुहोति हव्यम् । स देवता वसुवनिं दधाति यं सूरिरर्थी पृच्छमान एति ॥
7.1.e: O Agni, fair of face, the wealthy mortal who to the Immortal offers his oblation.  Hath him who wins him treasure by his Godhead, to whom the prince, in need, goes supplicating.

7.1.d: महो नो अग्ने सुवितस्य विद्वान्रयिं सूरिभ्य आ वहा बृहन्तम् । येन वयं सहसावन्मदेमाविक्षितास आयुषा सुवीराः ॥
7.1.e: Knowing our chief felicity, O Agni, bring hither ample riches to our nobles,  Wherewith we may enjoy ourselves, O Victor, with undiminished life and hero children.

7.1.d: नू मे ब्रह्माण्यग्न उच्छशाधि त्वं देव मघवद्भ्यः सुषूदः । रातौ स्यामोभयास आ ते यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.1.e: Give strength and power to these my prayers, O Agni; O God, pour blessings on bur chiefs and nobles.  Grant that both we and they may share thy bounty. Ye Gods, protect us evermore with blessings.

7.2.d: जुषस्व नः समिधमग्ने अद्य शोचा बृहद्यजतं धूममृण्वन् । उप स्पृश दिव्यं सानु स्तूपैः सं रश्मिभिस्ततनः सूर्यस्य ॥
7.2.e: GLADLY accept, this day, our fuel, Agni: send up thy sacred smoke and shine sublimely.  Touch the celestial summits with thy columns, and overspread thee with the rays of Sūrya.

7.2.d: नराशंसस्य महिमानमेषामुप स्तोषाम यजतस्य यज्ञैः । ये सुक्रतवः शुचयो धियंधाः स्वदन्ति देवा उभयानि हव्या ॥
7.2.e: With sacrifice to these we men will honour the majesty of holy Narāśaṁsa-  To these the pure, most wise, the thought. inspirers, Gods who enjoy both sorts of our oblations.

7.2.d: ईळेन्यं वो असुरं सुदक्षमन्तर्दूतं रोदसी सत्यवाचम् । मनुष्वदग्निं मनुना समिद्धं समध्वराय सदमिन्महेम ॥
7.2.e: We will extol at sacrifice for ever, as men may do, Agni whom Manu kindled,  Your very skilful Asura, meet for worship, envoy between both worlds, the truthful speaker.

7.2.d: सपर्यवो भरमाणा अभिज्ञु प्र वृञ्जते नमसा बर्हिरग्नौ । आजुह्वाना घृतपृष्ठं पृषद्वदध्वर्यवो हविषा मर्जयध्वम् ॥
7.2.e: Bearing the sacred grass, the men who serve him strew it with reverence, on their knees, by Agni.  Calling him to the spotted grass, oil-sprinkled, adorn him, ye Adhvaryus, with oblation.

7.2.d: स्वाध्यो३ वि दुरो देवयन्तोऽशिश्रयू रथयुर्देवताता । पूर्वी शिशुं न मातरा रिहाणे समग्रुवो न समनेष्वञ्जन् ॥
7.2.e: With holy thoughts the pious have thrown open Doors fain for chariots in the Gods’ assembly.  Like two full mother cows who lick their youngling, like maidens for the gathering, they adorn them.

7.2.d: उत योषणे दिव्ये मही न उषासानक्ता सुदुघेव धेनुः । बर्हिषदा पुरुहूते मघोनी आ यज्ञिये सुविताय श्रयेताम् ॥
7.2.e: And let the two exalted Heavenly Ladies, Morning and Night, like a cow good at milking,  Come, much-invoked, and on our grass be seated ' wealthy, deserving worship, for our welfare.

7.2.d: विप्रा यज्ञेषु मानुषेषु कारू मन्ये वां जातवेदसा यजध्यै । ऊर्ध्वं नो अध्वरं कृतं हवेषु ता देवेषु वनथो वार्याणि ॥
7.2.e: You, Bards and Singers at men's sacrifices, both filled with wisdom, I incline to worship.  Send up our offerings when we call upon you, and so among the Gods obtain us treasures.

7.2.d: आ भारती भारतीभिः सजोषा इळा देवैर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः । सरस्वती सारस्वतेभिरर्वाक्तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं सदन्तु ॥
7.2.e: May Bhāratī with all her Sisters, Iḷā accordant with the Gods, with mortals Agni,  Sarasvatī with all her kindred Rivers, come to this grass, Three Goddesses, and seat them.

7.2.d: तन्नस्तुरीपमध पोषयित्नु देव त्वष्टर्वि रराणः स्यस्व । यतो वीरः कर्मण्यः सुदक्षो युक्तग्रावा जायते देवकामः ॥
7.2.e: Well pleased with us do thou, O God, O Tvaṣṭar, give ready issue to our procreant vigour,  Whence springs the hero, powerful, skilled in action, lover of Gods, adjuster of the press-stones.

7.2.d: वनस्पतेऽव सृजोप देवानग्निर्हविः शमिता सूदयाति । सेदु होता सत्यतरो यजाति यथा देवानां जनिमानि वेद ॥
7.2.e: Send to the Gods the oblation, Lord of Forests, and let the Immolator, Agni, dress it.  He as the truer Priest shall offer worship, for the God'sgenerations well he knoweth.

7.2.d: आ याह्यग्ने समिधानो अर्वाङिन्द्रेण देवैः सरथं तुरेभिः । बर्हिर्न आस्तामदितिः सुपुत्रा स्वाहा देवा अमृता मादयन्ताम् ॥
7.2.e: Come thou to us, O Agni, duly kindled, together with the potent Gods and Indra.  On this our grass sit Aditi, happy Mother, and let our Hail! delight the Gods Immortal.

7.3.d: अग्निं वो देवमग्निभिः सजोषा यजिष्ठं दूतमध्वरे कृणुध्वम् । यो मर्त्येषु निध्रुविर्ऋतावा तपुर्मूर्धा घृतान्नः पावकः ॥
7.3.e: ASSOCIATE with fires, make your God Agni envoy at sacrifice, best skilled in worship,  Established firm among mankind, the Holy, flame-crowned and fed with oil, the Purifier.

7.3.d: प्रोथदश्वो न यवसेऽविष्यन्यदा महः संवरणाद्व्यस्थात् । आदस्य वातो अनु वाति शोचिरध स्म ते व्रजनं कृष्णमस्ति ॥
7.3.e: Like a steed neighing eager for the pasture, when he hath stepped forth from the great enclosure:  Then the wind following blows upon his splendour, and, straight, the path is black which thou hast travelled.

7.3.d: उद्यस्य ते नवजातस्य वृष्णोऽग्ने चरन्त्यजरा इधानाः । अच्छा द्यामरुषो धूम एति सं दूतो अग्न ईयसे हि देवान् ॥
7.3.e: From thee a Bull but newly born, O Agni, the kindled everlasting flames rise upward.  Aloft to heaven thy ruddy smoke ascendeth: Agni, thou speedest to the Gods as envoy.

7.3.d: वि यस्य ते पृथिव्यां पाजो अश्रेत्तृषु यदन्ना समवृक्त जम्भैः । सेनेव सृष्टा प्रसितिष्ट एति यवं न दस्म जुह्वा विवेक्षि ॥
7.3.e: Thou whose fresh lustre o’er the earth advanceth when greedily with thy jaws thy food thou eatest.  Like a host hurried onward comes thy lasso: fierce, with thy tongue thou piercest, as ’twere barley.

7.3.d: तमिद्दोषा तमुषसि यविष्ठमग्निमत्यं न मर्जयन्त नरः । निशिशाना अतिथिमस्य योनौ दीदाय शोचिराहुतस्य वृष्णः ॥
7.3.e: The men have decked him both at eve and morning, Most Youthful Agni, as they tend a courser.  They kindle him, a guest within his dwelling: bright shines the splendour of the worshipped Hero.

7.3.d: सुसंदृक्ते स्वनीक प्रतीकं वि यद्रुक्मो न रोचस उपाके । दिवो न ते तन्यतुरेति शुष्मश्चित्रो न सूरः प्रति चक्षि भानुम् ॥
7.3.e: O fair of face, beautiful is thine aspect when, very near at hand, like gold thou gleamest,  Like Heaven's thundering roar thy might approaches, and like the wondrous Sun thy light thou showest.

7.3.d: यथा वः स्वाहाग्नये दाशेम परीळाभिर्घृतवद्भिश्च हव्यैः । तेभिर्नो अग्ने अमितैर्महोभिः शतं पूर्भिरायसीभिर्नि पाहि ॥
7.3.e: That we may worship, with your Hail to Agni! with sacrificial cakes and fat oblations,  Guard us, O Agni, with those boundless glories as with a hundred fortresses of iron.

7.3.d: या वा ते सन्ति दाशुषे अधृष्टा गिरो वा याभिर्नृवतीरुरुष्याः । ताभिर्नः सूनो सहसो नि पाहि स्मत्सूरीञ्जरितॄञ्जातवेदः ॥
7.3.e: Thine are resistless songs for him who offers, and hero-giving hymns wherewith thou savest;  With these, O Son of Strength, O Jātavedas, guard us, preserve these princes and the singers.

7.3.d: निर्यत्पूतेव स्वधितिः शुचिर्गात्स्वया कृपा तन्वा३ रोचमानः । आ यो मात्रोरुशेन्यो जनिष्ट देवयज्याय सुक्रतुः पावकः ॥
7.3.e: When forth he cometh, like an axe new-sharpened, pure in his form, resplendent in his body,  Sprung, sought with eager longing, from his Parents, for the Gods’ worship, Sage and Purifier:

7.3.d: एता नो अग्ने सौभगा दिदीह्यपि क्रतुं सुचेतसं वतेम । विश्वा स्तोतृभ्यो गृणते च सन्तु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.3.e: Shine this felicity on us, O Agni: may we attain to perfect understanding.  All happiness be theirs who sing and praise thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.4.d: प्र वः शुक्राय भानवे भरध्वं हव्यं मतिं चाग्नये सुपूतम् । यो दैव्यानि मानुषा जनूंष्यन्तर्विश्वानि विद्मना जिगाति ॥
7.4.e: BRING forth your gifts to his refulgent splendour, your hymn as purest offering to Agni,  To him who goes as messenger with knowledge between all songs of men and Gods in heaven.

7.4.d: स गृत्सो अग्निस्तरुणश्चिदस्तु यतो यविष्ठो अजनिष्ट मातुः । सं यो वना युवते शुचिदन्भूरि चिदन्ना समिदत्ति सद्यः ॥
7.4.e: Wise must this Agni be, though young and tender, since he was born, Most Youthful, of his Mother;  He who with bright teeth seizeth fast the forests, and eats his food, though plenteous, in a moment.

7.4.d: अस्य देवस्य संसद्यनीके यं मर्तासः श्येतं जगृभ्रे । नि यो गृभं पौरुषेयीमुवोच दुरोकमग्निरायवे शुशोच ॥
7.4.e: Before his presence must we all assemble, this God's whom men have seized in his white splendour.  This Agni who hath brooked that men should seize him hath shone for man with glow insufferable.

7.4.d: अयं कविरकविषु प्रचेता मर्तेष्वग्निरमृतो नि धायि । स मा नो अत्र जुहुरः सहस्वः सदा त्वे सुमनसः स्याम ॥
7.4.e: Far-seeing hath this Agni been established, deathless mid mortals, wise among the foolish.  Here, O victorious God, forbear to harm us: may weforever share thy gracious favour.

7.4.d: आ यो योनिं देवकृतं ससाद क्रत्वा ह्य१ग्निरमृताँ अतारीत् । तमोषधीश्च वनिनश्च गर्भं भूमिश्च विश्वधायसं बिभर्ति ॥
7.4.e: He who hath occupied his God-made dwelling, Agni, in wisdom hath surpassed Immortals.  A Babe unborn, the plants and trees support him, and the earth beareth him the All-sustainer.

7.4.d: ईशे ह्य१ग्निरमृतस्य भूरेरीशे रायः सुवीर्यस्य दातोः । मा त्वा वयं सहसावन्नवीरा माप्सवः परि षदाम मादुवः ॥
7.4.e: Agni is Lord of Amṛta. in abundance, Lord of the gift of wealth and hero valour,  Victorious God, let us not sit about thee like men devoid of strength, beauty, and worship.

7.4.d: परिषद्यं ह्यरणस्य रेक्णो नित्यस्य रायः पतयः स्याम । न शेषो अग्ने अन्यजातमस्त्यचेतानस्य मा पथो वि दुक्षः ॥
7.4.e: The foeman's treasure may be won with labour: may we be masters of our own possessions.  Agni, no son is he who springs from others: lengthen not out the pathways of the foolish.

7.4.d: नहि ग्रभायारणः सुशेवोऽन्योदर्यो मनसा मन्तवा उ । अधा चिदोकः पुनरित्स एत्या नो वाज्यभीषाळेतु नव्यः ॥
7.4.e: Unwelcome for adoption is the stranger, one to be thought of as another's offipring,  Though grown familiar by continual presence. May our strong hero come, freshly triumphant.

7.4.d: त्वमग्ने वनुष्यतो नि पाहि त्वमु नः सहसावन्नवद्यात् । सं त्वा ध्वस्मन्वदभ्येतु पाथः सं रयिः स्पृहयाय्यः सहस्री ॥
7.4.e: Guard us from him who would assail us, Agni; preserve us O thou Victor, from dishonour.  Here let the place of darkening come upon thee: may wealth be ours, desirable, in thousands.

7.4.d: एता नो अग्ने सौभगा दिदीह्यपि क्रतुं सुचेतसं वतेम । विश्वा स्तोतृभ्यो गृणते च सन्तु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.4.e: Shine this felicity on us, O Agni: may we attain to perfect understanding.  All happiness be theirs who sing and praise thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.5.d: प्राग्नये तवसे भरध्वं गिरं दिवो अरतये पृथिव्याः । यो विश्वेषाममृतानामुपस्थे वैश्वानरो वावृधे जागृवद्भिः ॥
7.5.e: BRING forth your song of praise to mighty Agni, the speedy messenger of earth and heaven,  Vaiśvānara, who, with those who wake, hath waxen great in the lap of all the Gods Immortal.

7.5.d: पृष्टो दिवि धाय्यग्निः पृथिव्यां नेता सिन्धूनां वृषभः स्तियानाम् । स मानुषीरभि विशो वि भाति वैश्वानरो वावृधानो वरेण ॥
7.5.e: Sought in the heavens, on earth is Agni stablished, leader of rivers, Bull of standing waters.  Vaiśvānara when he hath grown in glory, shines on the tribes of men with light and treasure.

7.5.d: त्वद्भिया विश आयन्नसिक्नीरसमना जहतीर्भोजनानि । वैश्वानर पूरवे शोशुचानः पुरो यदग्ने दरयन्नदीदेः ॥
7.5.e: For fear of thee forth fled the dark-hued races, scattered abroad, deserting their possessions,  When, glowing, O Vaiśvānara, for Pūru, thou Agni didst light up and rend their castles.

7.5.d: तव त्रिधातु पृथिवी उत द्यौर्वैश्वानर व्रतमग्ने सचन्त । त्वं भासा रोदसी आ ततन्थाजस्रेण शोचिषा शोशुचानः ॥
7.5.e: Agni Vaiśvānara, both Earth and Heaven submit them to thy threefold jurisdiction.  Refulgent in thine undecaying lustre thou hast invested both the worlds with splendour.

7.5.d: त्वामग्ने हरितो वावशाना गिरः सचन्ते धुनयो घृताचीः । पतिं कृष्टीनां रथ्यं रयीणां वैश्वानरमुषसां केतुमह्नाम् ॥
7.5.e: Agni, the tawny horses, loudly neighing our resonant hymns that drop with oil, attend thee;  Lord of the tribes, our Charioteer of riches, Ensign of days, Vaiśvānara of mornings.

7.5.d: त्वे असुर्यं१ वसवो न्यृण्वन्क्रतुं हि ते मित्रमहो जुषन्त । त्वं दस्यूँरोकसो अग्न आज उरु ज्योतिर्जनयन्नार्याय ॥
7.5.e: In thee, O bright as Mitra, Vasus seated the might of Aduras, for they loved thy spirit.  Thou dravest Dasyus from their home, O Agni, and broughtest forth broad light to light the Ārya.

7.5.d: स जायमानः परमे व्योमन्वायुर्न पाथः परि पासि सद्यः । त्वं भुवना जनयन्नभि क्रन्नपत्याय जातवेदो दशस्यन् ॥
7.5.e: Born in the loftiest heaven thou in a moment reachest, like wind, the place where Gods inhabit.  Thou, favouring thine offspring, roaredst loudly when giving life to creatures, Jātavedas.

7.5.d: तामग्ने अस्मे इषमेरयस्व वैश्वानर द्युमतीं जातवेदः । यया राधः पिन्वसि विश्ववार पृथु श्रवो दाशुषे मर्त्याय ॥
7.5.e: Send us that strength, Vaiśvānara, send it, Agni, that strength, O Jātavedas, full of splendour,  Wherewith, all-bounteous God, thou pourest riches, as fame wide-spreading, on the man who offers.

7.5.d: तं नो अग्ने मघवद्भ्यः पुरुक्षुं रयिं नि वाजं श्रुत्यं युवस्व । वैश्वानर महि नः शर्म यच्छ रुद्रेभिरग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः ॥
7.5.e: Agni, bestow upon our chiefs and nobles that famous power, that wealth which feedeth many.  Accordant with the Vasus and the Rudras, Agni, Vaiśvānara, give us sure protection.

7.6.d: प्र सम्राजो असुरस्य प्रशस्तिं पुंसः कृष्टीनामनुमाद्यस्य । इन्द्रस्येव प्र तवसस्कृतानि वन्दे दारुं वन्दमानो विवक्मि ॥
7.6.e: PRAISE of the Asura, high imperial Ruler, the Manly One in whom the folk shall triumph-  I laud his deeds who is as strong as Indra, and lauding celebrate the Fort-destroyer.

7.6.d: कविं केतुं धासिं भानुमद्रेर्हिन्वन्ति शं राज्यं रोदस्योः । पुरंदरस्य गीर्भिरा विवासेऽग्नेर्व्रतानि पूर्व्या महानि ॥
7.6.e: Sage, Sing, Food, Light,—they bring him from the mountain, the blessed Sovran of the earth and heaven.  I decorate with songs the mighty actions which Agni, Fort-destroyer, did aforetime.

7.6.d: न्यक्रतून्ग्रथिनो मृध्रवाचः पणीँरश्रद्धाँ अवृधाँ अयज्ञान् । प्रप्र तान्दस्यूँरग्निर्विवाय पूर्वश्चकारापराँ अयज्यून् ॥
7.6.e: The foolish, faithless, rudely-speaking niggards, without belief or sacrifice or worship,—  Far far sway hath Agni chased those Dasytis, and, in the cast, hath turned the godless westward.

7.6.d: यो अपाचीने तमसि मदन्तीः प्राचीश्चकार नृतमः शचीभिः । तमीशानं वस्वो अग्निं गृणीषेऽनानतं दमयन्तं पृतन्यून् ॥
7.6.e: Him who brought eastward, manliest with his prowess, the Maids rejoicing in the western darkness,  That Agni I extol, the Lord of riches, unyielding tamer of assailing foemen.

7.6.d: यो देह्यो३ अनमयद्वधस्नैर्यो अर्यपत्नीरुषसश्चकार । स निरुध्या नहुषो यह्वो अग्निर्विशश्चक्रे बलिहृतः सहोभिः ॥
7.6.e: Him who brake down the walls with deadly weapons, and gave the Mornings to anoble Husband,  Young Agni, who with conquering strength subduing the tribes of Nahus made them bring their tribute.

7.6.d: यस्य शर्मन्नुप विश्वे जनास एवैस्तस्थुः सुमतिं भिक्षमाणाः । वैश्वानरो वरमा रोदस्योराग्निः ससाद पित्रोरुपस्थम् ॥
7.6.e: In whose protection all men rest by nature, desiring to enjoy his gracious favour-  Agni Vaiśvānara in his Parents, bosom hath found the choicest seat in earth and heaven.

7.6.d: आ देवो ददे बुध्न्या३ वसूनि वैश्वानर उदिता सूर्यस्य । आ समुद्रादवरादा परस्मादाग्निर्ददे दिव आ पृथिव्याः ॥
7.6.e: Vaiśvānara the God, at the sun's setting, hath taken to himself deep-hidden treasures:  Agni hath taken them from earth and heaven, from the sea under and the sea above us.

7.7.d: प्र वो देवं चित्सहसानमग्निमश्वं न वाजिनं हिषे नमोभिः । भवा नो दूतो अध्वरस्य विद्वान्त्मना देवेषु विविदे मितद्रुः ॥
7.7.e: I SEND forth even your God, victorious Agni, like a strong courser, with mine adoration.  Herald of sacrifice be he who knoweth he hath reached Gods, himself, with measured motion.

7.7.d: आ याह्यग्ने पथ्या३ अनु स्वा मन्द्रो देवानां सख्यं जुषाणः । आ सानु शुष्मैर्नदयन्पृथिव्या जम्भेभिर्विश्वमुशधग्वनानि ॥
7.7.e: By paths that are thine own come hither, Agni, joyous, delighting in the Gods’ alliance,  Making the heights of earth roar with thy fury, burning with eager teeth the woods and forests.

7.7.d: प्राचीनो यज्ञः सुधितं हि बर्हिः प्रीणीते अग्निरीळितो न होता । आ मातरा विश्ववारे हुवानो यतो यविष्ठ जज्ञिषे सुशेवः ॥
7.7.e: The grass is strewn; the sacrifice advances adored as Priest, Agni is made propitious,  Invoking both All-boon-bestowing Mothers of whom, Most Youthful! thou wast born to help us.

7.7.d: सद्यो अध्वरे रथिरं जनन्त मानुषासो विचेतसो य एषाम् । विशामधायि विश्पतिर्दुरोणे३ऽग्निर्मन्द्रो मधुवचा ऋतावा ॥
7.7.e: Forthwith the men, the best of these for wisdom, have made him leader in the solemn worship.  As Lord in homes of men is Agni stablished, the Holy One, the joyous, sweetly speaking.

7.7.d: असादि वृतो वह्निराजगन्वानग्निर्ब्रह्मा नृषदने विधर्ता । द्यौश्च यं पृथिवी वावृधाते आ यं होता यजति विश्ववारम् ॥
7.7.e: He hath come, chosen bearer, and is seated in man's home, Brahman, Agni, the Supporter,  He whom both Heaven anct Earth exalt and strengthenwhom, Giver of all boons, the Hotar worships.

7.7.d: एते द्युम्नेभिर्विश्वमातिरन्त मन्त्रं ये वारं नर्या अतक्षन् । प्र ये विशस्तिरन्त श्रोषमाणा आ ये मे अस्य दीधयन्नृतस्य ॥
7.7.e: These have passed all in glory, who, the manly, have wrought with skill the hymn of adoration;  Who, listening, have advanced the people's welfare, and set their thoughts on this my holy statute.

7.7.d: नू त्वामग्न ईमहे वसिष्ठा ईशानं सूनो सहसो वसूनाम् । इषं स्तोतृभ्यो मघवद्भ्य आनड्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.7.e: We, the Vasisthas, now implore thee, Agni, O Son of Strength, the Lord of wealth and treasure.  Thou hast brought food to singers and to nobles. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.8.d: इन्धे राजा समर्यो नमोभिर्यस्य प्रतीकमाहुतं घृतेन । नरो हव्येभिरीळते सबाध आग्निरग्र उषसामशोचि ॥
7.8.e: THE King whose face is decked with oil is kindled with homage offered by his faithful servant.  The men, the priests adore him with oblations. Agni hath shone forth when the dawn is breaking.

7.8.d: अयमु ष्य सुमहाँ अवेदि होता मन्द्रो मनुषो यह्वो अग्निः । वि भा अकः ससृजानः पृथिव्यां कृष्णपविरोषधीभिर्ववक्षे ॥
7.8.e: Yea, he hath been acknowledged as most mighty, the joyous Priest of men, the youthful Agni.  He, spreading o’er the earth, made light around him, and grew among the plants with blackened fellies..

7.8.d: कया नो अग्ने वि वसः सुवृक्तिं कामु स्वधामृणवः शस्यमानः । कदा भवेम पतयः सुदत्र रायो वन्तारो दुष्टरस्य साधोः ॥
7.8.e: How dost thou decorate our hymn, O Agni? What power dost thou exert when thou art lauded?  When, Bounteous God, may we be lords of riches, winners of precious wealth which none may conquer?

7.8.d: प्रप्रायमग्निर्भरतस्य शृण्वे वि यत्सूर्यो न रोचते बृहद्भाः । अभि यः पूरुं पृतनासु तस्थौ द्युतानो दैव्यो अतिथिः शुशोच ॥
7.8.e: Far famed is this the Bhārata's own Agni he shineth like the Sun with lofty splendour.  He who hath vanquished Pūru in the battle, the heavenly guest hath glowed in full refulgence.

7.8.d: असन्नित्त्वे आहवनानि भूरि भुवो विश्वेभिः सुमना अनीकैः । स्तुतश्चिदग्ने शृण्विषे गृणानः स्वयं वर्धस्व तन्वं सुजात ॥
7.8.e: Full many oblations are in thee collected: with all thine aspects thou hast waxen gracious.  Thou art already famed as praised and lauded, yet still, O nobly born, increase thy body.

7.8.d: इदं वचः शतसाः संसहस्रमुदग्नये जनिषीष्ट द्विबर्हाः । शं यत्स्तोतृभ्य आपये भवाति द्युमदमीवचातनं रक्षोहा ॥
7.8.e: Be this my song, that winneth countless treasure, engendered with redoubled force for Agni,  That, splendid, chasing sickness, slaying demons, it may delight our friend and bless the singers.

7.8.d: नू त्वामग्न ईमहे वसिष्ठा ईशानं सूनो सहसो वसूनाम् । इषं स्तोतृभ्यो मघवद्भ्य आनड्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.8.e: We, the Vasisthas, now implore thee, Agni, O Son of Strength, the Lord of wealth and riches.  Thou hast brought food to singers and to nobles. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.9.d: अबोधि जार उषसामुपस्थाद्धोता मन्द्रः कवितमः पावकः । दधाति केतुमुभयस्य जन्तोर्हव्या देवेषु द्रविणं सुकृत्सु ॥
7.9.e: ROUSED from their bosom is the Dawns' beloved, the joyous Priest, most sapient, Purifier.  He gives a signal both to Gods and mortals, to Gods oblations, riches to the pious.

7.9.d: स सुक्रतुर्यो वि दुरः पणीनां पुनानो अर्कं पुरुभोजसं नः । होता मन्द्रो विशां दमूनास्तिरस्तमो ददृशे राम्याणाम् ॥
7.9.e: Most wise is he who, forcing doors of Paṇis, brought the bright Sun to us who feedeth many.  The cheerful Priest, men's Friend and home-companion, through still night's darkness he is made apparent.

7.9.d: अमूरः कविरदितिर्विवस्वान्त्सुसंसन्मित्रो अतिथिः शिवो नः । चित्रभानुरुषसां भात्यग्रेऽपां गर्भः प्रस्व१ आ विवेश ॥
7.9.e: Wise, ne.'er deceived, uncircumscribed, refulgent, our gracious guest, a Friend with good attendants,  Shines forth with wondrous light before the Mornings; the young plants hath he entered, Child of Waters.

7.9.d: ईळेन्यो वो मनुषो युगेषु समनगा अशुचज्जातवेदाः । सुसंदृशा भानुना यो विभाति प्रति गावः समिधानं बुधन्त ॥
7.9.e: Seeking our gatherings, he, your Jātavedas, hath shone adorable through human ages,  Who gleams refulgent with his lovely lustre: the kine have waked to meet him when enkindled.

7.9.d: अग्ने याहि दूत्यं१ मा रिषण्यो देवाँ अच्छा ब्रह्मकृता गणेन । सरस्वतीं मरुतो अश्विनापो यक्षि देवान्रत्नधेयाय विश्वान् ॥
7.9.e: Go on thy message to the Gods, and fail not, O Agni, with their band who pray and worship.  Bring all the Gods that they may give us riches, Sarasvatī, the Maruts, Aśvins, Waters.

7.9.d: त्वामग्ने समिधानो वसिष्ठो जरूथं हन्यक्षि राये पुरंधिम् । पुरुणीथा जातवेदो जरस्व यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.9.e: Vasiṣṭha, when enkindling thee, O Agni, hath slain jarutha. Give us wealth in plenty.  Sing praise in choral song, O Jātavedas. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.10.d: उषो न जारः पृथु पाजो अश्रेद्दविद्युतद्दीद्यच्छोशुचानः । वृषा हरिः शुचिरा भाति भासा धियो हिन्वान उशतीरजीगः ॥
7.10.e: HE hath sent forth, bright, radiant, and refulgent, like the Dawn's Lover, his far-spreading lustre.  Pure in his splendour shines the golden Hero: our longing thoughts hath he aroused and wakened.

7.10.d: स्व१र्ण वस्तोरुषसामरोचि यज्ञं तन्वाना उशिजो न मन्म । अग्निर्जन्मानि देव आ वि विद्वान्द्रवद्दूतो देवयावा वनिष्ठः ॥
7.10.e: He, like the Sun, hath shone while Morn is breaking, and priests who weave the sacrifice sing praises,  Agni, the God, who knows their generations and visits Gods, most bounteous, rapid envoy.

7.10.d: अच्छा गिरो मतयो देवयन्तीरग्निं यन्ति द्रविणं भिक्षमाणाः । सुसंदृशं सुप्रतीकं स्वञ्चं हव्यवाहमरतिं मानुषाणाम् ॥
7.10.e: Our songs and holy hymns go forth to Agni, seeking the God and asking him for riches,  Him fair to see, of goodly aspect, mighty, men's messenger who carries their oblations.

7.10.d: इन्द्रं नो अग्ने वसुभिः सजोषा रुद्रं रुद्रेभिरा वहा बृहन्तम् । आदित्येभिरदितिं विश्वजन्यां बृहस्पतिमृक्वभिर्विश्ववारम् ॥
7.10.e: joined with the Vasus, Agni, bring thou Indra bring hither mighty Rudra with the Rudras,  Aditi good to all men with Ādityas, Bṛhaspati All-bounteous, with the Singers.

7.10.d: मन्द्रं होतारमुशिजो यविष्ठमग्निं विश ईळते अध्वरेषु । स हि क्षपावाँ अभवद्रयीणामतन्द्रो दूतो यजथाय देवान् ॥
7.10.e: Men eagerly implore at sacrifices Agni, Most Youthful God, the joyous Herald.  For he is Lord and Ruler over riches, and for Gods’ worship an unwearied envoy.

7.11.d: महाँ अस्यध्वरस्य प्रकेतो न ऋते त्वदमृता मादयन्ते । आ विश्वेभिः सरथं याहि देवैर्न्यग्ने होता प्रथमः सदेह ॥
7.11.e: GREAT art thou, Agni, sacrifice's Herald: not without thee are deathless Gods made joyful.  Come hither with all Deities about thee here take thy seat, the first, as Priest, O Agni.

7.11.d: त्वामीळते अजिरं दूत्याय हविष्मन्तः सदमिन्मानुषासः । यस्य देवैरासदो बर्हिरग्नेऽहान्यस्मै सुदिना भवन्ति ॥
7.11.e: Men with oblations evermore entreat thee, the swift, to undertake an envoy's duty.  He on whose sacred grass with Gods thou sittest, to him, O Agni, are the days propitious.

7.11.d: त्रिश्चिदक्तोः प्र चिकितुर्वसूनि त्वे अन्तर्दाशुषे मर्त्याय । मनुष्वदग्न इह यक्षि देवान्भवा नो दूतो अभिशस्तिपावा ॥
7.11.e: Three times a day in thee are shown the treasures sent for the mortal who presents oblation.  Bring the Gods hither like a man, O Agni: be thou our envoy, guarding us from curses.

7.11.d: अग्निरीशे बृहतो अध्वरस्याग्निर्विश्वस्य हविषः कृतस्य । क्रतुं ह्यस्य वसवो जुषन्ताथा देवा दधिरे हव्यवाहम् ॥
7.11.e: Lord of the lofty sacrifice is Agni, Agni is Lord of every gift presented.  The Vasus were contented with his wisdom, so the Gods made him their oblationbearer.

7.11.d: आग्ने वह हविरद्याय देवानिन्द्रज्येष्ठास इह मादयन्ताम् । इमं यज्ञं दिवि देवेषु धेहि यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.11.e: O Agni, bring the Gods to taste our presents: with Indra leading, here let them be joyful.  Convey this sacrifice to Gods in heaven. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.12.d: अगन्म महा नमसा यविष्ठं यो दीदाय समिद्धः स्वे दुरोणे । चित्रभानुं रोदसी अन्तरुर्वी स्वाहुतं विश्वतः प्रत्यञ्चम् ॥
7.12.e: WE with great reverence have approached The Youngest who hath shone forth well-kindled in his dwelling,  With wondrous light between wide earth and heaven, well-worshipped, looking forth in all directions.

7.12.d: स मह्ना विश्वा दुरितानि साह्वानग्निः ष्टवे दम आ जातवेदाः । स नो रक्षिषद्दुरितादवद्यादस्मान्गृणत उत नो मघोनः ॥
7.12.e: Through his great might o’ercoming all misfortunes, praised in the house is Agni Jātavedas.  May he protect us from disgrace and trouble, both us who laud him and our noble patrons.

7.12.d: त्वं वरुण उत मित्रो अग्ने त्वां वर्धन्ति मतिभिर्वसिष्ठाः । त्वे वसु सुषणनानि सन्तु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.12.e: O Agni, thou art Varuṇa and Mitra: Vasisthas with their holy hymns exalt thee.  With thee be most abundant gain of treasure. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.13.d: प्राग्नये विश्वशुचे धियंधेऽसुरघ्ने मन्म धीतिं भरध्वम् । भरे हविर्न बर्हिषि प्रीणानो वैश्वानराय यतये मतीनाम् ॥
7.13.e: BRING song and hymn to Agni, Asura-slayer, enlightener of all and thought-bestower.  Like an oblation on the grass, to please him, I bring this to Vaiśvānara, hymn-inspirer.

7.13.d: त्वमग्ने शोचिषा शोशुचान आ रोदसी अपृणा जायमानः । त्वं देवाँ अभिशस्तेरमुञ्चो वैश्वानर जातवेदो महित्वा ॥
7.13.e: Thou with thy flame, O Agni, brightly glowing, hast at thy birth filled full the earth and heaven.  TIOU with thy might, Vaiśvānara Jātavedas, settest the Gods free frodi the curse that bound them.

7.13.d: जातो यदग्ने भुवना व्यख्यः पशून्न गोपा इर्यः परिज्मा । वैश्वानर ब्रह्मणे विन्द गातुं यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.13.e: Agni, when, born thou lookedst on all creatures, like a brisk herdsman moving round his cattle.  The path to prayer, Vaiśvānara, thou foundest. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.14.d: समिधा जातवेदसे देवाय देवहूतिभिः । हविर्भिः शुक्रशोचिषे नमस्विनो वयं दाशेमाग्नये ॥
7.14.e: WITH reverence and with offered gifts serve we the God whose flame is bright:  Let us bring Jātavedas fuel, and adore Agni when we invoke the Gods.

7.14.d: वयं ते अग्ने समिधा विधेम वयं दाशेम सुष्टुती यजत्र । वयं घृतेनाध्वरस्य होतर्वयं देव हविषा भद्रशोचे ॥
7.14.e: Agni, may we perform thy rites with fuel, and honour thee, O Holy one, with praises:  Honour thee, Priest of sacrifice! with butter, thee, God of blessed light! with our oblation.

7.14.d: आ नो देवेभिरुप देवहूतिमग्ने याहि वषट्कृतिं जुषाणः । तुभ्यं देवाय दाशतः स्याम यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.14.e: Come, Agni, with the Gods to our invoking, come, pleased, to offerings sanctified with Vaṣaṭ.  May we be his who pays thee, God, due honour. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.15.d: उपसद्याय मीळ्हुष आस्ये जुहुता हविः । यो नो नेदिष्ठमाप्यम् ॥
7.15.e: OFFER oblations in his mouth, the bounteous God's whom we must serve.  His who is nearest kin to us:

7.15.d: यः पञ्च चर्षणीरभि निषसाद दमेदमे । कविर्गृहपतिर्युवा ॥
7.15.e: Who for the Fivefold People's take hath seated him in every home  Wise, Youthful, Master of the house.

7.15.d: स नो वेदो अमात्यमग्नी रक्षतु विश्वतः । उतास्मान्पात्वंहसः ॥
7.15.e: On all sides may that Agni guard our household folk and property;  May he deliver us from woe.

7.15.d: नवं नु स्तोममग्नये दिवः श्येनाय जीजनम् । वस्वः कुविद्वनाति नः ॥
7.15.e: I have begotten this new hymn for Agni, Falcon of the sky:  Will he not give us of his wealth?

7.15.d: स्पार्हा यस्य श्रियो दृशे रयिर्वीरवतो यथा । अग्रे यज्ञस्य शोचतः ॥
7.15.e: Whose lories when he glows in front of sacrite are fair to see,  Like wealth of one with hero sons.

7.15.d: सेमां वेतु वषट्कृतिमग्निर्जुषत नो गिरः । यजिष्ठो हव्यवाहनः ॥
7.15.e: May he enjoy this hallowed gift, Agni accept our songs, who bears  Oblations, best of worshippers.

7.15.d: नि त्वा नक्ष्य विश्पते द्युमन्तं देव धीमहि । सुवीरमग्न आहुत ॥
7.15.e: Lord of the house, whom men must seek, we set thee down, O Worshipped Onel  Bright, rich in heroes, Agni! God

7.15.d: क्षप उस्रश्च दीदिहि स्वग्नयस्त्वया वयम् । सुवीरस्त्वमस्मयुः ॥
7.15.e: Shine forth at night and morn: through thee with fires are we provided well.  Thou, rich in heroes, art our Friend.

7.15.d: उप त्वा सातये नरो विप्रासो यन्ति धीतिभिः । उपाक्षरा सहस्रिणी ॥
7.15.e: The men come near thee for their gain, the singers with their songs of praise:  Speech, thousandfold, comes near to thee.

7.15.d: अग्नी रक्षांसि सेधति शुक्रशोचिरमर्त्यः । शुचिः पावक ईड्यः ॥
7.15.e: Bright, Purifier, meet for praise, Immortal with refulgent glow,  Agni drives Rākṣasas away.

7.15.d: स नो राधांस्या भरेशानः सहसो यहो । भगश्च दातु वार्यम् ॥
7.15.e: As such, bring us abundant wealth, young Child of Strength, for this thou canst  May Bhaga give us what is choice.

7.15.d: त्वमग्ने वीरवद्यशो देवश्च सविता भगः । दितिश्च दाति वार्यम् ॥
7.15.e: Thou, Agni, givest hero fame: Bhaga and Savitar the God,  And Did give us what is good.

7.15.d: अग्ने रक्षा णो अंहसः प्रति ष्म देव रीषतः । तपिष्ठैरजरो दह ॥
7.15.e: Agni, preserve us from distress: consume our enemies, O God,  Eternal, with the hottest flames.

7.15.d: अधा मही न आयस्यनाधृष्टो नृपीतये । पूर्भवा शतभुजिः ॥
7.15.e: And, irresistible, be thou a mighty iron fort to us,  With hundred walls for man's defence.

7.15.d: त्वं नः पाह्यंहसो दोषावस्तरघायतः । दिवा नक्तमदाभ्य ॥
7.15.e: Do thou preserve us, eve and morn, from sorrow, from the wicked men,  Infallible! by day and night.

7.16.d: एना वो अग्निं नमसोर्जो नपातमा हुवे । प्रियं चेतिष्ठमरतिं स्वध्वरं विश्वस्य दूतममृतम् ॥
7.16.e: WITH this my reverent hymn I call Agni for you, the Son of Strength,  Dear, wisest envoy, served with noble sacrifice, immortal messenger of all.

7.16.d: स योजते अरुषा विश्वभोजसा स दुद्रवत्स्वाहुतः । सुब्रह्मा यज्ञः सुशमी वसूनां देवं राधो जनानाम् ॥
7.16.e: His two red horses, all-supporting, let him yoke: let him, well-worshipped, urge them fast.  Then hath the sacrifice good prayers and happy end, and heavenly gift of wealth to men.

7.16.d: उदस्य शोचिरस्थादाजुह्वानस्य मीळ्हुषः । उद्धूमासो अरुषासो दिविस्पृशः समग्निमिन्धते नरः ॥
7.16.e: The flame of him the Bountiful, the Much-invoked, hath mounted up,  And his red-coloured smoke-clouds reach and touch the sky: the men are kindling Agni well.

7.16.d: तं त्वा दूतं कृण्महे यशस्तमं देवाँ आ वीतये वह । विश्वा सूनो सहसो मर्तभोजना रास्व तद्यत्त्वेमहे ॥
7.16.e: Thee, thee Most Glorious One we make our messenger. Bring the Gods hither to the feast.  Give us, O Son of Strength, all food that fcedeth man: give that for which we pray to thee.

7.16.d: त्वमग्ने गृहपतिस्त्वं होता नो अध्वरे । त्वं पोता विश्ववार प्रचेता यक्षि वेषि च वार्यम् ॥
7.16.e: Thou, Agni, art the homestead's Lord, our Herald at the sacrifice.  Lord of all boons, thou art the Cleanser and a Sage. Pay worship, and enjoy the good.

7.16.d: कृधि रत्नं यजमानाय सुक्रतो त्वं हि रत्नधा असि । आ न ऋते शिशीहि विश्वमृत्विजं सुशंसो यश्च दक्षते ॥
7.16.e: Give riches to the sacrificer, O Most Wise, for thou art he who granteth wealth.  Inspire with zeal each priest at this our solemn rite; all who are skilled in singing praise.

7.16.d: त्वे अग्ने स्वाहुत प्रियासः सन्तु सूरयः । यन्तारो ये मघवानो जनानामूर्वान्दयन्त गोनाम् ॥
7.16.e: O Agni who art worshipped well, dear let our princes he to thee,  Our wealthy patrons who are governors of men, who part, as gifts, their stalls of kine.

7.16.d: येषामिळा घृतहस्ता दुरोण आँ अपि प्राता निषीदति । ताँस्त्रायस्व सहस्य द्रुहो निदो यच्छा नः शर्म दीर्घश्रुत् ॥
7.16.e: They in whose home, her hand bearing the sacred oil, Iḷā sits down well-satisfied-  Guard them, Victorious God, from slander and from harm. give us a refuge famed afar.

7.16.d: स मन्द्रया च जिह्वया वह्निरासा विदुष्टरः । अग्ने रयिं मघवद्भ्यो न आ वह हव्यदातिं च सूदय ॥
7.16.e: Do thou, a Priest with pleasant tongue, most wise, and very near to us,  Agni, bring riches hither to our liberal chiefs, and speed the oflering of our gifts.

7.16.d: ये राधांसि ददत्यश्व्या मघा कामेन श्रवसो महः । ताँ अंहसः पिपृहि पर्तृभिष्ट्वं शतं पूर्भिर्यविष्ठ्य ॥
7.16.e: They who bestow as bounty plenteous wealth of steeds, moved by desire of great renown-  Do thou with saving help preserve them from distress, Most Youthful! with a hundred forts.

7.16.d: देवो वो द्रविणोदाः पूर्णां विवष्ट्यासिचम् । उद्वा सिञ्चध्वमुप वा पृणध्वमादिद्वो देव ओहते ॥
7.16.e: The God who gives your wealth demands a full libation poured to him.  Pour ye it forth, then fill the vessel full again: then doth the God pay heed to you.

7.16.d: तं होतारमध्वरस्य प्रचेतसं वह्निं देवा अकृण्वत । दधाति रत्नं विधते सुवीर्यमग्निर्जनाय दाशुषे ॥
7.16.e: Him have the Gods appointed Priest of sacrifice, oblation-bearer, passing wise.  Agni gives wealth and valour to the worshipper, to folk who offer up their gifts.

7.17.d: अग्ने भव सुषमिधा समिद्ध उत बर्हिरुर्विया वि स्तृणीताम् ॥
7.17.e: AGNI, be kindled well with proper fuel, and let the grass be scattered wide about thee.

7.17.d: उत द्वार उशतीर्वि श्रयन्तामुत देवाँ उशत आ वहेह ॥
7.17.e: Let the impatient Portals be thrown open bring thou the Gods impatient to come hither.

7.17.d: अग्ने वीहि हविषा यक्षि देवान्त्स्वध्वरा कृणुहि जातवेदः ॥
7.17.e: Taste, Agni: serve the Gods with our oblation. Offer good sacrifices, Jātavedas!
Let Jātavedas pay fair sacrifices, worship andgratify the Gods Immortal.

7.17.d: वंस्व विश्वा वार्याणि प्रचेतः सत्या भवन्त्वाशिषो नो अद्य ॥
7.17.e: Wise God, win for us things that are all-goodly, and let the prayers, we pray today be fruitful.

7.17.d: त्वामु ते दधिरे हव्यवाहं देवासो अग्न ऊर्ज आ नपातम् ॥
7.17.e: Thee, even thee, the Son of Strength, O Agni, those Gods have made the bearer of oblations.

7.17.d: ते ते देवाय दाशतः स्याम महो नो रत्ना वि दध इयानः ॥
7.17.e: To thee the God may we perform our worship: do thou, besought, grant us abundant riches.

7.18.d: त्वे ह यत्पितरश्चिन्न इन्द्र विश्वा वामा जरितारो असन्वन् । त्वे गावः सुदुघास्त्वे ह्यश्वास्त्वं वसु देवयते वनिष्ठः ॥
7.18.e: ALL is with thee, O Indra, all the treasures which erst our fathers won who sang thy praises.  With thee are milch-kine good to milk, and horses: best winner thou of riches for the pious.

7.18.d: राजेव हि जनिभिः क्षेष्येवाव द्युभिरभि विदुष्कविः सन् । पिशा गिरो मघवन्गोभिरश्वैस्त्वायतः शिशीहि राये अस्मान् ॥
7.18.e: For like a King among his wives thou dwellest: with glories, as a Sage, surround and help us.  Make us, thy servants, strong for wealth, and honour our songs wirth kine and steeds and decoration.

7.18.d: इमा उ त्वा पस्पृधानासो अत्र मन्द्रा गिरो देवयन्तीरुप स्थुः । अर्वाची ते पथ्या राय एतु स्याम ते सुमताविन्द्र शर्मन् ॥
7.18.e: Here these our holy hymns with joy and gladness in pious emulation have approached thee.  Hitherward come thy path that leads to riches: may we find shelter in thy favour, Indra.

7.18.d: धेनुं न त्वा सूयवसे दुदुक्षन्नुप ब्रह्माणि ससृजे वसिष्ठः । त्वामिन्मे गोपतिं विश्व आहा न इन्द्रः सुमतिं गन्त्वच्छ ॥
7.18.e: Vasiṣṭha hath poured forth his prayers, desiring to milk thee like a cow in goodly pasture.  All these my people call thee Lord of cattle: may Indra. come unto the prayer we offer.

7.18.d: अर्णांसि चित्पप्रथाना सुदास इन्द्रो गाधान्यकृणोत्सुपारा । शर्धन्तं शिम्युमुचथस्य नव्यः शापं सिन्धूनामकृणोदशस्तीः ॥
7.18.e: What though the floods spread widely, Indra made them shallow and easy for Sudās to traverse.  He, worthy of our praises, caused the Simyu, foe of our hymn, to curse the rivers' fury.

7.18.d: पुरोळा इत्तुर्वशो यक्षुरासीद्राये मत्स्यासो निशिता अपीव । श्रुष्टिं चक्रुर्भृगवो द्रुह्यवश्च सखा सखायमतरद्विषूचोः ॥
7.18.e: Eager for spoil was Turvaśa Purodas, fain to win wealth, like fishes urged by hunger.  The Bhṛgus and the Druhyus quickly listened: friend rescued friend mid the two distant peoples.

7.18.d: आ पक्थासो भलानसो भनन्तालिनासो विषाणिनः शिवासः । आ योऽनयत्सधमा आर्यस्य गव्या तृत्सुभ्यो अजगन्युधा नॄन् ॥
7.18.e: Together came the Pakthas, the Bhalanas, the Alinas, the Sivas, the Visanins.  Yet to the Trtsus came the Ārya's Comrade, through love of spoil and heroes' war, to lead them.

7.18.d: दुराध्यो३ अदितिं स्रेवयन्तोऽचेतसो वि जगृभ्रे परुष्णीम् । मह्नाविव्यक्पृथिवीं पत्यमानः पशुष्कविरशयच्चायमानः ॥
7.18.e: Fools, in their folly fain to waste her waters, they parted inexhaustible Paruṣṇī.  Lord of the Earth, he with his might repressed them: still lay the herd and the affrighted herdsman.

7.18.d: ईयुरर्थं न न्यर्थं परुष्णीमाशुश्चनेदभिपित्वं जगाम । सुदास इन्द्रः सुतुकाँ अमित्रानरन्धयन्मानुषे वध्रिवाचः ॥
7.18.e: As to their goal they sped to their destruetion: they sought Paruṣṇī; e’en the swift returned not.  Indra abandoned, to Sudās the manly, the swiftly flying foes, unmanly babblers.

7.18.d: ईयुर्गावो न यवसादगोपा यथाकृतमभि मित्रं चितासः । पृश्निगावः पृश्निनिप्रेषितासः श्रुष्टिं चक्रुर्नियुतो रन्तयश्च ॥
7.18.e: They went like kine unherded from the pasture, each clinging to a friend as chance directed.  They who drive spotted steeds, sent down by Pṛśni, gave ear, the Warriors and the harnessed horses.

7.18.d: एकं च यो विंशतिं च श्रवस्या वैकर्णयोर्जनान्राजा न्यस्तः । दस्मो न सद्मन्नि शिशाति बर्हिः शूरः सर्गमकृणोदिन्द्र एषाम् ॥
7.18.e: The King who scattered one-and-twenty people of both Vaikarna tribes through lust of glory-  As the skilled priest clips grass within the chamber, so hath the Hero Indra, wrought their downfall.

7.18.d: अध श्रुतं कवषं वृद्धमप्स्वनु द्रुह्युं नि वृणग्वज्रबाहुः । वृणाना अत्र सख्याय सख्यं त्वायन्तो ये अमदन्ननु त्वा ॥
7.18.e: Thou, thunder-armed, o’erwhelmedst in the waters famed ancient Kavasa and then the Druhyu.  Others here claiming friendship to their friendship, devoted unto thee, in thee were joyful.

7.18.d: वि सद्यो विश्वा दृंहितान्येषामिन्द्रः पुरः सहसा सप्त दर्दः । व्यानवस्य तृत्सवे गयं भाग्जेष्म पूरुं विदथे मृध्रवाचम् ॥
7.18.e: Indra at once with conquering might demolished all their strong places and their seven castles.  The goods of Anu's son he gave to Trtsu. May we in sacrifice conquer scorned Pūru.

7.18.d: नि गव्यवोऽनवो द्रुह्यवश्च षष्टिः शता सुषुपुः षट् सहस्रा । षष्टिर्वीरासो अधि षड्दुवोयु विश्वेदिन्द्रस्य वीर्या कृतानि ॥
7.18.e: The Anavas and Druhyus, seeking booty, have slept, the sixty hundred, yea, six thousand,  And six-and-sixty heroes. For the pious were all these mighty exploits done by Indra.

7.18.d: इन्द्रेणैते तृत्सवो वेविषाणा आपो न सृष्टा अधवन्त नीचीः । दुर्मित्रासः प्रकलविन्मिमाना जहुर्विश्वानि भोजना सुदासे ॥
7.18.e: These Trtsus under Indra's careful guidance came speeding like loosed waters rushing downward.  The foemen, measuring exceeding closely, abandoned to Sudās all their provisions.

7.18.d: अर्धं वीरस्य शृतपामनिन्द्रं परा शर्धन्तं नुनुदे अभि क्षाम् । इन्द्रो मन्युं मन्युम्यो मिमाय भेजे पथो वर्तनिं पत्यमानः ॥
7.18.e: The hero's side who drank the dressed oblation, Indra's denier, far o’er earth he scattered.  Indra brought down the fierce destroyer's fury. He gave them various roads, the path's Controller.

7.18.d: आध्रेण चित्तद्वेकं चकार सिंह्यं चित्पेत्वेना जघान । अव स्रक्तीर्वेश्यावृश्चदिन्द्रः प्रायच्छद्विश्वा भोजना सुदासे ॥
7.18.e: E’en with the weak he wrought this matchless exploit: e’en with a goat he did to death a lion.  He pared the pillar's angles with a needle. Thus to Sudās Indra gave all provisions.

7.18.d: शश्वन्तो हि शत्रवो रारधुष्टे भेदस्य चिच्छर्धतो विन्द रन्धिम् । मर्ताँ एनः स्तुवतो यः कृणोति तिग्मं तस्मिन्नि जहि वज्रमिन्द्र ॥
7.18.e: To thee have all thine enemies submitted: e’en the fierce Bheda hast thou made thy subject.  Cast down thy sharpened thunderbolt, O Indra, on him who harms the men who sing thy praises.

7.18.d: आवदिन्द्रं यमुना तृत्सवश्च प्रात्र भेदं सर्वताता मुषायत् । अजासश्च शिग्रवो यक्षवश्च बलिं शीर्षाणि जभ्रुरश्व्यानि ॥
7.18.e: Yamuna and the Trtsus aided Indra. There he stripped Bheda bare of all his treasures.  The Ajas and the Sigrus and the Yaksus brought in to him as tribute heads of horses.

7.18.d: न त इन्द्र सुमतयो न रायः संचक्षे पूर्वा उषसो न नूत्नाः । देवकं चिन्मान्यमानं जघन्थाव त्मना बृहतः शम्बरं भेत् ॥
7.18.e: Not to be scorned, but like Dawns past and recent, O Indra, are thy favours and thy riches.  Devaka, Mānyamana's son, thou slewest, and smotest Śambara from the lofty mountain.

7.18.d: प्र ये गृहादममदुस्त्वाया पराशरः शतयातुर्वसिष्ठः । न ते भोजस्य सख्यं मृषन्ताधा सूरिभ्यः सुदिना व्युच्छान् ॥
7.18.e: They who, from home, have gladdened thee, thy servants Parasara, Vasiṣṭha, Satayatu,  Will not forget thy friendship, liberal Giver. So shall the days dawn prosperous for the princes.

7.18.d: द्वे नप्तुर्देववतः शते गोर्द्वा रथा वधूमन्ता सुदासः । अर्हन्नग्ने पैजवनस्य दानं होतेव सद्म पर्येमि रेभन् ॥
7.18.e: Priest-like, with praise, I move around the altar, earning Paijavana's reward, O Agni,  Two hundred cows from Devavan's descendant, two chariots from Sudās with mares to draw them.

7.18.d: चत्वारो मा पैजवनस्य दानाः स्मद्दिष्टयः कृशनिनो निरेके । ऋज्रासो मा पृथिविष्ठाः सुदासस्तोकं तोकाय श्रवसे वहन्ति ॥
7.18.e: Gift of Paijavana, four horses bear me in foremost place, trained steeds with pearl to deck them.  Sudās's brown steeds, firmly-stepping, carry me and my son for progeny and glory.

7.18.d: यस्य श्रवो रोदसी अन्तरुर्वी शीर्ष्णेशीर्ष्णे विबभाजा विभक्ता । सप्तेदिन्द्रं न स्रवतो गृणन्ति नि युध्यामधिमशिशादभीके ॥
7.18.e: Him whose fame spreads between wide earth and heaven, who, as dispenser, gives each chief his portion,  Seven flowing Rivers glorify like Indra. He slew Yudhyamadhi in close encounter.

7.18.d: इमं नरो मरुतः सश्चतानु दिवोदासं न पितरं सुदासः । अविष्टना पैजवनस्य केतं दूणाशं क्षत्रमजरं दुवोयु ॥
7.18.e: Attend on him O ye heroic Maruts as on Sudās's father Divodāsa.  Further Paijavana's desire with favour. Guard faithfully his lasting firm dominion.

7.19.d: यस्तिग्मशृङ्गो वृषभो न भीम एकः कृष्टीश्च्यावयति प्र विश्वाः । यः शश्वतो अदाशुषो गयस्य प्रयन्तासि सुष्वितराय वेदः ॥
7.19.e: HE like a bull with sharpened horns, terrific, singly excites and agitates all the people:  Thou givest him who largely pours libations his goods who pours not, for his own possession.

7.19.d: त्वं ह त्यदिन्द्र कुत्समावः शुश्रूषमाणस्तन्वा समर्ये । दासं यच्छुष्णं कुयवं न्यस्मा अरन्धय आर्जुनेयाय शिक्षन् ॥
7.19.e: Thou, verily, Indra, gavest help to Kutsa, willingly giving car to him in battle,  When, aiding Ārjuneya, thou subduedst to him both Kuyava and the Dāsa Śuṣṇa.

7.19.d: त्वं धृष्णो धृषता वीतहव्यं प्रावो विश्वाभिरूतिभिः सुदासम् । प्र पौरुकुत्सिं त्रसदस्युमावः क्षेत्रसाता वृत्रहत्येषु पूरुम् ॥
7.19.e: O Bold One, thou with all thine aids hast boldly holpen Sudās whose offerings were accepted,  Pūru in winning land and slaying foemen, and Trasadasyu son of Purukutsa.

7.19.d: त्वं नृभिर्नृमणो देववीतौ भूरीणि वृत्रा हर्यश्व हंसि । त्वं नि दस्युं चुमुरिं धुनिं चास्वापयो दभीतये सुहन्तु ॥
7.19.e: At the Gods’ banquet, hero-souled! with Heroes, Lord of Bay Steeds, thou slewest many foemen.  Thou sentest in swift death to sleep the Dasyu, both Cumuri and Dhuni, for Dabhīti.

7.19.d: तव च्यौत्नानि वज्रहस्त तानि नव यत्पुरो नवतिं च सद्यः । निवेशने शततमाविवेषीरहञ्च वृत्रं नमुचिमुताहन् ॥
7.19.e: These were thy mighty powers that, Thunder-wielder, thou swiftly crushedst nine-and-ninety castles:  Thou capturedst the hundredth in thine onslaught; thou slewest Namuci, thou slewest Vṛtra.

7.19.d: सना ता त इन्द्र भोजनानि रातहव्याय दाशुषे सुदासे । वृष्णे ते हरी वृषणा युनज्मि व्यन्तु ब्रह्माणि पुरुशाक वाजम् ॥
7.19.e: Old are the blessings, Indra, which thou gavest Sudās the worshipper who brought oblations.  For thee, the Strong, I yoke thy strong Bay Horses: may our prayers reach thee and win strength, Most Mighty!

7.19.d: मा ते अस्यां सहसावन्परिष्टावघाय भूम हरिवः परादै । त्रायस्व नोऽवृकेभिर्वरूथैस्तव प्रियासः सूरिषु स्याम ॥
7.19.e: Give us not up, Lord of Bay Horses, Victor, in this thine own assembly, to the wicked.  Deliver us with true and faithful succours: dear may we be to thee among the princes.

7.19.d: प्रियास इत्ते मघवन्नभिष्टौ नरो मदेम शरणे सखायः । नि तुर्वशं नि याद्वं शिशीह्यतिथिग्वाय शंस्यं करिष्यन् ॥
7.19.e: May we men, Maghavan, the friends thou lovest, near thee be joyful under thy protection.  Fain to fulfil the wish of Atithigva humble. the pride of Turvaśa and Yadva.

7.19.d: सद्यश्चिन्नु ते मघवन्नभिष्टौ नरः शंसन्त्युक्थशास उक्था । ये ते हवेभिर्वि पणीँरदाशन्नस्मान्वृणीष्व युज्याय तस्मै ॥
7.19.e: Swiftly, in truth, O Maghavan, about thee men skilled in hymning sing their songs and praises. '  Elect us also into their assembly who by their calls on thee despoiled the niggards.

7.19.d: एते स्तोमा नरां नृतम तुभ्यमस्मद्र्यञ्चो ददतो मघानि । तेषामिन्द्र वृत्रहत्ये शिवो भूः सखा च शूरोऽविता च नृणाम् ॥
7.19.e: Thine are these lauds, O manliest of heroes, lauds which revert to us and give us riches.  Favour these, Indra, when they fight with faemen, as Friend and Hero and the heroes' Helper.

7.19.d: नू इन्द्र शूर स्तवमान ऊती ब्रह्मजूतस्तन्वा वावृधस्व । उप नो वाजान्मिमीह्युप स्तीन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.19.e: Now, lauded for thine aid, Heroic Indra, sped by our prayer, wax mighty in thy body.  Apportion to us strength and habitations. Ye Gods, protect us evermore with blessings.

7.20.d: उग्रो जज्ञे वीर्याय स्वधावाञ्चक्रिरपो नर्यो यत्करिष्यन् । जग्मिर्युवा नृषदनमवोभिस्त्राता न इन्द्र एनसो महश्चित् ॥
7.20.e: STRONG, Godly-natured, born for hero exploit, man's Friend, hedoth whatever deed he willeth.  Saving us e’en from great transgression, Indra, the Youthful, visiteth man's home with favour.

7.20.d: हन्ता वृत्रमिन्द्रः शूशुवानः प्रावीन्नु वीरो जरितारमूती । कर्ता सुदासे अह वा उ लोकं दाता वसु मुहुरा दाशुषे भूत् ॥
7.20.e: Waxing greatness Indra slayeth Vṛtra: the Hero with his aid hath helped the singer.  He gave Sudās wide room and space, and often hath granted wealth to him who brought oblations.

7.20.d: युध्मो अनर्वा खजकृत्समद्वा शूरः सत्राषाड्जनुषेमषाळ्हः । व्यास इन्द्रः पृतनाः स्वोजा अधा विश्वं शत्रूयन्तं जघान ॥
7.20.e: Soldier unchecked, war-rousing, battling Hero, unconquered from of old, victorious ever,  Indra the very strong hath scattered armies; yea, he hath slain each foe who fought against him.

7.20.d: उभे चिदिन्द्र रोदसी महित्वा पप्राथ तविषीभिस्तुविष्मः । नि वज्रमिन्द्रो हरिवान्मिमिक्षन्त्समन्धसा मदेषु वा उवोच ॥
7.20.e: Thou with thy greatness hast filled full, O Indra, even both the worlds with might, O thou Most Mighty.  Lord of Bays, Indra, brandishing his thunder, is gratified with Soma at the banquet.

7.20.d: वृषा जजान वृषणं रणाय तमु चिन्नारी नर्यं ससूव । प्र यः सेनानीरध नृभ्यो अस्तीनः सत्वा गवेषणः स धृष्णुः ॥
7.20.e: A Bull begat the Bull for joy of battle, and a strong Mother brought forth him the manly.  He who is Chief of men, their armies' Leader, is strong Hero, bold, and fain for booty.

7.20.d: नू चित्स भ्रेषते जनो न रेषन्मनो यो अस्य घोरमाविवासात् । यज्ञैर्य इन्द्रे दधते दुवांसि क्षयत्स राय ऋतपा ऋतेजाः ॥
7.20.e: The people falter not, nor suffer sorrow, who win themselves this God's terrific spirit.  He who with sacrifices worships Indra is lord of wealth, law-born and law's protector.

7.20.d: यदिन्द्र पूर्वो अपराय शिक्षन्नयज्ज्यायान्कनीयसो देष्णम् । अमृत इत्पर्यासीत दूरमा चित्र चित्र्यं भरा रयिं नः ॥
7.20.e: Whene’er the elder fain would help the younger the greater cometh to the lesser's present.  Shall the Immortal sit aloof' inactive? O Wondrous Indra, bring us wondrous riches.

7.20.d: यस्त इन्द्र प्रियो जनो ददाशदसन्निरेके अद्रिवः सखा ते । वयं ते अस्यां सुमतौ चनिष्ठाः स्याम वरूथे अघ्नतो नृपीतौ ॥
7.20.e: Thy dear folk, Indra, who present oblations, are, in chief place, thy friends, O Thunder-wielder.  May we be best content in this thy favour, sheltered by One who slays not, but preserves us.

7.20.d: एष स्तोमो अचिक्रदद्वृषा त उत स्तामुर्मघवन्नक्रपिष्ट । रायस्कामो जरितारं त आगन्त्वमङ्ग शक्र वस्व आ शको नः ॥
7.20.e: To thee the mighty hymn hath clamoured loudly, and, Maghavan, the eloquent hath besought thee.  Desire of wealth hath come upon thy singer: help us then, gakra, to our share of riches.

7.20.d: स न इन्द्र त्वयताया इषे धास्त्मना च ये मघवानो जुनन्ति । वस्वी षु ते जरित्रे अस्तु शक्तिर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.20.e: Place us by food which thou hast given, O Indra, us and the wealthy patrons who command us.  Let thy great power bring good to him who lauds thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.21.d: असावि देवं गोऋजीकमन्धो न्यस्मिन्निन्द्रो जनुषेमुवोच । बोधामसि त्वा हर्यश्व यज्ञैर्बोधा नः स्तोममन्धसो मदेषु ॥
7.21.e: PRESSED is the juice divine with milk commingled: thereto hath Indra ever been accustomed.  We wake thee, Lord of Bays, with sacrifices: mark this our laud in the wild joy of Soma.

7.21.d: प्र यन्ति यज्ञं विपयन्ति बर्हिः सोममादो विदथे दुध्रवाचः । न्यु भ्रियन्ते यशसो गृभादा दूरउपब्दो वृषणो नृषाचः ॥
7.21.e: On to the rite they move, the grass they scatter, these Soma-drinkers eloquent in synod.  Hither, for men to grasp, are brought the press-stones, far-thundering, famous, strong, that wait on heroes.

7.21.d: त्वमिन्द्र स्रवितवा अपस्कः परिष्ठिता अहिना शूर पूर्वीः । त्वद्वावक्रे रथ्यो३ न धेना रेजन्ते विश्वा कृत्रिमाणि भीषा ॥
7.21.e: Indra, thou settest free the many waters that were encompassed, Hero, by the Dragon.  Down rolled, as if on chariots borne, the rivers: through fear of thee all things created tremble.

7.21.d: भीमो विवेषायुधेभिरेषामपांसि विश्वा नर्याणि विद्वान् । इन्द्रः पुरो जर्हृषाणो वि दूधोद्वि वज्रहस्तो महिना जघान ॥
7.21.e: Skilled in all manly deeds the God terrific hath with his weapons mastered these opponents.  Indra in rapturous joy shook down their castles he slew them in his might, the Thunder-wielder.

7.21.d: न यातव इन्द्र जूजुवुर्नो न वन्दना शविष्ठ वेद्याभिः । स शर्धदर्यो विषुणस्य जन्तोर्मा शिश्नदेवा अपि गुर्ऋतं नः ॥
7.21.e: No evil spirits have impelled us, Indra, nor fiends, O Mightiest God, with their devices.  Let our true God subdue the hostile rabble: let not the lewd approach our holy worship.

7.21.d: अभि क्रत्वेन्द्र भूरध ज्मन्न ते विव्यङ्महिमानं रजांसि । स्वेना हि वृत्रं शवसा जघन्थ न शत्रुरन्तं विविदद्युधा ते ॥
7.21.e: Thou in thy strength surpassest Earth and Heaven: the regions comprehend not all thy greatness.  With thine own power and might thou slewest Vṛtra: no foe hath found the end of thee in battle.

7.21.d: देवाश्चित्ते असुर्याय पूर्वेऽनु क्षत्राय ममिरे सहांसि । इन्द्रो मघानि दयते विषह्येन्द्रं वाजस्य जोहुवन्त सातौ ॥
7.21.e: Even the earlier Deities submitted their powers to thy supreme divine dominion.  Indra wins wealth and deals it out to other's: men in the strife for booty call on Indra.

7.21.d: कीरिश्चिद्धि त्वामवसे जुहावेशानमिन्द्र सौभगस्य भूरेः । अवो बभूथ शतमूते अस्मे अभिक्षत्तुस्त्वावतो वरूता ॥
7.21.e: The humble hath invoked thee for protection, thee, Lord of great felicity, O Indra.  Thou with a hundred aids hast been our Helper: one who brings gifts like thee hath his defender.

7.21.d: सखायस्त इन्द्र विश्वह स्याम नमोवृधासो महिना तरुत्र । वन्वन्तु स्मा तेऽवसा समीके३ऽभीतिमर्यो वनुषां शवांसि ॥
7.21.e: May we, O Indra, be thy friends for ever, eagerly, Conqueror, yielding greater homage.  May, through thy grace, the strength of us who battle quell in the shock the onset of the foeman.

7.21.d: स न इन्द्र त्वयताया इषे धास्त्मना च ये मघवानो जुनन्ति । वस्वी षु ते जरित्रे अस्तु शक्तिर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
