7.21.e: Place us by food which thou hast given, O Indra, us and the wealthy patrons who command us.  Let thy great power bring good to him who lauds thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.22.d: पिबा सोममिन्द्र मन्दतु त्वा यं ते सुषाव हर्यश्वाद्रिः । सोतुर्बाहुभ्यां सुयतो नार्वा ॥
7.22.e: DRINK Soma, Lord of Bays, and let it cheer thee: Indra, the stone, like a well guided courser,  Directed by the presser's arms hath pressed it.

7.22.d: यस्ते मदो युज्यश्चारुरस्ति येन वृत्राणि हर्यश्व हंसि । स त्वामिन्द्र प्रभूवसो ममत्तु ॥
7.22.e: So let the draught of joy, thy dear companion, by which, O Lord of Bays, thou slayest foemen,  Delight thee, Indra, Lord of princely treasures.

7.22.d: बोधा सु मे मघवन्वाचमेमां यां ते वसिष्ठो अर्चति प्रशस्तिम् । इमा ब्रह्म सधमादे जुषस्व ॥
7.22.e: Mark closely, Maghavan, the words I utter, this eulogy recited by Vasiṣṭha:  Accept the prayers I offer at thy banquet.

7.22.d: श्रुधी हवं विपिपानस्याद्रेर्बोधा विप्रस्यार्चतो मनीषाम् । कृष्वा दुवांस्यन्तमा सचेमा ॥
7.22.e: Hear thou the call of the juice-drinking press-stone: hear thou the Brahman's hymn who sings and lauds thee.  Take to thine inmost self these adorations.

7.22.d: न ते गिरो अपि मृष्ये तुरस्य न सुष्टुतिमसुर्यस्य विद्वान् । सदा ते नाम स्वयशो विवक्मि ॥
7.22.e: I know and ne’er forget the hymns and praises of thee, the Conqueror, and thy strength immortal.  Thy name I ever utter. Self-Refulgent

7.22.d: भूरि हि ते सवना मानुषेषु भूरि मनीषी हवते त्वामित् । मारे अस्मन्मघवञ्ज्योक्कः ॥
7.22.e: Among mankind many are thy libations, and many a time the pious sageinvokes thee.  O Maghavan, be not long distant from us.

7.22.d: तुभ्येदिमा सवना शूर विश्वा तुभ्यं ब्रह्माणि वर्धना कृणोमि । त्वं नृभिर्हव्यो विश्वधासि ॥
7.22.e: All these libations are for thee, O Hero: to thee I offer these my prayers. that strengthen.  Ever, in every place, must men invoke thee.

7.22.d: नू चिन्नु ते मन्यमानस्य दस्मोदश्नुवन्ति महिमानमुग्र । न वीर्यमिन्द्र ते न राधः ॥
7.22.e: Never do men attain, O Wonder-Worker, thy greatness, Mighty One, who must be lauded,  Nor, Indra, thine heroic power and bounty.

7.22.d: ये च पूर्व ऋषयो ये च नूत्ना इन्द्र ब्रह्माणि जनयन्त विप्राः । अस्मे ते सन्तु सख्या शिवानि यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.22.e: Among all Ṛṣis, Indra, old and recent, who have engendered hymns as sacred singers,  Even with us be thine auspicious friendships. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.23.d: उदु ब्रह्माण्यैरत श्रवस्येन्द्रं समर्ये महया वसिष्ठ । आ यो विश्वानि शवसा ततानोपश्रोता म ईवतो वचांसि ॥
7.23.e: PRAYERS have been offered up through love of glory: Vasiṣṭha, honour Indra in the battle.  He who with might extends through all existence hears words which I, his faithful servant, utter.

7.23.d: अयामि घोष इन्द्र देवजामिरिरज्यन्त यच्छुरुधो विवाचि । नहि स्वमायुश्चिकिते जनेषु तानीदंहांस्यति पर्ष्यस्मान् ॥
7.23.e: A cry was raised which reached the Gods, O Indra, a cry to them to send us strength in combat.  None among men knows his own life's duration: bear us in safety over these our troubles.

7.23.d: युजे रथं गवेषणं हरिभ्यामुप ब्रह्माणि जुजुषाणमस्थुः । वि बाधिष्ट स्य रोदसी महित्वेन्द्रो वृत्राण्यप्रती जघन्वान् ॥
7.23.e: The Bays, the booty-seeking car I harness: my prayers have reached him who accepts them gladly.  Indra, when he had slain resistless foemen, forced with his might the two world-halves asunder.

7.23.d: आपश्चित्पिप्युः स्तर्यो३ न गावो नक्षन्नृतं जरितारस्त इन्द्र । याहि वायुर्न नियुतो नो अच्छा त्वं हि धीभिर्दयसे वि वाजान् ॥
7.23.e: Like barren cows, moreover, swelled the waters: the singen sought thy holy rite, O Indra.  Come unto us as with his team comes Vāyu: thou, through our solemn hymns bestowest booty.

7.23.d: ते त्वा मदा इन्द्र मादयन्तु शुष्मिणं तुविराधसं जरित्रे । एको देवत्रा दयसे हि मर्तानस्मिञ्छूर सवने मादयस्व ॥
7.23.e: So may these gladdening draughts rejoice thee, Indra, the Mighty, very bounteous to the singer.  Alone among the Gods thou pitiest mortals: O Hero, make thee glad at this libation.

7.23.d: एवेदिन्द्रं वृषणं वज्रबाहुं वसिष्ठासो अभ्यर्चन्त्यर्कैः । स नः स्तुतो वीरवद्धातु गोमद्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.23.e: Thus the Vasisthas glorify with praises Indra, the Powerful whose arm wields thunder.  Praised, may he guard our wealth in kine and heroes. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.24.d: योनिष्ट इन्द्र सदने अकारि तमा नृभिः पुरुहूत प्र याहि । असो यथा नोऽविता वृधे च ददो वसूनि ममदश्च सोमैः ॥
7.24.e: A HOME is made for thee to dwell in, Indra: O Much-invoked, go thitherwith the heroes.  That thou, to prosper us, mayst be our Helper, vouchsafe us wealth, rejoice with draughts of Soma.

7.24.d: गृभीतं ते मन इन्द्र द्विबर्हाः सुतः सोमः परिषिक्ता मधूनि । विसृष्टधेना भरते सुवृक्तिरियमिन्द्रं जोहुवती मनीषा ॥
7.24.e: Indra, thy wish, twice-strong, is comprehended: pressed is the Soma, poured are pleasant juices.  This hymn of praise, from loosened tongue, made perfect, draws Indra to itself with loud invoking.

7.24.d: आ नो दिव आ पृथिव्या ऋजीषिन्निदं बर्हिः सोमपेयाय याहि । वहन्तु त्वा हरयो मद्र्यञ्चमाङ्गूषमच्छा तवसं मदाय ॥
7.24.e: Come, thou Impetuous; God, from earth or heaven; come to our holy grass to drink the Soma.  Hither to me let thy Bay Horses bring thee to listen to our hymns and make thee joyful.

7.24.d: आ नो विश्वाभिरूतिभिः सजोषा ब्रह्म जुषाणो हर्यश्व याहि । वरीवृजत्स्थविरेभिः सुशिप्रास्मे दधद्वृषणं शुष्ममिन्द्र ॥
7.24.e: Come unto us with all thine aids, accordant, Lord of Bay Steeds, accepting our devotions,  Fair-helmeted, o’ercoming with the mighty, and lending us the strength of bulls, O Indra.

7.24.d: एष स्तोमो मह उग्राय वाहे धुरी३वात्यो न वाजयन्नधायि । इन्द्र त्वायमर्क ईट्टे वसूनां दिवीव द्यामधि नः श्रोमतं धाः ॥
7.24.e: As to the chariot pole a vigorous courser, this laud is brought to the great strong Upholder.  This hymn solicits wealth of thee: in heaven, as ’twere above the sky, set thou our glory.

7.24.d: एवा न इन्द्र वार्यस्य पूर्धि प्र ते महीं सुमतिं वेविदाम । इषं पिन्व मघवद्भ्यः सुवीरां यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.24.e: With precious things. O Indra, thus content us: may we attain to thine exalted favour.  Send our chiefs plenteous food with hero children. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.25.d: आ ते मह इन्द्रोत्युग्र समन्यवो यत्समरन्त सेनाः । पताति दिद्युन्नर्यस्य बाह्वोर्मा ते मनो विष्वद्र्य१ग्वि चारीत् ॥
7.25.e: WHEN with thy mighty help, O potent Indra, the armies rush together in their fury.  When from the strong man's arm the lightning flieth, let not the mind go forth to side with others.

7.25.d: नि दुर्ग इन्द्र श्नथिह्यमित्राँ अभि ये नो मर्तासो अमन्ति । आरे तं शंसं कृणुहि निनित्सोरा नो भर सम्भरणं वसूनाम् ॥
7.25.e: O Indra, where the ground is hard to traverse, smite down our foes, the mortals who assail us,  Keep far from us the curse of the reviler: bring us accumulated store of treasures.

7.25.d: शतं ते शिप्रिन्नूतयः सुदासे सहस्रं शंसा उत रातिरस्तु । जहि वधर्वनुषो मर्त्यस्यास्मे द्युम्नमधि रत्नं च धेहि ॥
7.25.e: God of the fair helm, give Sudās a hundred succours, a thousand blessings, and thy bounty.  Strike down the weapon of our mortal foeman: bestow upon us splendid fame and riches.

7.25.d: त्वावतो हीन्द्र क्रत्वे अस्मि त्वावतोऽवितुः शूर रातौ । विश्वेदहानि तविषीव उग्रँ ओकः कृणुष्व हरिवो न मर्धीः ॥
7.25.e: I wait the power of one like thee, O Indra, gifts of a Helper such as thou art, Hero.  Strong, Mighty God, dwell with me now and ever: Lord of Bay Horses, do not thou desert us.

7.25.d: कुत्सा एते हर्यश्वाय शूषमिन्द्रे सहो देवजूतमियानाः । सत्रा कृधि सुहना शूर वृत्रा वयं तरुत्राः सनुयाम वाजम् ॥
7.25.e: Here are the Kutsas supplicating Indra for might, the Lord of Bays for God-sent conquest.  Make our foes ever easy to be vanquished: may we, victorious, win the spoil, O Hero.

7.25.d: एवा न इन्द्र वार्यस्य पूर्धि प्र ते महीं सुमतिं वेविदाम । इषं पिन्व मघवद्भ्यः सुवीरां यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.25.e: With precious things, O Indra, thus content us: may we attain to thine exalted favour.  Send our chiefs plenteous food with hero children. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.26.d: न सोम इन्द्रमसुतो ममाद नाब्रह्माणो मघवानं सुतासः । तस्मा उक्थं जनये यज्जुजोषन्नृवन्नवीयः शृणवद्यथा नः ॥
7.26.e: SOMA unpressed ne’er gladdened liberal Indra, no juices pressed without a prayer have pleased him.  I generate a laud that shall delight him, new and heroic, so that he may hear us.

7.26.d: उक्थउक्थे सोम इन्द्रं ममाद नीथेनीथे मघवानं सुतासः । यदीं सबाधः पितरं न पुत्राः समानदक्षा अवसे हवन्ते ॥
7.26.e: At every laud the Soma gladdens Indra: pressed juices please him as each psalm is chanted,  What time the priests with one united effort call him to aid, as sons invoke their father.

7.26.d: चकार ता कृणवन्नूनमन्या यानि ब्रुवन्ति वेधसः सुतेषु । जनीरिव पतिरेकः समानो नि मामृजे पुर इन्द्रः सु सर्वाः ॥
7.26.e: These deeds he did; let him achieve new exploits, such as the priests declare at their libations.  Indra hath taken and possessed all castles, like as one common husband doth his spouses.

7.26.d: एवा तमाहुरुत शृण्व इन्द्र एको विभक्ता तरणिर्मघानाम् । मिथस्तुर ऊतयो यस्य पूर्वीरस्मे भद्राणि सश्चत प्रियाणि ॥
7.26.e: Even thus have they declared him. Famed is Indra as Conqueror, sole distributer of treasures;  Whose many succours come in close succession. May dear delightful benefits attend us.

7.26.d: एवा वसिष्ठ इन्द्रमूतये नॄन्कृष्टीनां वृषभं सुते गृणाति । सहस्रिण उप नो माहि वाजान्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.26.e: Thus, to bring help to men, Vasiṣṭha laudeth Indra, the peoples' Hero, at libation.  Bestow upon us strength and wealth in thousands. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.27.d: इन्द्रं नरो नेमधिता हवन्ते यत्पार्या युनजते धियस्ताः । शूरो नृषाता शवसश्चकान आ गोमति व्रजे भजा त्वं नः ॥
7.27.e: MEN call on Indra in the armed encounter that he may make the hymns they sing decisive.  Hero, rejoicing in thy might, in combat give us a portion of the stall of cattle,

7.27.d: य इन्द्र शुष्मो मघवन्ते अस्ति शिक्षा सखिभ्यः पुरुहूत नृभ्यः । त्वं हि दृळ्हा मघवन्विचेता अपा वृधि परिवृतं न राधः ॥
7.27.e: Grant, Indra Maghavan, invoked of many, to these my friends the strength which thou possessest.  Thou, Maghavan, hast rent strong places open: unclose for us, Wise God, thy hidden bounty.

7.27.d: इन्द्रो राजा जगतश्चर्षणीनामधि क्षमि विषुरूपं यदस्ति । ततो ददाति दाशुषे वसूनि चोदद्राध उपस्तुतश्चिदर्वाक् ॥
7.27.e: King of the living world, of men, is Indra, of all in varied form that earth containeth.  Thence to the worshipper he giveth riches: may he enrich us also when we laud him.

7.27.d: नू चिन्न इन्द्रो मघवा सहूती दानो वाजं नि यमते न ऊती । अनूना यस्य दक्षिणा पीपाय वामं नृभ्यो अभिवीता सखिभ्यः ॥
7.27.e: Maghavan Indra, when we all invoke him, bountiful ever sendeth strength to aid us:  Whose perfect guerdon, never failing, bringeth wealth to the men, to friends the thing they covet.

7.27.d: नू इन्द्र राये वरिवस्कृधी न आ ते मनो ववृत्याम मघाय । गोमदश्वावद्रथवद्व्यन्तो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.27.e: Quick, Indra, give us room and way to riches, and let us bring thy mind to grant us treasures,  That we may win us cars and Steeds and cattle. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.28.d: ब्रह्मा ण इन्द्रोप याहि विद्वानर्वाञ्चस्ते हरयः सन्तु युक्ताः । विश्वे चिद्धि त्वा विहवन्त मर्ता अस्माकमिच्छृणुहि विश्वमिन्व ॥
7.28.e: COME to our prayers, O Indra, thou who knowest: let thy Bay Steeds be yoked and guided hither.  Though mortal men on every side invoke thee, still give thine ear to us, O All-impeller.

7.28.d: हवं त इन्द्र महिमा व्यानड्ब्रह्म यत्पासि शवसिन्नृषीणाम् । आ यद्वज्रं दधिषे हस्त उग्र घोरः सन्क्रत्वा जनिष्ठा अषाळ्हः ॥
7.28.e: Thy greatness reacheth to our invocation, the sages' prayer which, Potent God, thou guardest.  What time thy hand, O Mighty, holds the thunder, awful in strength thou hast become resistless.

7.28.d: तव प्रणीतीन्द्र जोहुवानान्त्सं यन्नॄन्न रोदसी निनेथ । महे क्षत्राय शवसे हि जज्ञेऽतूतुजिं चित्तूतुजिरशिश्नत् ॥
7.28.e: What time thou drewest both world-halves together, like heroes led by thee who call each other-  For thou wast born for strength and high dominion-then e’en the active overthrew the sluggish.

7.28.d: एभिर्न इन्द्राहभिर्दशस्य दुर्मित्रासो हि क्षितयः पवन्ते । प्रति यच्चष्टे अनृतमनेना अव द्विता वरुणो मायी नः सात् ॥
7.28.e: Honour us in these present days, O Indra, for hostile men are making expiation.  Our sin that sinless Varuṇa discovered, the Wondrous-Wise hath long ago forgiven.

7.28.d: वोचेमेदिन्द्रं मघवानमेनं महो रायो राधसो यद्ददन्नः । यो अर्चतो ब्रह्मकृतिमविष्ठो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.28.e: We will address this liberal Lord, this Indra, that he may grant us gifts of ample riches,  Best favourer of the singer's prayer and praises. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.29.d: अयं सोम इन्द्र तुभ्यं सुन्व आ तु प्र याहि हरिवस्तदोकाः । पिबा त्व१स्य सुषुतस्य चारोर्ददो मघानि मघवन्नियानः ॥
7.29.e: THIS Soma hath been pressed for thee, O Indra: come hither, Lord of Bays, for this thou lovest.  Drink of this fair, this well-effused libation: Maghavan, give us wealth when we implore thee.

7.29.d: ब्रह्मन्वीर ब्रह्मकृतिं जुषाणोऽर्वाचीनो हरिभिर्याहि तूयम् । अस्मिन्नू षु सवने मादयस्वोप ब्रह्माणि शृणव इमा नः ॥
7.29.e: Come to us quickly with thy Bay Steeds, Hero, come to our prayer, accepting our devotion.  Enjoy thyself aright at this libation, and listen thou unto the prayers we offer.

7.29.d: का ते अस्त्यरंकृतिः सूक्तैः कदा नूनं ते मघवन्दाशेम । विश्वा मतीरा ततने त्वायाधा म इन्द्र शृणवो हवेमा ॥
7.29.e: What satisfaction do our hymns afford thee? When, Maghavan? Now let us do thee service.  Hymns, only hymns, with love for thee, I weave thee: then hear, O Indra, these mine invocations.

7.29.d: उतो घा ते पुरुष्या३ इदासन्येषां पूर्वेषामशृणोर्ऋषीणाम् । अधाहं त्वा मघवञ्जोहवीमि त्वं न इन्द्रासि प्रमतिः पितेव ॥
7.29.e: They, verily, were also human beings whom thou wast wont to hear, those earlier sages.  Hence I, O Indra Maghavan, invoke thee: thou art our Providence, even as a Father.

7.29.d: वोचेमेदिन्द्रं मघवानमेनं महो रायो राधसो यद्ददन्नः । यो अर्चतो ब्रह्मकृतिमविष्ठो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.29.e: We will address this liberal Lord, this Indra, that he may grant us gifts of ample riches,  Best favourer of the singer's prayer and praises. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.30.d: आ नो देव शवसा याहि शुष्मिन्भवा वृध इन्द्र रायो अस्य । महे नृम्णाय नृपते सुवज्र महि क्षत्राय पौंस्याय शूर ॥
7.30.e: WITH power and strength, O Mighty God, approach us: be the augmenter, Indra, of these riches;  Strong Thunderer, Lord of men, for potent valour, for manly exploit and for high dominion.

7.30.d: हवन्त उ त्वा हव्यं विवाचि तनूषु शूराः सूर्यस्य सातौ । त्वं विश्वेषु सेन्यो जनेषु त्वं वृत्राणि रन्धया सुहन्तु ॥
7.30.e: Thee, worth invoking, in the din of battle, heroes invoke in fray for life and sunlight.  Among all people thou art foremost fighter: give up our enemies to easy slaughter.

7.30.d: अहा यदिन्द्र सुदिना व्युच्छान्दधो यत्केतुमुपमं समत्सु । न्य१ग्निः सीददसुरो न होता हुवानो अत्र सुभगाय देवान् ॥
7.30.e: When fair bright days shall dawn on us, O Indra, and thou shalt bring thy banner near in battle,  Agni the Asura shall sit as Herald, calling Gods hither for our great good fortune.

7.30.d: वयं ते त इन्द्र ये च देव स्तवन्त शूर ददतो मघानि । यच्छा सूरिभ्य उपमं वरूथं स्वाभुवो जरणामश्नवन्त ॥
7.30.e: Thine are we, Indra, thine, both these who praise thee, and those who give rich gifts, O God and Hero.  Grant to our princes excellent protection, may they wax old and still be strong and happy.

7.30.d: वोचेमेदिन्द्रं मघवानमेनं महो रायो राधसो यद्ददन्नः । यो अर्चतो ब्रह्मकृतिमविष्ठो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.30.e: We will address this liberal Lord, this Indra that he may grant us gifts of ample riches:  Best favourer of the singer's prayer and praises. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.31.d: प्र व इन्द्राय मादनं हर्यश्वाय गायत । सखायः सोमपाव्ने ॥
7.31.e: SING ye a song, to make him glad, to Indra, Lord of Tawny Steeds,  The Soma-drinker, O my friends.

7.31.d: शंसेदुक्थं सुदानव उत द्युक्षं यथा नरः । चकृमा सत्यराधसे ॥
7.31.e: To him the Bounteous say the laud, and let us glorify, as men May do, the Giver of true gifts.

7.31.d: त्वं न इन्द्र वाजयुस्त्वं गव्युः शतक्रतो । त्वं हिरण्ययुर्वसो ॥
7.31.e: O Indra, Lord of boundless might, for us thou winnest strength and kine,  Thou winnest gold for us, Good Lord.

7.31.d: वयमिन्द्र त्वायवोऽभि प्र णोनुमो वृषन् । विद्धी त्व१स्य नो वसो ॥
7.31.e: Faithful to thee we loudly sing, heroic Indra, songs to thee: Mark, O Good Lord, this act of ours.

7.31.d: मा नो निदे च वक्तवेऽर्यो रन्धीरराव्णे । त्वे अपि क्रतुर्मम ॥
7.31.e: Give us not up to man's reproach, to foeman's hateful calumny: In thee alone is all my strength.

7.31.d: त्वं वर्मासि सप्रथः पुरोयोधश्च वृत्रहन् । त्वया प्रति ब्रुवे युजा ॥
7.31.e: Thou art mine ample coat of mail, my Champion, Vṛtra-Slayer, thou:  With thee for Friend I brave the foe.

7.31.d: महाँ उतासि यस्य तेऽनु स्वधावरी सहः । मम्नाते इन्द्र रोदसी ॥
7.31.e: Yea, great art thou whose conquering might two independent Powers confess.  The Heaven, O India, and the Earth.

7.31.d: तं त्वा मरुत्वती परि भुवद्वाणी सयावरी । नक्षमाणा सह द्युभिः ॥
7.31.e: So let the voice surround thee, which attends the Maruts on their way,  Reaching thee with the rays of light.

7.31.d: ऊर्ध्वासस्त्वान्विन्दवो भुवन्दस्ममुप द्यवि । सं ते नमन्त कृष्टयः ॥
7.31.e: Let the ascending drops attain to thee, the Wondrous God, in heaven:  Let all the folk bow down to thee.

7.31.d: प्र वो महे महिवृधे भरध्वं प्रचेतसे प्र सुमतिं कृणुध्वम् । विशः पूर्वीः प्र चरा चर्षणिप्राः ॥
7.31.e: Bring to the Wise, the Great, who waxeth mighty, your offerings, and make ready your devotion;  To many clans he goeth, man's controller.

7.31.d: उरुव्यचसे महिने सुवृक्तिमिन्द्राय ब्रह्म जनयन्त विप्राः । तस्य व्रतानि न मिनन्ति धीराः ॥
7.31.e: For Indra, the sublime, the far-pervading, have singers generated prayer and praises:  The sages never violate his statutes.

7.31.d: इन्द्रं वाणीरनुत्तमन्युमेव सत्रा राजानं दधिरे सहध्यै । हर्यश्वाय बर्हया समापीन् ॥
7.31.e: The choirs have stablished Indra King for ever, for victory, him whose anger is resistless:  And, for the Bays' Lord, strengthened those he loveth.

7.32.d: मो षु त्वा वाघतश्चनारे अस्मन्नि रीरमन् । आरात्ताच्चित्सधमादं न आ गहीह वा सन्नुप श्रुधि ॥
7.32.e: LET none, no, not thy worshippers, delay thee far away from us.  Even from far away come thou unto our feast, or listen if already here.

7.32.d: इमे हि ते ब्रह्मकृतः सुते सचा मधौ न मक्ष आसते । इन्द्रे कामं जरितारो वसूयवो रथे न पादमा दधुः ॥
7.32.e: For here, like flies on honey, these who pray to thee sit by the juice that they have poured.  Wealth-craving singers have on Indra set their hope, as men set foot upon a car.

7.32.d: रायस्कामो वज्रहस्तं सुदक्षिणं पुत्रो न पितरं हुवे ॥
7.32.e: Longing for wealth I call on him, the Thunderer with the strong right hand,  As a son calleth on his sire.

7.32.d: इम इन्द्राय सुन्विरे सोमासो दध्याशिरः । ताँ आ मदाय वज्रहस्त पीतये हरिभ्यां याह्योक आ ॥
7.32.e: These Soma juices, mixed with curd, have been expressed for Indra here.  Come with thy Bay Steeds, Thunder-wielder, to our home, to drink them till they make thee glad.

7.32.d: श्रवच्छ्रुत्कर्ण ईयते वसूनां नू चिन्नो मर्धिषद्गिरः । सद्यश्चिद्यः सहस्राणि शता ददन्नकिर्दित्सन्तमा मिनत् ॥
7.32.e: May he whose ear is open hear us. He is asked for wealth: will he despise our prayer?  Him who bestows at once a hundred thousand gifts none shall restrain when he would give.

7.32.d: स वीरो अप्रतिष्कुत इन्द्रेण शूशुवे नृभिः । यस्ते गभीरा सवनानि वृत्रहन्त्सुनोत्या च धावति ॥
7.32.e: The hero never checked by men hath gained his strength through Indra, he  Who presses out and pours his deep libations forth, O Vṛtra-slayer, unto thee.

7.32.d: भवा वरूथं मघवन्मघोनां यत्समजासि शर्धतः । वि त्वाहतस्य वेदनं भजेमह्या दूणाशो भरा गयम् ॥
7.32.e: When thou dost drive the fighting men together be, thou Mighty One, the mighty's shield.  May we divide the wealth of him whom thou hast slain: bring us, Unreachable, his goods.

7.32.d: सुनोता सोमपाव्ने सोममिन्द्राय वज्रिणे । पचता पक्तीरवसे कृणुध्वमित्पृणन्नित्पृणते मयः ॥
7.32.e: For Indra, Soma-drinker, armed with thunder, press the Soma juice.  Make ready your dressed meats: cause him to favour us. The Giver blesses him who gives.

7.32.d: मा स्रेधत सोमिनो दक्षता महे कृणुध्वं राय आतुजे । तरणिरिज्जयति क्षेति पुष्यति न देवासः कवत्नवे ॥
7.32.e: Grudge not, ye Soma pourers; stir you, pay the rites, for wealth, to the great Conqueror.  Only the active conquers dwells in peace, and thrives: not for the niggard are the Gods.

7.32.d: नकिः सुदासो रथं पर्यास न रीरमत् । इन्द्रो यस्याविता यस्य मरुतो गमत्स गोमति व्रजे ॥
7.32.e: No one hath overturned or stayed the car of him who freely gives.  The man whom Indra and the Marut host defend comes to a stable full of kine.

7.32.d: गमद्वाजं वाजयन्निन्द्र मर्त्यो यस्य त्वमविता भुवः । अस्माकं बोध्यविता रथानामस्माकं शूर नृणाम् ॥
7.32.e: Indra, that man when fighting shall obtain the spoil, whose strong defender thou wilt be.  Be thou the gracious helper, Hero I of our cars, be thou the helper of our men.

7.32.d: उदिन्न्वस्य रिच्यतेंऽशो धनं न जिग्युषः । य इन्द्रो हरिवान्न दभन्ति तं रिपो दक्षं दधाति सोमिनि ॥
7.32.e: His portion is exceeding great like a victorious soldier's spoil.  Him who is Indra, Lord of Bays, no foes subdue. He gives the Soma-pourer strength.

7.32.d: मन्त्रमखर्वं सुधितं सुपेशसं दधात यज्ञियेष्वा । पूर्वीश्चन प्रसितयस्तरन्ति तं य इन्द्रे कर्मणा भुवत् ॥
7.32.e: Make for the Holy Gods a hymn that is not mean, but well-arranged and fair of form.  Even many snares and bonds subdue not him who dwells with Indra through his sacrifice.

7.32.d: कस्तमिन्द्र त्वावसुमा मर्त्यो दधर्षति । श्रद्धा इत्ते मघवन्पार्ये दिवि वाजी वाजं सिषासति ॥
7.32.e: Indra, what mortal will attack the man who hath his wealth in thee?  The strong will win the spoil on the decisive day through faith in thee, O Maghavan.

7.32.d: मघोनः स्म वृत्रहत्येषु चोदय ये ददति प्रिया वसु । तव प्रणीती हर्यश्व सूरिभिर्विश्वा तरेम दुरिता ॥
7.32.e: In battles with the foe urge on our mighty ones who give the treasures dear to thee,  And may we with our princes, Lord of Tawny Steeds! pass through all peril, led by thee.

7.32.d: तवेदिन्द्रावमं वसु त्वं पुष्यसि मध्यमम् । सत्रा विश्वस्य परमस्य राजसि नकिष्ट्वा गोषु वृण्वते ॥
7.32.e: Thine, Indra, is the lowest wealth, thou cherishest the mid-most wealth,  Thou ever rulest all the highest: in the fray for cattle none resisteth thee.

7.32.d: त्वं विश्वस्य धनदा असि श्रुतो य ईं भवन्त्याजयः । तवायं विश्वः पुरुहूत पार्थिवोऽवस्युर्नाम भिक्षते ॥
7.32.e: Thou art renowned as giving wealth to every one in all the battles that are fought.  Craving protection, all these people of the earth, O Much-invoked, implore thy name.

7.32.d: यदिन्द्र यावतस्त्वमेतावदहमीशीय । स्तोतारमिद्दिधिषेय रदावसो न पापत्वाय रासीय ॥
7.32.e: If I, O Indra, were the Lord of riches ample as thine own,  I should support the singer, God. who givest wealth! and not abandon him to woe.

7.32.d: शिक्षेयमिन्महयते दिवेदिवे राय आ कुहचिद्विदे । नहि त्वदन्यन्मघवन्न आप्यं वस्यो अस्ति पिता चन ॥
7.32.e: Each day would I enrich the man who sang my praise, in whatsoever place he were.  No kinship is there better, Maghavan, than thine: a father even is no more.

7.32.d: तरणिरित्सिषासति वाजं पुरंध्या युजा । आ व इन्द्रं पुरुहूतं नमे गिरा नेमिं तष्टेव सुद्र्वम् ॥
7.32.e: With Plenty for his true ally the active man will gain the spoil.  Your Indra, Much-invoked, I bend with song, as bends a wright his wheel of solid wood.

7.32.d: न दुष्टुती मर्त्यो विन्दते वसु न स्रेधन्तं रयिर्नशत् । सुशक्तिरिन्मघवन्तुभ्यं मावते देष्णं यत्पार्ये दिवि ॥
7.32.e: A moral wins no riches by unworthy praise: wealth comes not to the niggard churl.  Light is the task to give, O Maghavan, to one like me on the decisive day.

7.32.d: अभि त्वा शूर नोनुमोऽदुग्धा इव धेनवः । ईशानमस्य जगतः स्वर्दृशमीशानमिन्द्र तस्थुषः ॥
7.32.e: Like kine unmilked we call aloud, Hero, to thee, and sing thy praise,  Looker on heavenly light, Lord of this moving world, Lord, Indra, of what moveth not.

7.32.d: न त्वावाँ अन्यो दिव्यो न पार्थिवो न जातो न जनिष्यते । अश्वायन्तो मघवन्निन्द्र वाजिनो गव्यन्तस्त्वा हवामहे ॥
7.32.e: None other like to thee, of earth or of the heavens, hath been or ever will be born.  Desiring horses, Indra Maghavan! and kine, as men of might we call on thee.

7.32.d: अभी षतस्तदा भरेन्द्र ज्यायः कनीयसः । पुरूवसुर्हि मघवन्त्सनादसि भरेभरे च हव्यः ॥
7.32.e: Bring, Indra, the Victorious Ones; bring, elder thou, the younger host.  For, Maghavan, thou art rich in treasures from of old, and must be called in every fight.

7.32.d: परा णुदस्व मघवन्नमित्रान्त्सुवेदा नो वसू कृधि । अस्माकं बोध्यविता महाधने भवा वृधः सखीनाम् ॥
7.32.e: Drive thou away our enemies, O Maghavan: make riches easy to be won.  Be thou our good Protector in the strife for spoil: Cherisher of our friends be thou.

7.32.d: इन्द्र क्रतुं न आ भर पिता पुत्रेभ्यो यथा । शिक्षा णो अस्मिन्पुरुहूत यामनि जीवा ज्योतिरशीमहि ॥
7.32.e: O Indra, give us wisdom as a sire gives wisdom to his sons.  Guide us, O Much-invoked, in this our way may we still live and look upon the light.

7.32.d: मा नो अज्ञाता वृजना दुराध्यो३ माशिवासो अव क्रमुः । त्वया वयं प्रवतः शश्वतीरपोऽति शूर तरामसि ॥
7.32.e: Grant that no mighty foes, unknown, malevolent, unhallowed, tread us to the ground.  With thine assistance, Hero, may we ass through all the waters that are rul`ng down.

7.33.d: श्वित्यञ्चो मा दक्षिणतस्कपर्दा धियंजिन्वासो अभि हि प्रमन्दुः । उत्तिष्ठन्वोचे परि बर्हिषो नॄन्न मे दूरादवितवे वसिष्ठाः ॥
7.33.e: THESE who wear hair-knots on the right, the movers of holy thought, white-robed, have won me over.  I warned the men, when from the grass I raised me, Not from afar can my Vasisthas help you.

7.33.d: दूरादिन्द्रमनयन्ना सुतेन तिरो वैशन्तमति पान्तमुग्रम् । पाशद्युम्नस्य वायतस्य सोमात्सुतादिन्द्रोऽवृणीता वसिष्ठान् ॥
7.33.e: With  Soma  they brought Indra from a distance, Over Vaisanta, from the strong libation.  Indra preferred Vasisthas to the Soma pressed by the son of Vayata, Pasadyumna.

7.33.d: एवेन्नु कं सिन्धुमेभिस्ततारेवेन्नु कं भेदमेभिर्जघान । एवेन्नु कं दाशराज्ञे सुदासं प्रावदिन्द्रो ब्रह्मणा वो वसिष्ठाः ॥
7.33.e: So, verily, with these he crossed the river, in company with these he slaughtered Bheda.  So in the fight with the Ten Kings, Vasisthas! did Indra help Sudās through your devotions.

7.33.d: जुष्टी नरो ब्रह्मणा वः पितॄणामक्षमव्ययं न किला रिषाथ । यच्छक्वरीषु बृहता रवेणेन्द्रे शुष्ममदधाता वसिष्ठाः ॥
7.33.e: I gladly, men I with prayer prayed by our fathers have fixed your axle: ye shall not be injured:  Since, when ye sang aloud the Sakvari verses, Vasisthas! ye invigorated Indra.

7.33.d: उद्द्यामिवेत्तृष्णजो नाथितासोऽदीधयुर्दाशराज्ञे वृतासः । वसिष्ठस्य स्तुवत इन्द्रो अश्रोदुरुं तृत्सुभ्यो अकृणोदु लोकम् ॥
7.33.e: Like thirsty men they looked to heaven, in battle with the Ten Kings, surrounded and imploring.  Then Indra heard Vasiṣṭha as he praised him, and gave the Trtsus ample room and freedom.

7.33.d: दण्डा इवेद्गोअजनास आसन्परिच्छिन्ना भरता अर्भकासः । अभवच्च पुरएता वसिष्ठ आदित्तृत्सूनां विशो अप्रथन्त ॥
7.33.e: Like sticks and staves wherewith they drive the cattle, Stripped bare, the Bharatas were found defenceless:  Vasiṣṭha then became their chief and leader: then widely. were the Trtsus' clans extended.

7.33.d: त्रयः कृण्वन्ति भुवनेषु रेतस्तिस्रः प्रजा आर्या ज्योतिरग्राः । त्रयो घर्मास उषसं सचन्ते सर्वाँ इत्ताँ अनु विदुर्वसिष्ठाः ॥
7.33.e: Three fertilize the worlds with genial moisture: three noble Creatures cast a light before them.  Three that give warmth to all attend the morning. All these have they discovered, these Vasisthas.

7.33.d: सूर्यस्येव वक्षथो ज्योतिरेषां समुद्रस्येव महिमा गभीरः । वातस्येव प्रजवो नान्येन स्तोमो वसिष्ठा अन्वेतवे वः ॥
7.33.e: Like the Sun's growing glory is their splendour, and like the sea's is their unflathomed greatness.  Their course is like the wind's. Your laud, Vasisthas, can never be attained by any other.

7.33.d: त इन्निण्यं हृदयस्य प्रकेतैः सहस्रवल्शमभि सं चरन्ति । यमेन ततं परिधिं वयन्तोऽप्सरस उप सेदुर्वसिष्ठाः ॥
7.33.e: They with perceptions of the heart in secret resort to that which spreads a thousand branches.  The Apsaras brought hither the Vasisthas wearing the vesture spun for them by Yama.

7.33.d: विद्युतो ज्योतिः परि संजिहानं मित्रावरुणा यदपश्यतां त्वा । तत्ते जन्मोतैकं वसिष्ठागस्त्यो यत्त्वा विश आजभार ॥
7.33.e: A form of lustre springing from the lightning wast thou, when Varuṇa and Mitra saw thee.  Tliy one and only birth was then, Vasiṣṭha, when from thy stock Agastya brought thee hither.

7.33.d: उतासि मैत्रावरुणो वसिष्ठोर्वश्या ब्रह्मन्मनसोऽधि जातः । द्रप्सं स्कन्नं ब्रह्मणा दैव्येन विश्वे देवाः पुष्करे त्वाददन्त ॥
7.33.e: Born of their love for Urvasi, Vasiṣṭha thou, priest, art son of Varuṇa and Mitra;  And as a fallen drop, in heavenly fervour, all the Gods laid thee on a lotus-blossorn.

7.33.d: स प्रकेत उभयस्य प्रविद्वान्त्सहस्रदान उत वा सदानः । यमेन ततं परिधिं वयिष्यन्नप्सरसः परि जज्ञे वसिष्ठः ॥
7.33.e: He thinker, knower both of earth and heaven, endowed with many a gift, bestowing thousands,  Destined to wear the vesture spun by Yama, sprang from the Apsaras to life, Vasiṣṭha.

7.33.d: सत्रे ह जाताविषिता नमोभिः कुम्भे रेतः सिषिचतुः समानम् । ततो ह मान उदियाय मध्यात्ततो जातमृषिमाहुर्वसिष्ठम् ॥
7.33.e: Born at the sacrifice, urged by adorations, both with a common flow bedewed the pitcher.  Then from the midst thereof there rose up Māna, and thence they say was born the sage Vasiṣṭha.

7.33.d: उक्थभृतं सामभृतं बिभर्ति ग्रावाणं बिभ्रत्प्र वदात्यग्रे । उपैनमाध्वं सुमनस्यमाना आ वो गच्छाति प्रतृदो वसिष्ठः ॥
7.33.e: He brings the bearer of the laud and Sāman: first shall he speak bringing the stone for pressing.  With grateful hearts in reverence approach him: to you, O Pratrdas, Vasiṣṭha cometh.

7.34.d: प्र शुक्रैतु देवी मनीषा अस्मत्सुतष्टो रथो न वाजी ॥
7.34.e: MAY our divine and brilliant hymn go forth, like a swift chariot wrought and fashioned well.

7.34.d: विदुः पृथिव्या दिवो जनित्रं शृण्वन्त्यापो अध क्षरन्तीः ॥
7.34.e: The waters listen as they flow along: they know the origin of heaven and earth.

7.34.d: आपश्चिदस्मै पिन्वन्त पृथ्वीर्वृत्रेषु शूरा मंसन्त उग्राः ॥
7.34.e: Yea, the broad waters swell their flood ior him: of him strong heroes think amid their foes.

7.34.d: आ धूर्ष्वस्मै दधाताश्वानिन्द्रो न वज्री हिरण्यबाहुः ॥
7.34.e: Set ye for him the coursers to the pole: like Indra Thunderer is the Golden-armed.

7.34.d: अभि प्र स्थाताहेव यज्ञं यातेव पत्मन्त्मना हिनोत ॥
7.34.e: Arouse you, like the days, to sacrifice speed gladly like a traveller on the way.

7.34.d: त्मना समत्सु हिनोत यज्ञं दधात केतुं जनाय वीरम् ॥
7.34.e: Go swift to battles, to the sacrifice: set up a flag, a hero for the folk.

7.34.d: उदस्य शुष्माद्भानुर्नार्त बिभर्ति भारं पृथिवी न भूम ॥
7.34.e: Up from his strength hath risen as ’twere a light: it bears the load as earth bears living things.

7.34.d: ह्वयामि देवाँ अयातुरग्ने साधन्नृतेन धियं दधामि ॥
7.34.e: Agni, no demon I invoke the Gods: by law completing it, I form a hymn.

7.34.d: अभि वो देवीं धियं दधिध्वं प्र वो देवत्रा वाचं कृणुध्वम् ॥
7.34.e: Closely albout you lay your heavenly song, and send your voice to where the Gods abide.

7.34.d: आ चष्ट आसां पाथो नदीनां वरुण उग्रः सहस्रचक्षाः ॥
7.34.e: Varuṇa, Mighty, with a thousand eyes, beholds the paths wherein these rivers run.

7.34.d: राजा राष्ट्रानां पेशो नदीनामनुत्तमस्मै क्षत्रं विश्वायु ॥
7.34.e: He, King of kings, the glory of the floods, o’er all that liveth hath resistless sway.

7.34.d: अविष्टो अस्मान्विश्वासु विक्ष्वद्युं कृणोत शंसं निनित्सोः ॥
7.34.e: May he assist us among all the tribes, and make the envier's praise devoid of light.

7.34.d: व्येतु दिद्युद्द्विषामशेवा युयोत विष्वग्रपस्तनूनाम् ॥
7.34.e: May the foes' threatening arrow pass us by: may he put far from us our bodies' sin.

7.34.d: अवीन्नो अग्निर्हव्यान्नमोभिः प्रेष्ठो अस्मा अधायि स्तोमः ॥
7.34.e: Agni, oblation-cater, through our prayers aid us: to him our dearest laud is brought.

7.34.d: सजूर्देवेभिरपां नपातं सखायं कृध्वं शिवो नो अस्तु ॥
7.34.e: Accordant with the Gods choose for our Friend the Waters’ Child: may he be good to us.

7.34.d: अब्जामुक्थैरहिं गृणीषे बुध्ने नदीनां रजःसु षीदन् ॥
7.34.e: With lauds I sing the Dragon born of floods: he sits beneath the streams in middle air.

7.34.d: मा नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यो रिषे धान्मा यज्ञो अस्य स्रिधदृतायोः ॥
7.34.e: Ne’er may the Dragon of the Deep harm us: ne’er fail this faithful servant's sacrifice.

7.34.d: उत न एषु नृषु श्रवो धुः प्र राये यन्तु शर्धन्तो अर्यः ॥
7.34.e: To these our heroes may they grant renown: may pious men march boldly on to wealth.

7.34.d: तपन्ति शत्रुं स्व१र्ण भूमा महासेनासो अमेभिरेषाम् ॥
7.34.e: Leading great hosts, with fierce attacks of these, they burn their foes as the Sun burns the earth.

7.34.d: आ यन्नः पत्नीर्गमन्त्यच्छा त्वष्टा सुपाणिर्दधातु वीरान् ॥
7.34.e: What time our wives draw near to us, may he, left-handed Tvaṣṭar, give us hero sons.

7.34.d: प्रति नः स्तोमं त्वष्टा जुषेत स्यादस्मे अरमतिर्वसूयुः ॥
7.34.e: May Tvaṣṭar find our hymn acceptable, and may Aramati, seeking wealth, be ours.

7.34.d: ता नो रासन्रातिषाचो वसून्या रोदसी वरुणानी शृणोतु । वरूत्रीभिः सुशरणो नो अस्तु त्वष्टा सुदत्रो वि दधातु रायः ॥
7.34.e: May they who lavish gifts bestow those treasures: may Rodasī and Varuṇānī listen.  May he, with the Varūtrīs, be our refuge, may bountiful Tvaṣṭar give us store of riches.

7.34.d: तन्नो रायः पर्वतास्तन्न आपस्तद्रातिषाच ओषधीरुत द्यौः । वनस्पतिभिः पृथिवी सजोषा उभे रोदसी परि पासतो नः ॥
7.34.e: So may rich Mountains and the liberal Waters, so may all Herbs that grow on ground, and Heaven,  And Earth accordant with the Forest-Sovrans, and both the World-halves round about protect us.

7.34.d: अनु तदुर्वी रोदसी जिहातामनु द्युक्षो वरुण इन्द्रसखा । अनु विश्वे मरुतो ये सहासो रायः स्याम धरुणं धियध्यै ॥
7.34.e: To this may both the wide Worlds lend approval, and Varuṇa in heaven, whose Friend is Indra.  May all the Maruts give consent, the Victors, that we may hold great wealth in firm possession.

7.34.d: तन्न इन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निराप ओषधीर्वनिनो जुषन्त । शर्मन्त्स्याम मरुतामुपस्थे यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.34.e: May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni, Waters, Herbs, Trees accept the praise we offer.  May we find refuge in the Marut's bosom. Protect us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.35.d: शं न इन्द्राग्नी भवतामवोभिः शं न इन्द्रावरुणा रातहव्या । शमिन्द्रासोमा सुविताय शं योः शं न इन्द्रापूषणा वाजसातौ ॥
7.35.e: BEFRIEND us with their aids Indra and Agni, Indra and Varuṇa who receive oblations!  Indra and Soma give health, strength and comfort, Indra and Pūṣan be our help in battle.

7.35.d: शं नो भगः शमु नः शंसो अस्तु शं नः पुरंधिः शमु सन्तु रायः । शं नः सत्यस्य सुयमस्य शंसः शं नो अर्यमा पुरुजातो अस्तु ॥
7.35.e: Auspicious Friends to us be Bhaga, Sathsa, auspicious be Purandhi aid all Riches;  The blessing of the true and well-conducted, and Aryaman in many forms apparent.

7.35.d: शं नो धाता शमु धर्ता नो अस्तु शं न उरूची भवतु स्वधाभिः । शं रोदसी बृहती शं नो अद्रिः शं नो देवानां सुहवानि सन्तु ॥
7.35.e: Kind unto us he Maker and Sustainer, and the far-reaching Pair with God-like natures.  Auspicious unto us be Earth and Heaven, the Mountain, and the Gods’ fair invocations.

7.35.d: शं नो अग्निर्ज्योतिरनीको अस्तु शं नो मित्रावरुणावश्विना शम् । शं नः सुकृतां सुकृतानि सन्तु शं न इषिरो अभि वातु वातः ॥
7.35.e: Favour us Agni with his face of splendour, and Varuva and Mitra and the Aśvins.  Favour us noble actions of the pious, impetuous vita blow on us with favour.

7.35.d: शं नो द्यावापृथिवी पूर्वहूतौ शमन्तरिक्षं दृशये नो अस्तु । शं न ओषधीर्वनिनो भवन्तु शं नो रजसस्पतिरस्तु जिष्णुः ॥
7.35.e: Early invoked, may Heaven and Earth be friendly, and Air's mid-region good for us to look on.  To us may Herbs and Forest-Trees be gracious, gracious the Lord Victorious of the region.

7.35.d: शं न इन्द्रो वसुभिर्देवो अस्तु शमादित्येभिर्वरुणः सुशंसः । शं नो रुद्रो रुद्रेभिर्जलाषः शं नस्त्वष्टा ग्नाभिरिह शृणोतु ॥
7.35.e: Be the God Indra with the Vasus friendly, and, with Ādityas, Varuṇa who blesseth.  Kind, with the Rudras, be the Healer Rudra, and, with the Dames, may Tvaṣṭar kindly listen.

7.35.d: शं नः सोमो भवतु ब्रह्म शं नः शं नो ग्रावाणः शमु सन्तु यज्ञाः । शं नः स्वरूणां मितयो भवन्तु शं नः प्रस्व१ः शम्वस्तु वेदिः ॥
7.35.e: Blest unto us be Soma, and devotions, blest be the Sacrifice, the Stones for pressing.  Blest be the fixing of the sacred Pillars, blest be the tender Grass and blest the Altar.

7.35.d: शं नः सूर्य उरुचक्षा उदेतु शं नश्चतस्रः प्रदिशो भवन्तु । शं नः पर्वता ध्रुवयो भवन्तु शं नः सिन्धवः शमु सन्त्वापः ॥
7.35.e: May the far-seeing Sun rise up to bless us: be the four Quarters of the sky auspicious.  Auspicious be the firmly-seated Mountains, auspicious be the Rivers and the Waters.

7.35.d: शं नो अदितिर्भवतु व्रतेभिः शं नो भवन्तु मरुतः स्वर्काः । शं नो विष्णुः शमु पूषा नो अस्तु शं नो भवित्रं शम्वस्तु वायुः ॥
7.35.e: May Adid through holy works be gracioas, and may the Maruts, loud in song, be friendly.  May Viṣṇu give felicity, and Pūṣan, the Air that cherisheth our life, and Vāyu.

7.35.d: शं नो देवः सविता त्रायमाणः शं नो भवन्तूषसो विभातीः । शं नः पर्जन्यो भवतु प्रजाभ्यः शं नः क्षेत्रस्य पतिरस्तु शम्भुः ॥
7.35.e: Prosper us Savitar, the God who rescues, and let the radiant Mornings be propitious.  Auspicious to all creatures be Parjanya, auspicious be the field's benign Protector.

7.35.d: शं नो देवा विश्वदेवा भवन्तु शं सरस्वती सह धीभिरस्तु । शमभिषाचः शमु रातिषाचः शं नो दिव्याः पार्थिवाः शं नो अप्याः ॥
7.35.e: May all the fellowship of Gods befriend us, Sarasvatī, with Holy Thoughts, be gracious.  Friendly be they, the Liberal Ones who seek us, yea, those who dwell in heaven, on earth, in waters.

7.35.d: शं नः सत्यस्य पतयो भवन्तु शं नो अर्वन्तः शमु सन्तु गावः । शं न ऋभवः सुकृतः सुहस्ताः शं नो भवन्तु पितरो हवेषु ॥
7.35.e: May the great Lords of Truth protect and aid us: blest to us be our horses and our cattle.  Kind be the pious skilful-handed Ṛbhus, kind be the Fathers at our invocations.

7.35.d: शं नो अज एकपाद्देवो अस्तु शं नोऽहिर्बुध्न्य१ः शं समुद्रः । शं नो अपां नपात्पेरुरस्तु शं नः पृश्निर्भवतु देवगोपा ॥
7.35.e: May Aja-Ekapād, the God, be gracious, gracious the Dragon of the Deep, and Ocean.  Gracious be he the swelling Child of Waters, gracious be Pṛśni who hath Gods to guard her.

7.35.d: आदित्या रुद्रा वसवो जुषन्तेदं ब्रह्म क्रियमाणं नवीयः । शृण्वन्तु नो दिव्याः पार्थिवासो गोजाता उत ये यज्ञियासः ॥
7.35.e: So may the Rudras, Vasus, and Ādityas accept the new hymn which we now are making.  May all the Holy Ones of earth and heaven, and the Cow's offipring hear our invocation.

7.35.d: ये देवानां यज्ञिया यज्ञियानां मनोर्यजत्रा अमृता ऋतज्ञाः । ते नो रासन्तामुरुगायमद्य यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.35.e: They who of Holy Gods are very holy, Immortal, knowing Law, whom man must worship,—  May these to-day give us broad paths to travel. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.36.d: प्र ब्रह्मैतु सदनादृतस्य वि रश्मिभिः ससृजे सूर्यो गाः । वि सानुना पृथिवी सस्र उर्वी पृथु प्रतीकमध्येधे अग्निः ॥
7.36.e: LET the prayer issue from the seat of Order, for Sūrya with his beams hath loosed the cattle.  With lofty ridges earth is far extended, and Agni's flame hath lit the spacious surface.

7.36.d: इमां वां मित्रावरुणा सुवृक्तिमिषं न कृण्वे असुरा नवीयः । इनो वामन्यः पदवीरदब्धो जनं च मित्रो यतति ब्रुवाणः ॥
7.36.e: O Asuras, O Varuṇa and Mitra, this hymn to you, like food, anew I offer.  One of you is a strong unerring Leader, and Mitra, speaking, stirreth men to labour.

7.36.d: आ वातस्य ध्रजतो रन्त इत्या अपीपयन्त धेनवो न सूदाः । महो दिवः सदने जायमानोऽचिक्रदद्वृषभः सस्मिन्नूधन् ॥
7.36.e: The movements of the gliding wind come hither: like cows, the springs are filled to overflowing.  Born in the station e’en of lofty heaven the Bull hath loudly bellowed in this region.

7.36.d: गिरा य एता युनजद्धरी त इन्द्र प्रिया सुरथा शूर धायू । प्र यो मन्युं रिरिक्षतो मिनात्या सुक्रतुमर्यमणं ववृत्याम् ॥
7.36.e: May I bring hither with my song, O Indra, wise Aryaman who yokes thy dear Bay Horses,  Voracious, with thy noble car, O Hero, him who defeats the wrath of the malicious.

7.36.d: यजन्ते अस्य सख्यं वयश्च नमस्विनः स्व ऋतस्य धामन् । वि पृक्षो बाबधे नृभिः स्तवान इदं नमो रुद्राय प्रेष्ठम् ॥
7.36.e: In their own place of sacrifice adorers worship to gain long life and win his friendship.  He hath poured food on men when they have praised him; be this, the dearest reverence, paid to Rudra.

7.36.d: आ यत्साकं यशसो वावशानाः सरस्वती सप्तथी सिन्धुमाता । याः सुष्वयन्त सुदुघाः सुधारा अभि स्वेन पयसा पीप्यानाः ॥
7.36.e: Coming together, glorious, loudly roaring - Sarasvatī, Mother of Floods, the seventh-  With copious milk, with fair streams, strongly flowing, full swelling with the volume of their water;

7.36.d: उत त्ये नो मरुतो मन्दसाना धियं तोकं च वाजिनोऽवन्तु । मा नः परि ख्यदक्षरा चरन्त्यवीवृधन्युज्यं ते रयिं नः ॥
7.36.e: And may the mighty Maruts, too, rejoicing, aid our devotion and protect our offspring.  Let not swift-moving Aksara neglect us: they have increased our own appropriate riches,

7.36.d: प्र वो महीमरमतिं कृणुध्वं प्र पूषणं विदथ्यं१ न वीरम् । भगं धियोऽवितारं नो अस्याः सातौ वाजं रातिषाचं पुरंधिम् ॥
7.36.e: Bring ye the great Aramati before you, and Pūṣan as the Hero of the synod,  Bhaga who looks upon this hymn with favour, and, as our strength, the bountiful Purandbi.

7.36.d: अच्छायं वो मरुतः श्लोक एत्वच्छा विष्णुं निषिक्तपामवोभिः । उत प्रजायै गृणते वयो धुर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.36.e: May this our song of praise reach you, O Maruts, and Viṣṇu guardian of the future infant.  May they vouchsafe the singer strength for offspring. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.37.d: आ वो वाहिष्ठो वहतु स्तवध्यै रथो वाजा ऋभुक्षणो अमृक्तः । अभि त्रिपृष्ठैः सवनेषु सोमैर्मदे सुशिप्रा महभिः पृणध्वम् ॥
7.37.e: LET your best-bearing car that must be lauded, ne’er injured, bring you Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans.  Fill you, fair-helmeted! with mighty Soma, thrice-mixed, at our libations to delight you.

7.37.d: यूयं ह रत्नं मघवत्सु धत्थ स्वर्दृश ऋभुक्षणो अमृक्तम् । सं यज्ञेषु स्वधावन्तः पिबध्वं वि नो राधांसि मतिभिर्दयध्वम् ॥
7.37.e: Ye who behold the light of heaven, Ṛbhukṣans, give our rich patrons unmolested riches.  Drink, heavenly-natured. at our sacrifices, and give us bounties for the hymns we sing you.

7.37.d: उवोचिथ हि मघवन्देष्णं महो अर्भस्य वसुनो विभागे । उभा ते पूर्णा वसुना गभस्ती न सूनृता नि यमते वसव्या ॥
7.37.e: For thou, O Bounteous One, art used to giving, at parting treasure whether small or ample.  Filled full are both thine arms with great possessions: thy goodness keeps thee not from granting riches.

7.37.d: त्वमिन्द्र स्वयशा ऋभुक्षा वाजो न साधुरस्तमेष्यृक्वा । वयं नु ते दाश्वांसः स्याम ब्रह्म कृण्वन्तो हरिवो वसिष्ठाः ॥
7.37.e: Indra, high-famed, as Vāja and Ṛbhukṣans, thou goest working, singing to the dwelling.  Lord of Bay Steeds, this day may we Vasisthas offer our prayers to thee and bring oblations.

7.37.d: सनितासि प्रवतो दाशुषे चिद्याभिर्विवेषो हर्यश्व धीभिः । ववन्मा नु ते युज्याभिरूती कदा न इन्द्र राय आ दशस्येः ॥
7.37.e: Thou winnest swift advancement for thy servant, through hymns, Lord of Bay Steeds, which thou hast favoured.  For thee with friendly succour have we battled, and when, O Indra, wilt thou grant us riches?

7.37.d: वासयसीव वेधसस्त्वं नः कदा न इन्द्र वचसो बुबोधः । अस्तं तात्या धिया रयिं सुवीरं पृक्षो नो अर्वा न्युहीत वाजी ॥
7.37.e: To us thy priests a home, as ’twere, thou givest: when, Indra wilt thou recognize our praises?  May thy strong Steed, through our ancestral worship, bring food and wealth with heroes to our dwelling.

7.37.d: अभि यं देवी निर्ऋतिश्चिदीशे नक्षन्त इन्द्रं शरदः सुपृक्षः । उप त्रिबन्धुर्जरदष्टिमेत्यस्ववेशं यं कृणवन्त मर्ताः ॥
7.37.e: Though Nirrti the Goddess reigneth round him, Autumns with food in plenty come to Indra.  With three close Friends to length of days he cometh, he whom men let not rest at home in quiet.

7.37.d: आ नो राधांसि सवितः स्तवध्या आ रायो यन्तु पर्वतस्य रातौ । सदा नो दिव्यः पायुः सिषक्तु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.37.e: Promise us gifts, O Savitar: may riches come unto us in Parvata's full bounty.  May the Celestial Guardian still attend us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.38.d: उदु ष्य देवः सविता ययाम हिरण्ययीममतिं यामशिश्रेत् । नूनं भगो हव्यो मानुषेभिर्वि यो रत्ना पुरूवसुर्दधाति ॥
7.38.e: ON high hath Savitar, this God, extended the golden lustre which he spreads around him.  Now, now must Bhaga be invoked by mortals, Lord of great riches who distributes treasures.

7.38.d: उदु तिष्ठ सवितः श्रुध्य१स्य हिरण्यपाणे प्रभृतावृतस्य । व्यु१र्वीं पृथ्वीममतिं सृजान आ नृभ्यो मर्तभोजनं सुवानः ॥
7.38.e: Rise up, O Savitar whose hands are golden, and hear this man while sacrifice is offered,  Spreading afar thy broad and wide effulgence, and bringing mortal men the food that feeds them.

7.38.d: अपि ष्टुतः सविता देवो अस्तु यमा चिद्विश्वे वसवो गृणन्ति । स नः स्तोमान्नमस्य१श्चनो धाद्विश्वेभिः पातु पायुभिर्नि सूरीन् ॥
7.38.e: Let Savitar the God he hymned with praises, to whom the Vasus, even, all sing glory.  Sweet be our lauds to him whose due is worship: may he with all protection guard our princes.

7.38.d: अभि यं देव्यदितिर्गृणाति सवं देवस्य सवितुर्जुषाणा । अभि सम्राजो वरुणो गृणन्त्यभि मित्रासो अर्यमा सजोषाः ॥
7.38.e: Even he whom Aditi the Goddess praises, rejoicing in God Savitar's incitement:  Even he who praise the high imperial Rulers, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, sing in concert.

7.38.d: अभि ये मिथो वनुषः सपन्ते रातिं दिवो रातिषाचः पृथिव्याः । अहिर्बुध्न्य उत नः शृणोतु वरूत्र्येकधेनुभिर्नि पातु ॥
7.38.e: They who come emulous to our oblation, dispensing bounty, from the earth and heaven.  May they and Ahibudhnya hear our calling: guard us Varūtrī with the Ekadhenus.

7.38.d: अनु तन्नो जास्पतिर्मंसीष्ट रत्नं देवस्य सवितुरियानः । भगमुग्रोऽवसे जोहवीति भगमनुग्रो अध याति रत्नम् ॥
7.38.e: This may the Lord of Life, entreated, grant us,—the wealth which Savitar the God possesses.  The mighty calls on Bhaga for protection, on Bhaga calls the weak to give him riches.

7.38.d: शं नो भवन्तु वाजिनो हवेषु देवताता मितद्रवः स्वर्काः । जम्भयन्तोऽहिं वृकं रक्षांसि सनेम्यस्मद्युयवन्नमीवाः ॥
7.38.e: Bless us the Vajins when we call, while slowly they move, strong Singers, to the Gods’ assembly.  Crushing the wolf, the serpent, and the demons, may they completely banish all affliction.

7.38.d: वाजेवाजेऽवत वाजिनो नो धनेषु विप्रा अमृता ऋतज्ञाः । अस्य मध्वः पिबत मादयध्वं तृप्ता यात पथिभिर्देवयानैः ॥
7.38.e: Deep-skilled in Law eternal, deathless, Singers, O Vajins, help us in each fray for booty.  Drink of this meath, he satisfied, be joyful: then go on paths which Gods are wont to travel.

7.39.d: ऊर्ध्वो अग्निः सुमतिं वस्वो अश्रेत्प्रतीची जूर्णिर्देवतातिमेति । भेजाते अद्री रथ्येव पन्थामृतं होता न इषितो यजाति ॥
7.39.e: AGNI, erect, hath shown enriching favour: the flame goes forward to the Gods’ assembly.  Like car-borne men the stones their path have chosen: let the priest, quickened, celebrate our worship.

7.39.d: प्र वावृजे सुप्रया बर्हिरेषामा विश्पतीव बीरिट इयाते । विशामक्तोरुषसः पूर्वहूतौ वायुः पूषा स्वस्तये नियुत्वान् ॥
7.39.e: Soft to the tread, their sacred grass is scattered: these go like Kings amid the band around them,  At the folks early call on Night and Morning,—Vāyu, and Pūṣan with his team, to bless us.

7.39.d: ज्मया अत्र वसवो रन्त देवा उरावन्तरिक्षे मर्जयन्त शुभ्राः । अर्वाक्पथ उरुज्रयः कृणुध्वं श्रोता दूतस्य जग्मुषो नो अस्य ॥
7.39.e: Here on their path the noble Gods proceeded: in the wide firmament the Beauteous decked them.  Bend your way hither, ye who travel widely: hear this our envoy who hath gone to meet you.

7.39.d: ते हि यज्ञेषु यज्ञियास ऊमाः सधस्थं विश्वे अभि सन्ति देवाः । ताँ अध्वर उशतो यक्ष्यग्ने श्रुष्टी भगं नासत्या पुरंधिम् ॥
7.39.e: For they are holy aids at sacrifices: all Gods approach the place of congregation.  Bring these, desirous, to our worship, Agni, swift the Nisatyas, Bhaga, and Purandhi.

7.39.d: आग्ने गिरो दिव आ पृथिव्या मित्रं वह वरुणमिन्द्रमग्निम् । आर्यमणमदितिं विष्णुमेषां सरस्वती मरुतो मादयन्ताम् ॥
7.39.e: Agni, to these men's hymns, from earth, from heaven, bring Mitra, Varuṇa, Indra, and Agni,  And Aryaman, and Aditi, and Viṣṇu. Sarasvatī be joyful, and the Maruts.

7.39.d: ररे हव्यं मतिभिर्यज्ञियानां नक्षत्कामं मर्त्यानामसिन्वन् । धाता रयिमविदस्यं सदासां सक्षीमहि युज्येभिर्नु देवैः ॥
7.39.e: Even as the holy wish, the gift is offered: may he, unsated, come when men desire him.  Give never-failing ever-conquering riches: with Gods for our allies may we be victors.

7.39.d: नू रोदसी अभिष्टुते वसिष्ठैर्ऋतावानो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निः । यच्छन्तु चन्द्रा उपमं नो अर्कं यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.39.e: Now have both worlds been praised by the Vasisthas; and holy Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.  May they, bright Deities, make our song supremest. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.40.d: ओ श्रुष्टिर्विदथ्या३ समेतु प्रति स्तोमं दधीमहि तुराणाम् । यदद्य देवः सविता सुवाति स्यामास्य रत्निनो विभागे ॥
7.40.e: BE gathered all the audience of the synod: let us begin their praise whose course is rapid.  Whate’er God Savitar this day produces, may we be where the Wealthy One distributes.

7.40.d: मित्रस्तन्नो वरुणो रोदसी च द्युभक्तमिन्द्रो अर्यमा ददातु । दिदेष्टु देव्यदिती रेक्णो वायुश्च यन्नियुवैते भगश्च ॥
7.40.e: This, dealt from heaven ' may both the Worlds vouchsafe us, and Varuṇa, Indra, Aryaman, and Mitra.  May Goddess Aditi assign us riches, Vāyu and Bhaga make them ours for ever.

7.40.d: सेदुग्रो अस्तु मरुतः स शुष्मी यं मर्त्यं पृषदश्वा अवाथ । उतेमग्निः सरस्वती जुनन्ति न तस्य रायः पर्येतास्ति ॥
7.40.e: Strong be the man and full of power, O Maruts, whom ye, borne on by spotted coursers, favour.  Him, too, Sarasvatī and Agni further, and there is none to rob him of his riches.

7.40.d: अयं हि नेता वरुण ऋतस्य मित्रो राजानो अर्यमापो धुः । सुहवा देव्यदितिरनर्वा ते नो अंहो अति पर्षन्नरिष्टान् ॥
7.40.e: This Varuṇa is guide of Law, he, Mitra, and Aryaman, the Kings, our work have finished.  Divine and foeless Aditi quickly listens. May these deliver us unharmed from trouble.

7.40.d: अस्य देवस्य मीळ्हुषो वया विष्णोरेषस्य प्रभृथे हविर्भिः । विदे हि रुद्रो रुद्रियं महित्वं यासिष्टं वर्तिरश्विनाविरावत् ॥
7.40.e: With offerings I propitiate the branches of this swift-moving God, the bounteous Viṣṇu.  Hence Rudra gained his Rudra-strength: O Aśvins, ye sought the house that hath celestial viands.

7.40.d: मात्र पूषन्नाघृण इरस्यो वरूत्री यद्रातिषाचश्च रासन् । मयोभुवो नो अर्वन्तो नि पान्तु वृष्टिं परिज्मा वातो ददातु ॥
7.40.e: Be not thou angry here, O glowing Pūṣan, for what Varūtrī and the Bounteous gave us.  May the swift-moving Gods protect and bless us, and Vāta send us rain, wha wanders round us.

7.40.d: नू रोदसी अभिष्टुते वसिष्ठैर्ऋतावानो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निः । यच्छन्तु चन्द्रा उपमं नो अर्कं यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.40.e: Now have both worlds been praised by the Vasisthas, and holy Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.  May they, bright Deities, make our song supremest. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.41.d: प्रातरग्निं प्रातरिन्द्रं हवामहे प्रातर्मित्रावरुणा प्रातरश्विना । प्रातर्भगं पूषणं ब्रह्मणस्पतिं प्रातः सोममुत रुद्रं हुवेम ॥
7.41.e: AGNI at dawn, and Indra we invoke at dawn, and Varuṇa and Mitra, and the Aśvins twain.  Bhaga at dawn, Pūṣan, and Brahmaṇaspati, Soma at dawn, Rudra we will invoke at dawn.

7.41.d: प्रातर्जितं भगमुग्रं हुवेम वयं पुत्रमदितेर्यो विधर्ता । आध्रश्चिद्यं मन्यमानस्तुरश्चिद्राजा चिद्यं भगं भक्षीत्याह ॥
7.41.e: We will invoke strong, early-conquering Bhaga, the Son of Aditi, the great supporter:  Thinking of whom, the poor, yea, even the mighty, even the King himself says, Give me Bhaga.

7.41.d: भग प्रणेतर्भग सत्यराधो भगेमां धियमुदवा ददन्नः । भग प्र णो जनय गोभिरश्वैर्भग प्र नृभिर्नृवन्तः स्याम ॥
7.41.e: Bhaga our guide, Bhaga whose gifts are faithful, favour this song, and give us wealth, O Bhaga.  Bhaga, augment our store of kine and horses, Bhaga, may we be rich in men and heroes.

7.41.d: उतेदानीं भगवन्तः स्यामोत प्रपित्व उत मध्ये अह्नाम् । उतोदिता मघवन्त्सूर्यस्य वयं देवानां सुमतौ स्याम ॥
7.41.e: So may felicity be ours at present, and when the day approaches, and at noontide;  And may we still, O Bounteous One, at sunset be happy in the Deities' loving-kindness.

7.41.d: भग एव भगवाँ अस्तु देवास्तेन वयं भगवन्तः स्याम । तं त्वा भग सर्व इज्जोहवीति स नो भग पुरएता भवेह ॥
7.41.e: May Bhaga verily be bliss-bestower, and through him, Gods! may happiness attend us.  As such, O Bhaga, all with might invoke thee: as such be thou our Champion here, O Bhaga.

7.41.d: समध्वरायोषसो नमन्त दधिक्रावेव शुचये पदाय । अर्वाचीनं वसुविदं भगं नो रथमिवाश्वा वाजिन आ वहन्तु ॥
7.41.e: To this our worship may all Dawns incline them, and come to the pure place like Dadhikrāvan.  As strong steeds draw a chariot may they bring us hitherward Bhaga who discovers treasure.

7.41.d: अश्वावतीर्गोमतीर्न उषासो वीरवतीः सदमुच्छन्तु भद्राः । घृतं दुहाना विश्वतः प्रपीता यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.41.e: May blessed Mornings dawn on us for ever, with wealth of kine, of horses, and of heroes,  Streaming with all abundance, pouring fatness. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.42.d: प्र ब्रह्माणो अङ्गिरसो नक्षन्त प्र क्रन्दनुर्नभन्यस्य वेतु । प्र धेनव उदप्रुतो नवन्त युज्यातामद्री अध्वरस्य पेशः ॥
7.42.e: LET Brahmans and Aṅgirases come forward, and let the roar of cloudy heaven surround us.  Loud low the Milch-kine swimming in the waters: set be the stones that grace our holy service.

7.42.d: सुगस्ते अग्ने सनवित्तो अध्वा युक्ष्वा सुते हरितो रोहितश्च । ये वा सद्मन्नरुषा वीरवाहो हुवे देवानां जनिमानि सत्तः ॥
7.42.e: Fair, Agni, is thy long-known path to travel: yoke for the juice tfiy bay, thy ruddy horses,  Or red steeds, Hero-bearing, for the chamber. Seated, I call the Deities' generations.

7.42.d: समु वो यज्ञं महयन्नमोभिः प्र होता मन्द्रो रिरिच उपाके । यजस्व सु पुर्वणीक देवाना यज्ञियामरमतिं ववृत्याः ॥
7.42.e: They glorify your sacrifice with worship, yet the glad Priest near them is left unequalled.  Bring the Gods hither, thou of many aspects: turn hitherward Aramati the Holy.

7.42.d: यदा वीरस्य रेवतो दुरोणे स्योनशीरतिथिराचिकेतत् । सुप्रीतो अग्निः सुधितो दम आ स विशे दाति वार्यमियत्यै ॥
7.42.e: What time the Guest hath made himself apparent, at ease reclining in the rich man's dwelling,  Agni, well-pleased, well-placed within the chamber gives to a house like this wealth worth the choosing.

7.42.d: इमं नो अग्ने अध्वरं जुषस्व मरुत्स्विन्द्रे यशसं कृधी नः । आ नक्ता बर्हिः सदतामुषासोशन्ता मित्रावरुणा यजेह ॥
7.42.e: Accept this sacrifice of ours, O Agni; glorify it with Indra and the Maruts.  Here on our grass let Night and Dawn be seated: bring longing Varuṇa and Mitra hither.

7.42.d: एवाग्निं सहस्यं१ वसिष्ठो रायस्कामो विश्वप्स्न्यस्य स्तौत् । इषं रयिं पप्रथद्वाजमस्मे यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.42.e: Thus hath Vasiṣṭha praised victorious Agni, yearning for wealth that giveth all subsistence.  May he bestow on us food, strength, and riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.43.d: प्र वो यज्ञेषु देवयन्तो अर्चन्द्यावा नमोभिः पृथिवी इषध्यै । येषां ब्रह्माण्यसमानि विप्रा विष्वग्वियन्ति वनिनो न शाखाः ॥
7.43.e: SING out the pious at your sacrifices to move with adorations Earth and Heaven-  The Holy Singers, whose unmatched devotions, like a tree's branches, part in all directions.

7.43.d: प्र यज्ञ एतु हेत्वो न सप्तिरुद्यच्छध्वं समनसो घृताचीः । स्तृणीत बर्हिरध्वराय साधूर्ध्वा शोचींषि देवयून्यस्थुः ॥
7.43.e: Let sacrifice proceed like some fleet courser: with one accord lift ye on high the ladles.  Strew sacred grass meet for the solenm service: bright flames that love the Gods have mounted upward.

7.43.d: आ पुत्रासो न मातरं विभृत्राः सानौ देवासो बर्हिषः सदन्तु । आ विश्वाची विदथ्यामनक्त्वग्ने मा नो देवताता मृधस्कः ॥
7.43.e: Like babes in arms reposing on their mother, let the Gods sit upon the grass's summit.  Let general fire make bright the flame of worship: scorn us not, Agni, in the Gods’ assembly.

7.43.d: ते सीषपन्त जोषमा यजत्रा ऋतस्य धाराः सुदुघा दुहानाः । ज्येष्ठं वो अद्य मह आ वसूनामा गन्तन समनसो यति ष्ठ ॥
7.43.e: Gladly the Gods have let themselves be honoured, milking the copious streams of holy Order.  The highest might to-day is yours, the Vasits': come ye, as many as ye are, one-minded.

7.43.d: एवा नो अग्ने विक्ष्वा दशस्य त्वया वयं सहसावन्नास्क्राः । राया युजा सधमादो अरिष्टा यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.43.e: So, Agni, send us wealth among the people: may we be closely knit to thee, O Victor,  Unharmed, and rich, and taking joy together. Preserve us evermore, ye ods, with blessings.

7.44.d: दधिक्रां वः प्रथममश्विनोषसमग्निं समिद्धं भगमूतये हुवे । इन्द्रं विष्णुं पूषणं ब्रह्मणस्पतिमादित्यान्द्यावापृथिवी अपः स्वः ॥
7.44.e: I CALL on Dadhikrās, the first, to give you aid, the Aśvins, Bhaga, Dawn, and Agni kindled well,  Indra, and Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Light.

7.44.d: दधिक्रामु नमसा बोधयन्त उदीराणा यज्ञमुपप्रयन्तः । इळां देवीं बर्हिषि सादयन्तोऽश्विना विप्रा सुहवा हुवेम ॥
7.44.e: When, rising, to the sacrifice we hasten, awaking Dadhikrās with adorations.  Seating on sacred grass the Goddess Iḷā. let us invoke the sage swift-hearing Aśvins.

7.44.d: दधिक्रावाणं बुबुधानो अग्निमुप ब्रुव उषसं सूर्यं गाम् । ब्रध्नं मँश्चतोर्वरुणस्य बभ्रुं ते विश्वास्मद्दुरिता यावयन्तु ॥
7.44.e: While I am thus arousing Dadhikrāvan I speak to Agni, Earth, and Dawn, and Sūrya,  The red, the brown of Varuṇa ever mindful: may they ward off from us all grief and trouble.

7.44.d: दधिक्रावा प्रथमो वाज्यर्वाग्रे रथानां भवति प्रजानन् । संविदान उषसा सूर्येणादित्येभिर्वसुभिरङ्गिरोभिः ॥
7.44.e: Foremost is Dadhikrāvan, vigorous courser; in forefront of the cars, his way he knoweth,  Closely allied with Sūrya and with Morning, Ādityas, and Aṅgirases, and Vasus.

7.44.d: आ नो दधिक्राः पथ्यामनक्त्वृतस्य पन्थामन्वेतवा उ । शृणोतु नो दैव्यं शर्धो अग्निः शृण्वन्तु विश्वे महिषा अमूराः ॥
7.44.e: May Dadhikrās prepare the way we travel that we may pass along the path of Order.  May Agni bear us, and the Heavenly Army: hear us all Mighty Ones whom none deceiveth.

7.45.d: आ देवो यातु सविता सुरत्नोऽन्तरिक्षप्रा वहमानो अश्वैः । हस्ते दधानो नर्या पुरूणि निवेशयञ्च प्रसुवञ्च भूम ॥
7.45.e: MAY the God Savitar, rich in goodly treasures, filling the region, borne by steeds, come hither,  In his hand holding much that makes men happy, lulling to slumber and arousing creatures.

7.45.d: उदस्य बाहू शिथिरा बृहन्ता हिरण्यया दिवो अन्ताँ अनष्टाम् । नूनं सो अस्य महिमा पनिष्ट सूरश्चिदस्मा अनु दादपस्याम् ॥
7.45.e: Golden, sublime, and easy in their motion, his arms extend unto the bounds of heaven.  Now shall that mightiness of his he lauded: even Sūrya yields to him in active vigour.

7.45.d: स घा नो देवः सविता सहावा साविषद्वसुपतिर्वसूनि । विश्रयमाणो अमतिमुरूचीं मर्तभोजनमध रासते नः ॥
7.45.e: May this God Savitar, the Strong and Mighty, the Lord of precious wealth, vouchsafe us treasures.  May he, advancing his far-spreading lustre, bestow on us the food that feedeth mortals.

7.45.d: इमा गिरः सवितारं सुजिह्वं पूर्णगभस्तिमीळते सुपाणिम् । चित्रं वयो बृहदस्मे दधातु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.45.e: These songs praise Savitar whose tongue is pleasant, praise him whose arms are full, whose hands are lovely.  High vital strength, and manifold, may he grant us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.46.d: इमा रुद्राय स्थिरधन्वने गिरः क्षिप्रेषवे देवाय स्वधाव्ने । अषाळ्हाय सहमानाय वेधसे तिग्मायुधाय भरता शृणोतु नः ॥
7.46.e: To Rudra bring these songs, whose bow is firm and strong, the self-dependent God with swiftly-flying shafts,  The Wise, the Conqueror whom none may overcome, armed with sharp-pointed weapons: may he hear our call.

7.46.d: स हि क्षयेण क्षम्यस्य जन्मनः साम्राज्येन दिव्यस्य चेतति । अवन्नवन्तीरुप नो दुरश्चरानमीवो रुद्र जासु नो भव ॥
7.46.e: He through his lordship thinks on beings of the earth, on heavenly beings through his high imperial sway.  Come willingly to our doors that gladly welcome thee, and heal all sickness, Rudra., in our families.

7.46.d: या ते दिद्युदवसृष्टा दिवस्परि क्ष्मया चरति परि सा वृणक्तु नः । सहस्रं ते स्वपिवात भेषजा मा नस्तोकेषु तनयेषु रीरिषः ॥
7.46.e: May thy bright arrow which, shot down by thee from heaven, flieth upon the earth, pass us uninjured by.  Thou, very gracious God, hast thousand medicines: inflict no evil on our sons or progeny.

7.46.d: मा नो वधी रुद्र मा परा दा मा ते भूम प्रसितौ हीळितस्य । आ नो भज बर्हिषि जीवशंसे यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.46.e: Slay us not, nor abandon us, O Rudra let not thy noose, when thou art angry, seize us.  Give us trimmed grass and fame among the living. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.47.d: आपो यं वः प्रथमं देवयन्त इन्द्रपानमूर्मिमकृण्वतेळः । तं वो वयं शुचिमरिप्रमद्य घृतप्रुषं मधुमन्तं वनेम ॥
7.47.e: MAY we obtain this day from you, O Waters, that wave of pure refreshment, which the pious  Made erst the special beverage of Indra, bright, stainless, rich in sweets and dropping fatness.

7.47.d: तमूर्मिमापो मधुमत्तमं वोऽपां नपादवत्वाशुहेमा । यस्मिन्निन्द्रो वसुभिर्मादयाते तमश्याम देवयन्तो वो अद्य ॥
7.47.e: May the Floods' Offspring, he whose course is rapid, protect that wave most rich in sweets, O Waters,  That shall make Indra and the Vasus joyful. This may we gain from you to-day, we pious.

7.47.d: शतपवित्राः स्वधया मदन्तीर्देवीर्देवानामपि यन्ति पाथः । ता इन्द्रस्य न मिनन्ति व्रतानि सिन्धुभ्यो हव्यं घृतवज्जुहोत ॥
7.47.e: All-purifying, joying in their nature, to paths of Gods the Goddesses move onward.  They never violate the laws of Indra. Present the oil-rich offering to the Rivers.

7.47.d: याः सूर्यो रश्मिभिराततान याभ्य इन्द्रो अरदद्गातुमूर्मिम् । ते सिन्धवो वरिवो धातना नो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.47.e: Whom Sūrya with his bright beams hath attracted, and Indra dug the path for them to travel,  May these Streams give us ample room and freedom. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.48.d: ऋभुक्षणो वाजा मादयध्वमस्मे नरो मघवानः सुतस्य । आ वोऽर्वाचः क्रतवो न यातां विभ्वो रथं नर्यं वर्तयन्तु ॥
7.48.e: YE liberal Heroes, Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans, come and delight you with our flowing Soma.  May your strength, Vibhus, as ye come to meet us, turn hitherward your car that brings men profit.

7.48.d: ऋभुर्ऋभुभिरभि वः स्याम विभ्वो विभुभिः शवसा शवांसि । वाजो अस्माँ अवतु वाजसाताविन्द्रेण युजा तरुषेम वृत्रम् ॥
7.48.e: May we as Ṛbhu with your Ṛbhus conquer strength with our strength, as Vibhus with the Vibhus.  May Vāja aid us in the fight for booty, and helped by Indra may we quell the foeman.

7.48.d: ते चिद्धि पूर्वीरभि सन्ति शासा विश्वाँ अर्य उपरताति वन्वन् । इन्द्रो विभ्वाँ ऋभुक्षा वाजो अर्यः शत्रोर्मिथत्या कृणवन्वि नृम्णम् ॥
7.48.e: For they rule many tribes with high dominion, and conquer all their foes in close encounter.  May Indra, Vibhvan, Vāja, and Ṛbhukṣan destroy by turns the wicked foeman's valour.

7.48.d: नू देवासो वरिवः कर्तना नो भूत नो विश्वेऽवसे सजोषाः । समस्मे इषं वसवो ददीरन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.48.e: Now, Deities, give us ample room and freedom: be all of you, one-minded, our protection.  So let the Vasus grant us strength and vigour. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.49.d: समुद्रज्येष्ठाः सलिलस्य मध्यात्पुनाना यन्त्यनिविशमानाः । इन्द्रो या वज्री वृषभो रराद ता आपो देवीरिह मामवन्तु ॥
7.49.e: FORTH from the middle of the flood the Waters-their chief the Sea-flow cleansing, never sleeping.  Indra, the Bull, the Thunderer, dug their channels: here let those Waters, Goddesses, protect me.

7.49.d: या आपो दिव्या उत वा स्रवन्ति खनित्रिमा उत वा याः स्वयंजाः । समुद्रार्था याः शुचयः पावकास्ता आपो देवीरिह मामवन्तु ॥
7.49.e: Waters which come from heaven, or those that wander dug from the earth, or flowing free by nature,  Bright, purifying, speeding to the Ocean, here let those Waters. Goddesses, protect me.

7.49.d: यासां राजा वरुणो याति मध्ये सत्यानृते अवपश्यञ्जनानाम् । मधुश्चुतः शुचयो याः पावकास्ता आपो देवीरिह मामवन्तु ॥
7.49.e: Those amid whom goes Varuṇa the Sovran, he who discriminates men's truth and falsehood-  Distilling meath, the bright, the purifying, here let those Waters, Goddesses, protect me.

7.49.d: यासु राजा वरुणो यासु सोमो विश्वे देवा यासूर्जं मदन्ति । वैश्वानरो यास्वग्निः प्रविष्टस्ता आपो देवीरिह मामवन्तु ॥
7.49.e: They from whom Varuṇa the King, and Soma, and all the Deities drink strength and vigour,  They into whom Vaiśvānara Agni entered, here let those Waters, Goddesses, protect Me.

7.50.d: आ मां मित्रावरुणेह रक्षतं कुलाययद्विश्वयन्मा न आ गन् । अजकावं दुर्दृशीकं तिरो दधे मा मां पद्येन रपसा विदत्त्सरुः ॥
7.50.e: O MITRA-VARUNA, guard and protect me here: let not that come to me which nests within and swells.  I drive afar the scorpion hateful to the sight: let not the winding worm touch me and wound my foot.

7.50.d: यद्विजामन्परुषि वन्दनं भुवदष्ठीवन्तौ परि कुल्फौ च देहत् । अग्निष्टच्छोचन्नप बाधतामितो मा मां पद्येन रपसा विदत्त्सरुः ॥
7.50.e: Eruption that appears upon the twofold joints, and that which overspreads the ankles and the knees,  May the refulgent Agni banish far away let not the winding worm touch me and wound my foot.

7.50.d: यच्छल्मलौ भवति यन्नदीषु यदोषधीभ्यः परि जायते विषम् । विश्वे देवा निरितस्तत्सुवन्तु मा मां पद्येन रपसा विदत्त्सरुः ॥
7.50.e: The poison that is formed upon the Salmali, that which is found in streams, that which the plants produce,  All this may all the Gods banish and drive away: let not the winding worm touch me and wound my foot.

7.50.d: याः प्रवतो निवत उद्वत उदन्वतीरनुदकाश्च याः । ता अस्मभ्यं पयसा पिन्वमानाः शिवा देवीरशिपदा भवन्तु सर्वा नद्यो अशिमिदा भवन्तु ॥
7.50.e: The steep declivities, the valleys, and the heights, the channels full of water, and the waterless-  May those who swell with water, gracious Goddesses, never afflict us with the Sipada disease, may all the rivers keep us free from Simida.

7.51.d: आदित्यानामवसा नूतनेन सक्षीमहि शर्मणा शंतमेन । अनागास्त्वे अदितित्वे तुरास इमं यज्ञं दधतु श्रोषमाणाः ॥
7.51.e: THROUGH the Ādityas’ most auspicious shelter, through their most recent succour may we conquer.  May they, the Mighty, giving ear, establish this sacrifice, to make us free and sinless.

7.51.d: आदित्यासो अदितिर्मादयन्तां मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणो रजिष्ठाः । अस्माकं सन्तु भुवनस्य गोपाः पिबन्तु सोममवसे नो अद्य ॥
7.51.e: Let Aditi rejoice and the Ādityas, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, most righteous.  May they, the Guardians of the world, protect us, and, to show favour, drink this day our Soma.

7.51.d: आदित्या विश्वे मरुतश्च विश्वे देवाश्च विश्व ऋभवश्च विश्वे । इन्द्रो अग्निरश्विना तुष्टुवाना यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.51.e: All Universal Deities, the Maruts, all the Ādityas, yea, and all the Ṛbhus,  Indra, and Agni, and the Aśvins, lauded. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.52.d: आदित्यासो अदितयः स्याम पूर्देवत्रा वसवो मर्त्यत्रा । सनेम मित्रावरुणा सनन्तो भवेम द्यावापृथिवी भवन्तः ॥
7.52.e: MAY we be free from every bond, Ādityas! a castle among Gods and men, ye Vasus.  Winning, may we win Varuṇa and Mitra, and, being, may we be, O Earth and Heaven.

7.52.d: मित्रस्तन्नो वरुणो मामहन्त शर्म तोकाय तनयाय गोपाः । मा वो भुजेमान्यजातमेनो मा तत्कर्म वसवो यच्चयध्वे ॥
7.52.e: May Varuṇa and Mitra grant this blessing, our Guardians, shelter to our seed and offspring.  Let us not suffer for another's trespass. nor do the thing that ye, O Vasus, punish.

7.52.d: तुरण्यवोऽङ्गिरसो नक्षन्त रत्नं देवस्य सवितुरियानाः । पिता च तन्नो महान्यजत्रो विश्वे देवाः समनसो जुषन्त ॥
7.52.e: The ever-prompt Aṅgirases, imploring riches from Savitar the God, obtained them.  So may our Father who is great and holy, and all the Gods, accordant, grant this favour.

7.53.d: प्र द्यावा यज्ञैः पृथिवी नमोभिः सबाध ईळे बृहती यजत्रे । ते चिद्धि पूर्वे कवयो गृणन्तः पुरो मही दधिरे देवपुत्रे ॥
7.53.e: AS priest with solemn rites and adorations I worship Heaven and Earth, the High and Holy.  To them, great Parents of the Gods, have sages of ancient time, singing, assigned precedence.

7.53.d: प्र पूर्वजे पितरा नव्यसीभिर्गीर्भिः कृणुध्वं सदने ऋतस्य । आ नो द्यावापृथिवी दैव्येन जनेन यातं महि वां वरूथम् ॥
7.53.e: With newest hymns set in the seat of Order, those the Two Parents, born before all others,  Come, Heaven and Earth, with the Celestial People, hither to us, for strong is your protection.

7.53.d: उतो हि वां रत्नधेयानि सन्ति पुरूणि द्यावापृथिवी सुदासे । अस्मे धत्तं यदसदस्कृधोयु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.53.e: Yea, Heaven and Earth, ye hold in your possession full many a treasure for the liberal giver.  Grant us that wealth which comes in free abundance. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.54.d: वास्तोष्पते प्रति जानीह्यस्मान्त्स्वावेशो अनमीवो भवा नः । यत्त्वेमहे प्रति तन्नो जुषस्व शं नो भव द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे ॥
7.54.e: ACKNOWLEDGE us, O Guardian of the Homestead: bring no disease, and give us happy entrance.  Whate’er we ask of thee, be pleased to grant it, and prosper thou quadrupeds and bipeds.

7.54.d: वास्तोष्पते प्रतरणो न एधि गयस्फानो गोभिरश्वेभिरिन्दो । अजरासस्ते सख्ये स्याम पितेव पुत्रान्प्रति नो जुषस्व ॥
7.54.e: Protector of the Home, be our promoter: increase our wealth in kine and steeds, O Indu.  May we be ever-youthful in thy friendship: be pleased in us as in his sons a father.

7.54.d: वास्तोष्पते शग्मया संसदा ते सक्षीमहि रण्वया गातुमत्या । पाहि क्षेम उत योगे वरं नो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.54.e: Through thy dear fellowship that bringeth welfare, may we be victors, Guardian of the Dwelling!  Protect our happiness in rest and labour. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.55.d: अमीवहा वास्तोष्पते विश्वा रूपाण्याविशन् । सखा सुशेव एधि नः ॥
7.55.e: VASTOSPATI, who killest all disease and wearest every form,  Be an auspicious Friend to us.

7.55.d: यदर्जुन सारमेय दतः पिशङ्ग यच्छसे । वीव भ्राजन्त ऋष्टय उप स्रक्वेषु बप्सतो नि षु स्वप ॥
7.55.e: When, O bright Son of Saramā, thou showest, tawny-hued! thy teeth,  They gleam like lances' points within thy mouth when thou wouldst bite; go thou to steep.

7.55.d: स्तेनं राय सारमेय तस्करं वा पुनःसर । स्तोतॄनिन्द्रस्य रायसि किमस्मान्दुच्छुनायसे नि षु स्वप ॥
7.55.e: Saramā's Son, retrace thy way: bark at the robber and the thief.  At Indra's singers barkest thou? Why dust thou seek to terrify us? Go to sleep.

7.55.d: त्वं सूकरस्य दर्दृहि तव दर्दर्तु सूकरः । स्तोतॄनिन्द्रस्य रायसि किमस्मान्दुच्छुनायसे नि षु स्वप ॥
7.55.e: Be on thy guard against the boar, and let the boar beware of thee.  At Indra's singers barkest thou? Why dost thou seek to terrify us? Go to sleep.

7.55.d: सस्तु माता सस्तु पिता सस्तु श्वा सस्तु विश्पतिः । ससन्तु सर्वे ज्ञातयः सस्त्वयमभितो जनः ॥
7.55.e: Sleep mother, let the father sleep, sleep dog and master of the house.  Let all the kinsmen sleep, sleep all the people who are round about.

7.55.d: य आस्ते यश्च चरति यश्च पश्यति नो जनः । तेषां सं हन्मो अक्षाणि यथेदं हर्म्यं तथा ॥
7.55.e: The man who sits, the man who walks, and whosoever looks on us,  Of these we closely shut the eyes, even as we closely shut this house.

7.55.d: सहस्रशृङ्गो वृषभो यः समुद्रादुदाचरत् । तेना सहस्येना वयं नि जनान्त्स्वापयामसि ॥
7.55.e: The Bull who hath a thousand horns, who rises up from out the sea,—  By him the Strong and Mighty One we lull and make the people sleep.

7.55.d: प्रोष्ठेशया वह्येशया नारीर्यास्तल्पशीवरीः । स्त्रियो याः पुण्यगन्धास्ताः सर्वाः स्वापयामसि ॥
7.55.e: The women sleeping in the court, lying without, or stretched on beds,  The matrons with their odorous sweetsthese, one and all, we lull to sleep.

7.56.d: क ईं व्यक्ता नरः सनीळा रुद्रस्य मर्या अध स्वश्वाः ॥
7.56.e: Wno are these radiant men in serried rank, Rudra's young heroes borne by noble steeds?

7.56.d: नकिर्ह्येषां जनूंषि वेद ते अङ्ग विद्रे मिथो जनित्रम् ॥
7.56.e: Verily no one knoweth whence they sprang: they, and they only, know each other's birth.

7.56.d: अभि स्वपूभिर्मिथो वपन्त वातस्वनसः श्येना अस्पृध्रन् ॥
7.56.e: They strew each other with their blasts, these Hawks: they strove together, roaring like the wind.

7.56.d: एतानि धीरो निण्या चिकेत पृश्निर्यदूधो मही जभार ॥
7.56.e: A sage was he who knew these mysteries, what in her udder mighty Pṛśni bore.

7.56.d: सा विट् सुवीरा मरुद्भिरस्तु सनात्सहन्ती पुष्यन्ती नृम्णम् ॥
7.56.e: Ever victorious, through the Maruts, be this band of Heroes, nursing manly strength,

7.56.d: यामं येष्ठाः शुभा शोभिष्ठाः श्रिया सम्मिश्ला ओजोभिरुग्राः ॥
7.56.e: Most bright in splendour, flectest on their way, close-knit to glory, strong with varied power.

7.56.d: उग्रं व ओजः स्थिरा शवांस्यधा मरुद्भिर्गणस्तुविष्मान् ॥
7.56.e: Yea, mighty is your power and firm your strength: so, potent, with the Maruts, be the band.

7.56.d: शुभ्रो वः शुष्मः क्रुध्मी मनांसि धुनिर्मुनिरिव शर्धस्य धृष्णोः ॥
7.56.e: Bright is your spirit, wrathful are your minds: your bold troop's minstrel is like one inspired.

7.56.d: सनेम्यस्मद्युयोत दिद्युं मा वो दुर्मतिरिह प्रणङ्नः ॥
7.56.e: Ever avert your blazing shaft from us, and let not your displeasure reach us here

7.56.d: प्रिया वो नाम हुवे तुराणामा यत्तृपन्मरुतो वावशानाः ॥
7.56.e: Your dear names, conquering Maruts, we invoke, calling aloud till we are satisfied.

7.56.d: स्वायुधास इष्मिणः सुनिष्का उत स्वयं तन्व१ः शुम्भमानाः ॥
7.56.e: Well-armed, impetuous in their haste, they deck themselves, their forms, with oblations: to you, the pure, ornaments made of gold.

7.56.d: शुची वो हव्या मरुतः शुचीनां शुचिं हिनोम्यध्वरं शुचिभ्यः । ऋतेन सत्यमृतसाप आयञ्छुचिजन्मानः शुचयः पावकाः ॥
7.56.e: Pure, Maruts, pure yourselves, are your oblations: to you, the pure, pure sacrifice I offer.  By Law they came to truth, the Law's observers, bright by their birth, and pure, and sanctifying.

7.56.d: अंसेष्वा मरुतः खादयो वो वक्षःसु रुक्मा उपशिश्रियाणाः । वि विद्युतो न वृष्टिभी रुचाना अनु स्वधामायुधैर्यच्छमानाः ॥
7.56.e: Your rings, O Maruts, rest upon your shoulders, and chains of gold are twined upon your bosoms.  Gleaming with drops of rain, like lightning-flashes, after your wont ye whirl about your weapons.

7.56.d: प्र बुध्न्या व ईरते महांसि प्र नामानि प्रयज्यवस्तिरध्वम् । सहस्रियं दम्यं भागमेतं गृहमेधीयं मरुतो जुषध्वम् ॥
7.56.e: Wide in the depth of air spread forth your glories, far, most adorable, ye bear your titles.  Maruts, accept this thousandfold allotment of household sacrifice and household treasure.

7.56.d: यदि स्तुतस्य मरुतो अधीथेत्था विप्रस्य वाजिनो हवीमन् । मक्षू रायः सुवीर्यस्य दात नू चिद्यमन्य आदभदरावा ॥
7.56.e: If, Maruts, ye regard the praise recited here at this mighty singer invocation,  Vouchsafe us quickly wealth with noble heroes, wealth which no man uho hateth us may injure.

7.56.d: अत्यासो न ये मरुतः स्वञ्चो यक्षदृशो न शुभयन्त मर्याः । ते हर्म्येष्ठाः शिशवो न शुभ्रा वत्सासो न प्रक्रीळिनः पयोधाः ॥
7.56.e: The Maruts, fleet as coursers, while they deck them like youths spectators of a festal meeting,  Linger, like beauteous colts, about the dwelling, like frisking calves, these who pour down the water.

7.56.d: दशस्यन्तो नो मरुतो मृळन्तु वरिवस्यन्तो रोदसी सुमेके । आरे गोहा नृहा वधो वो अस्तु सुम्नेभिरस्मे वसवो नमध्वम् ॥
7.56.e: So may the Maruts help us and be gracious, bringing free room to lovely Earth and Heaven.  Far be your bolt that slayeth men and cattle. Ye Vasus, turn yourselves to us with blessings.

7.56.d: आ वो होता जोहवीति सत्तः सत्राचीं रातिं मरुतो गृणानः । य ईवतो वृषणो अस्ति गोपाः सो अद्वयावी हवते व उक्थैः ॥
7.56.e: The priest, when seated, loudly calls you, Maruts, praising in song your universal bounty.  He, Bulls! who hath so much in his possession, free from duplicity, with hymns invokes you.

7.56.d: इमे तुरं मरुतो रामयन्तीमे सहः सहस आ नमन्ति । इमे शंसं वनुष्यतो नि पान्ति गुरु द्वेषो अररुषे दधन्ति ॥
7.56.e: These Maruts bring the swift man to a stand-still, and strength with mightier strength they break and humble  These guard the singer from the man who hates him and lay their sore displeasure on the wicked.

7.56.d: इमे रध्रं चिन्मरुतो जुनन्ति भृमिं चिद्यथा वसवो जुषन्त । अप बाधध्वं वृषणस्तमांसि धत्त विश्वं तनयं तोकमस्मे ॥
7.56.e: These Maruts rouse even the poor and needy: the Vasus love him as an active champion.  Drive to a distance, O ye Bulls, the darkness: give us full store of children and descendants.

7.56.d: मा वो दात्रान्मरुतो निरराम मा पश्चाद्दघ्म रथ्यो विभागे । आ नः स्पार्हे भजतना वसव्ये३ यदीं सुजातं वृषणो वो अस्ति ॥
7.56.e: Never, O Maruts, may we lose your bounty, nor, car-borne Lords! be hitidmost when ye deal it.  Give us a share in that delightful treasure, the genuine wealth that, Bulls! is your possession.

7.56.d: सं यद्धनन्त मन्युभिर्जनासः शूरा यह्वीष्वोषधीषु विक्षु । अध स्मा नो मरुतो रुद्रियासस्त्रातारो भूत पृतनास्वर्यः ॥
7.56.e: What time the men in fury rush together for running streams, for pastures, and for houses.  Then, O ye Maruts, ye who spring from Rudra, be our protectors in the strife with foemen.

7.56.d: भूरि चक्र मरुतः पित्र्याण्युक्थानि या वः शस्यन्ते पुरा चित् । मरुद्भिरुग्रः पृतनासु साळ्हा मरुद्भिरित्सनिता वाजमर्वा ॥
7.56.e: Full many a deed ye did for our forefathers worthy of lauds which, even of old, they sang you.  lle strong man, with the Maruts, wins in battle, the charger, with the Maruts, gains the booty.

7.56.d: अस्मे वीरो मरुतः शुष्म्यस्तु जनानां यो असुरो विधर्ता । अपो येन सुक्षितये तरेमाध स्वमोको अभि वः स्याम ॥
7.56.e: Ours, O ye Maruts, be the vigorous Hero, the Lord Divine of men, the strong Sustainer,  With whom to fair lands we may cross the waters, and dwell in our own home with you beside us.

7.56.d: तन्न इन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निराप ओषधीर्वनिनो जुषन्त । शर्मन्त्स्याम मरुतामुपस्थे यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.56.e: May Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni, Waters, and Plants, and Trees accept our praises.  May we find shelter in the Marut's bosom. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.57.d: मध्वो वो नाम मारुतं यजत्राः प्र यज्ञेषु शवसा मदन्ति । ये रेजयन्ति रोदसी चिदुर्वी पिन्वन्त्युत्सं यदयासुरुग्राः ॥
7.57.e: YEA, through the power of your sweet juice, ye Holy! the Marut host is glad at sacrifices.  They cause even spacious heaven and earth to tremble, they make the spring flow when they come, the Mighty.

7.57.d: निचेतारो हि मरुतो गृणन्तं प्रणेतारो यजमानस्य मन्म । अस्माकमद्य विदथेषु बर्हिरा वीतये सदत पिप्रियाणाः ॥
7.57.e: The Maruts watch the man who sings their praises, promoters of the thought of him who worships.  Seat you on sacred grass in our assembly, this day, with friendly minds, to share the banquet.

7.57.d: नैतावदन्ये मरुतो यथेमे भ्राजन्ते रुक्मैरायुधैस्तनूभिः । आ रोदसी विश्वपिशः पिशानाः समानमञ्ज्यञ्जते शुभे कम् ॥
7.57.e: No others gleam so brightly as these Maruts with their own forms, their golden gauds, their weapons.  With all adornments, decking earth and heaven, they heighten, for bright show, their common splendour.

7.57.d: ऋधक्सा वो मरुतो दिद्युदस्तु यद्व आगः पुरुषता कराम । मा वस्तस्यामपि भूमा यजत्रा अस्मे वो अस्तु सुमतिश्चनिष्ठा ॥
7.57.e: Far from us be your blazing dart, O Maruts, when we, through human frailty, sin against you.  Let us not he exposed to that, ye Holy! May your most loving favour still attend us.

7.57.d: कृते चिदत्र मरुतो रणन्तानवद्यासः शुचयः पावकाः । प्र णोऽवत सुमतिभिर्यजत्राः प्र वाजेभिस्तिरत पुष्यसे नः ॥
7.57.e: May even what we have done delight the Maruts, the blameless Ones, the bright, the purifying.  Further us, O ye Holy, with your kindness: advance us mightily that we may prosper.

7.57.d: उत स्तुतासो मरुतो व्यन्तु विश्वेभिर्नामभिर्नरो हवींषि । ददात नो अमृतस्य प्रजायै जिगृत रायः सूनृता मघानि ॥
7.57.e: And may the Maruts, praised by all their titles, Heroes, enjoy the taste of our oblations.  Give us of Amṛta for the sake of offspring: awake the excellent fair stores of riches.

7.57.d: आ स्तुतासो मरुतो विश्व ऊती अच्छा सूरीन्त्सर्वताता जिगात । ये नस्त्मना शतिनो वर्धयन्ति यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.57.e: Hither, ye Maruts, praised, with all your succours, with all felicity come to our princes,  Who, of themselves, a hundredfold increase us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.58.d: प्र साकमुक्षे अर्चता गणाय यो दैव्यस्य धाम्नस्तुविष्मान् । उत क्षोदन्ति रोदसी महित्वा नक्षन्ते नाकं निर्ऋतेरवंशात् ॥
