7.58.e: SING to the troop that pours down rain in common, the Mighty Company of celestial nature.  They make the world-halves tremble with their greatness: from depths of earth and sky they reach to heaven.

7.58.d: जनूश्चिद्वो मरुतस्त्वेष्येण भीमासस्तुविमन्यवोऽयासः । प्र ये महोभिरोजसोत सन्ति विश्वो वो यामन्भयते स्वर्दृक् ॥
7.58.e: Yea, your birth, Maruts, was with wild commotion, ye who move swiftly, fierce in wrath, terrific.  Ye all-surpassing in your might and vigour, each looker on the light fears at your coming.

7.58.d: बृहद्वयो मघवद्भ्यो दधात जुजोषन्निन्मरुतः सुष्टुतिं नः । गतो नाध्वा वि तिराति जन्तुं प्र णः स्पार्हाभिरूतिभिस्तिरेत ॥
7.58.e: Give ample vital power unto our princes let our fair praises gratify the Maruts.  As the way travelled helpeth people onward, so further us with your delightful succours.

7.58.d: युष्मोतो विप्रो मरुतः शतस्वी युष्मोतो अर्वा सहुरिः सहस्री । युष्मोतः सम्राळुत हन्ति वृत्रं प्र तद्वो अस्तु धूतयो देष्णम् ॥
7.58.e: Your favoured singer counts his wealth by hundreds: the strong steed whom ye favour wins a thousand.  The Sovran whom ye aid destroys the foeman. May this your gift, ye Shakers, be distinguished.

7.58.d: ताँ आ रुद्रस्य मीळ्हुषो विवासे कुविन्नंसन्ते मरुतः पुनर्नः । यत्सस्वर्ता जिहीळिरे यदाविरव तदेन ईमहे तुराणाम् ॥
7.58.e: I call, as such, the Sons of bounteous Rudra: will not the Maruts turn again to us-ward?  What secret sin or open stirs their anger, that we implore the Swift Ones to forgive us.

7.58.d: प्र सा वाचि सुष्टुतिर्मघोनामिदं सूक्तं मरुतो जुषन्त । आराच्चिद्द्वेषो वृषणो युयोत यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.58.e: This eulogy of the Bounteous hath been spoken: accept, ye Maruts, this our hymn of praises.  Ye Bulls, keep those who hate us at a distance. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.59.d: यं त्रायध्व इदमिदं देवासो यं च नयथ । तस्मा अग्ने वरुण मित्रार्यमन्मरुतः शर्म यच्छत ॥
7.59.e: WHOMSO ye rescue here and there, whomso ye guide, O Deities,  To him give shelter, Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa, ye Maruts, and thou Aryaman.

7.59.d: युष्माकं देवा अवसाहनि प्रिय ईजानस्तरति द्विषः । प्र स क्षयं तिरते वि महीरिषो यो वो वराय दाशति ॥
7.59.e: Through your kind favour, Gods, on some auspicious day, the worshipper subdues his foes.  That man increases home and strengthening ample food who brings you offerings as ye list.

7.59.d: नहि वश्चरमं चन वसिष्ठः परिमंसते । अस्माकमद्य मरुतः सुते सचा विश्वे पिबत कामिनः ॥
7.59.e: Vasiṣṭha will not overlook the lowliest one among you all.  O Maruts, of our Soma juice effused to-day drink all of you with eager haste.

7.59.d: नहि व ऊतिः पृतनासु मर्धति यस्मा अराध्वं नरः । अभि व आवर्त्सुमतिर्नवीयसी तूयं यात पिपीषवः ॥
7.59.e: Your succour in the battle injures not the man to whom ye, Heroes, grant your gifts.  May your most recent favour turn to us again. Come quickly, ye who fain would drink.

7.59.d: ओ षु घृष्विराधसो यातनान्धांसि पीतये । इमा वो हव्या मरुतो ररे हि कं मो ष्व१न्यत्र गन्तन ॥
7.59.e: Come hitherward to drink the juice, O ye whose bounties give you joy.  These offerings are for you, these, Maruts, I present. Go not to any place but this.

7.59.d: आ च नो बर्हिः सदताविता च नः स्पार्हाणि दातवे वसु । अस्रेधन्तो मरुतः सोम्ये मधौ स्वाहेह मादयाध्वै ॥
7.59.e: Sit on our sacred grass, be graciously inclined to give the wealth for which we long,  To take delight, ye Maruts, Friends of all, with Svāhā, in sweet Soma juice.

7.59.d: सस्वश्चिद्धि तन्व१ः शुम्भमाना आ हंसासो नीलपृष्ठा अपप्तन् । विश्वं शर्धो अभितो मा नि षेद नरो न रण्वाः सवने मदन्तः ॥
7.59.e: Decking the beauty of their forms in secret the Swans with purple backs have flown down hither.  Around me all the Company hath settled, like joyous Heroes glad in our libation.

7.59.d: यो नो मरुतो अभि दुर्हृणायुस्तिरश्चित्तानि वसवो जिघांसति । द्रुहः पाशान्प्रति स मुचीष्ट तपिष्ठेन हन्मना हन्तना तम् ॥
7.59.e: Maruts, the man whose wrath is hard to master, he who would slay us ere we think, O Vasus,  May he be tangled in the toils of mischief; smite ye him down with your most flaming weapon.
O Maruts, ye consuming Gods, enjoy this offering brought for you,  To help us, ye who slay the foe.

7.59.d: गृहमेधास आ गत मरुतो माप भूतन । युष्माकोती सुदानवः ॥
7.59.e: Sharers of household sacrifice, come, Maruts, stay not far away,  That ye may help us, Bounteous Ones.

7.59.d: इहेह वः स्वतवसः कवयः सूर्यत्वचः । यज्ञं मरुत आ वृणे ॥
7.59.e: Here, Self-strong Maruts, yea, even here. ye Sages with your sunbright skins  I dedicate your sacrifice.

7.59.d: त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्धनम् । उर्वारुकमिव बन्धनान्मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मामृतात् ॥
7.59.e: Tryambaka we worship, sweet augmenter of prosperity.  As from its stem the cucumber, so may I be released from death, not reft of immortality.

7.60.d: यदद्य सूर्य ब्रवोऽनागा उद्यन्मित्राय वरुणाय सत्यम् । वयं देवत्रादिते स्याम तव प्रियासो अर्यमन्गृणन्तः ॥
7.60.e: WHEN thou, O Sun, this day, arising sinless, shalt speak the truth to Varuṇa and Mitra,  O Aditi, may all the Deities love us, and thou, O Aryaman, while we are singing.

7.60.d: एष स्य मित्रावरुणा नृचक्षा उभे उदेति सूर्यो अभि ज्मन् । विश्वस्य स्थातुर्जगतश्च गोपा ऋजु मर्तेषु वृजिना च पश्यन् ॥
7.60.e: Looking on man, O Varuṇa and Mitra, this Sun ascendeth up by both the pathways,  Guardian of all things fixt, of all that moveth, beholding good and evil acts of mortals.

7.60.d: अयुक्त सप्त हरितः सधस्थाद्या ईं वहन्ति सूर्यं घृताचीः । धामानि मित्रावरुणा युवाकुः सं यो यूथेव जनिमानि चष्टे ॥
7.60.e: He from their home hath yoked the Seven gold Coursers who, dropping oil and fatness, carry Sūrya.  Yours, Varuṇa and Mitra, he surveyeth the worlds and living creatures like a herdsman.

7.60.d: उद्वां पृक्षासो मधुमन्तो अस्थुरा सूर्यो अरुहच्छुक्रमर्णः । यस्मा आदित्या अध्वनो रदन्ति मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणः सजोषाः ॥
7.60.e: Your coursers rich in store of sweets have mounted: to the bright ocean Sūrya hath ascended,  For whom the Ādityas make his pathway ready, Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa, accordant.

7.60.d: इमे चेतारो अनृतस्य भूरेर्मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणो हि सन्ति । इम ऋतस्य वावृधुर्दुरोणे शग्मासः पुत्रा अदितेरदब्धाः ॥
7.60.e: For these, even Aryaman, Varuṇa and Mitra, are the chastisers of all guile and falsehood.  These, Aditi's Sons, infallible and mighty, have waxen in the home of law Eternal.

7.60.d: इमे मित्रो वरुणो दूळभासोऽचेतसं चिच्चितयन्ति दक्षैः । अपि क्रतुं सुचेतसं वतन्तस्तिरश्चिदंहः सुपथा नयन्ति ॥
7.60.e: These, Mitra, Varuṇa whom none deceiveth, with great power quicken even the fool to wisdom,  And, wakening, moreover, thoughtful insight, lead it by easy paths o’er grief and trouble.

7.60.d: इमे दिवो अनिमिषा पृथिव्याश्चिकित्वांसो अचेतसं नयन्ति । प्रव्राजे चिन्नद्यो गाधमस्ति पारं नो अस्य विष्पितस्य पर्षन् ॥
7.60.e: They ever vigilant, with eyes that close not, caring for heaven and earth, lead on the thoughtless.  Even in the river's bed there is a shallow. across this broad expanse may they conduct us.

7.60.d: यद्गोपावददितिः शर्म भद्रं मित्रो यच्छन्ति वरुणः सुदासे । तस्मिन्ना तोकं तनयं दधाना मा कर्म देवहेळनं तुरासः ॥
7.60.e: When Aditi and Varuṇa and Mitra, like guardians, give Sudās their friendly shelter,  Granting him sons and lineal succession, let us not, bold ones! move the Gods to anger.

7.60.d: अव वेदिं होत्राभिर्यजेत रिपः काश्चिद्वरुणध्रुतः सः । परि द्वेषोभिरर्यमा वृणक्तूरुं सुदासे वृषणा उ लोकम् ॥
7.60.e: May he with ofierings purify the altar from any stains of Varuṇa's reviler.  Aryaman save us us all those who hate us: give room and freedom to Sudās, ye Mighty.

7.60.d: सस्वश्चिद्धि समृतिस्त्वेष्येषामपीच्येन सहसा सहन्ते । युष्मद्भिया वृषणो रेजमाना दक्षस्य चिन्महिना मृळता नः ॥
7.60.e: Hid from our eyes is their resplendent meeting: by their mysterious might they hold dominion.  Heroes! we cry trembling in fear before you, even in the greatness of your power have mercy.

7.60.d: यो ब्रह्मणे सुमतिमायजाते वाजस्य सातौ परमस्य रायः । सीक्षन्त मन्युं मघवानो अर्य उरु क्षयाय चक्रिरे सुधातु ॥
7.60.e: He who wins favour for his prayer by worship, that he may gain him strength and highest riches,  That good man's mind the Mighty Ones will follow: they have brought comfort to his spacious dwelling.

7.60.d: इयं देव पुरोहितिर्युवभ्यां यज्ञेषु मित्रावरुणावकारि । विश्वानि दुर्गा पिपृतं तिरो नो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.60.e: This priestly task, Gods! Varuṇa and Mitra! hath been performed for you at sacrifices.  Convey us safely over every peril. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.61.d: उद्वां चक्षुर्वरुण सुप्रतीकं देवयोरेति सूर्यस्ततन्वान् । अभि यो विश्वा भुवनानि चष्टे स मन्युं मर्त्येष्वा चिकेत ॥
7.61.e: O VARUNA and Mitra, Sūrya spreading the beauteous light of you Twain Gods ariseth.  He who beholdetb all existing creatures observetb well the zeal that is in mortals.

7.61.d: प्र वां स मित्रावरुणावृतावा विप्रो मन्मानि दीर्घश्रुदियर्ति । यस्य ब्रह्माणि सुक्रतू अवाथ आ यत्क्रत्वा न शरदः पृणैथे ॥
7.61.e: The holy sage, renowned afar, directeth his hymns to you, O Varuṇa and Mitra,—  He whose devotions, sapient Gods, ye favour so that ye fill, as ’twere, with power his autumns.

7.61.d: प्रोरोर्मित्रावरुणा पृथिव्याः प्र दिव ऋष्वाद्बृहतः सुदानू । स्पशो दधाथे ओषधीषु विक्ष्वृधग्यतो अनिमिषं रक्षमाणा ॥
7.61.e: From the wide earth, O Varuṇa and Mitra from the great lofty heaven, ye, Bounteous Givers, -  Have in the fields and houses set your warder-, who visit every spot and watch unceasing.

7.61.d: शंसा मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धाम शुष्मो रोदसी बद्बधे महित्वा । अयन्मासा अयज्वनामवीराः प्र यज्ञमन्मा वृजनं तिराते ॥
7.61.e: I praise the strength of Varuṇa and Mitra that strength, by mightiness, keeps both worlds asunder.  Heroless pass the months of the ungodly he who loves sacrifice makes his home enduring.

7.61.d: अमूरा विश्वा वृषणाविमा वां न यासु चित्रं ददृशे न यक्षम् । द्रुहः सचन्ते अनृता जनानां न वां निण्यान्यचिते अभूवन् ॥
7.61.e: Steers, all infallible are these your people in whom no wondrous thing is seen, no worship.  Guile follows close the men who are untruthful: no secrets may be hidden from your knowledge.

7.61.d: समु वां यज्ञं महयं नमोभिर्हुवे वां मित्रावरुणा सबाधः । प्र वां मन्मान्यृचसे नवानि कृतानि ब्रह्म जुजुषन्निमानि ॥
7.61.e: I will exalt your sacrifice with homage: as priest, I, Mitra-Varuṇa, invoke you.  May these new hymns and prayers that I have fashioned delight you to the profit of the singer.

7.61.d: इयं देव पुरोहितिर्युवभ्यां यज्ञेषु मित्रावरुणावकारि । विश्वानि दुर्गा पिपृतं तिरो नो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.61.e: This priestly task, Gods! Varuṇa and Mitra! hath been performed for you at sacrifices.  Convey us safely over every peril. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.62.d: उत्सूर्यो बृहदर्चींष्यश्रेत्पुरु विश्वा जनिम मानुषाणाम् । समो दिवा ददृशे रोचमानः क्रत्वा कृतः सुकृतः कर्तृभिर्भूत् ॥
7.62.e: SURYA hath sent aloft his beams of splendour o’er all the tribes of men in countless places.  Together with the heaven he shines apparent, formed by his Makers well with power and wisdom.

7.62.d: स सूर्य प्रति पुरो न उद्गा एभिः स्तोमेभिरेतशेभिरेवैः । प्र नो मित्राय वरुणाय वोचोऽनागसो अर्यम्णे अग्नये च ॥
7.62.e: So hast thou mounted up before us, Sūrya, through these our praises, with fleet dappled horses.  Declare us free from all offence to Mitra, and Varuṇa, and Aryaman, and Agni.

7.62.d: वि नः सहस्रं शुरुधो रदन्त्वृतावानो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निः । यच्छन्तु चन्द्रा उपमं नो अर्कमा नः कामं पूपुरन्तु स्तवानाः ॥
7.62.e: May holy Agni, Varuṇa, and Mitra send down their riches upon us in thousands.  May they, the Bright Ones, make our praise-song perfect, and, when we laud them, grant us all our wishes.

7.62.d: द्यावाभूमी अदिते त्रासीथां नो ये वां जज्ञुः सुजनिमान ऋष्वे । मा हेळे भूम वरुणस्य वायोर्मा मित्रस्य प्रियतमस्य नृणाम् ॥
7.62.e: O undivided Heaven and Earth, preserve us, us, Lofty Ones! your nobIy-born descendants.  Let us not anger Varuṇa, nor Vāyu, nor him, the dearest Friend of mortals, Mitra.

7.62.d: प्र बाहवा सिसृतं जीवसे न आ नो गव्यूतिमुक्षतं घृतेन । आ नो जने श्रवयतं युवाना श्रुतं मे मित्रावरुणा हवेमा ॥
7.62.e: Stretch forth your arms and let our lives be lengthened: with fatness dew the pastures of our cattle.  Ye Youthful, make us famed among the people: hear, Mitra-Varuṇa, these mine invocations.

7.62.d: नू मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमा नस्त्मने तोकाय वरिवो दधन्तु । सुगा नो विश्वा सुपथानि सन्तु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.62.e: Now Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman vouchsafe us freedom and room, for us and for our children.  May we find paths all fair and good to travel. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.63.d: उद्वेति सुभगो विश्वचक्षाः साधारणः सूर्यो मानुषाणाम् । चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्य देवश्चर्मेव यः समविव्यक्तमांसि ॥
7.63.e: COMMON to all mankind, auspicious Sūrya, he who beholdeth all, is mounting upward;  The God, the eye of Varuṇa and Mitra, who rolled up darkness like a piece of leather.

7.63.d: उद्वेति प्रसवीता जनानां महान्केतुरर्णवः सूर्यस्य । समानं चक्रं पर्याविवृत्सन्यदेतशो वहति धूर्षु युक्तः ॥
7.63.e: Sūrya's great ensign, restless as the billow, that urgeth men to action, is advancing:  Onward he still would roll the wheel well-rounded, which Etaśa, harnessed to the car-pole, moveth.

7.63.d: विभ्राजमान उषसामुपस्थाद्रेभैरुदेत्यनुमद्यमानः । एष मे देवः सविता चच्छन्द यः समानं न प्रमिनाति धाम ॥
7.63.e: Refulgent from the bosom of the Mornings, he in Whom singers take delight ascendeth.  This Savitar, God, is my chief joy and pleasure, who breaketh not the universal statute.

7.63.d: दिवो रुक्म उरुचक्षा उदेति दूरेअर्थस्तरणिर्भ्राजमानः । नूनं जनाः सूर्येण प्रसूता अयन्नर्थानि कृणवन्नपांसि ॥
7.63.e: Golden, far-seeing, from the heaven he riseth: far is his goal, he hasteth on resplendent.  Men, verily, inspirited by Sūrya speed to their aims and do the work assigned them.

7.63.d: यत्रा चक्रुरमृता गातुमस्मै श्येनो न दीयन्नन्वेति पाथः । प्रति वां सूर उदिते विधेम नमोभिर्मित्रावरुणोत हव्यैः ॥
7.63.e: Where the irrunortals have prepared his pathway he flieth through the region like a falcon.  With homage and oblations will we serve you, O Mitra-Varuṇa, when the Sun hath risen.

7.63.d: नू मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमा नस्त्मने तोकाय वरिवो दधन्तु । सुगा नो विश्वा सुपथानि सन्तु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.63.e: Now Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman vouchsafe us freedom and room, for us and for our children.  May we find paths all fair and good to travel. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.64.d: दिवि क्षयन्ता रजसः पृथिव्यां प्र वां घृतस्य निर्णिजो ददीरन् । हव्यं नो मित्रो अर्यमा सुजातो राजा सुक्षत्रो वरुणो जुषन्त ॥
7.64.e: YE Twain who rule, in heaven and earth, the region, clothed be your clouds in robes of oil and fatness.  May the imperial Varuṇa, and Mitra, and high-born Aryaman accept our presents.

7.64.d: आ राजाना मह ऋतस्य गोपा सिन्धुपती क्षत्रिया यातमर्वाक् । इळां नो मित्रावरुणोत वृष्टिमव दिव इन्वतं जीरदानू ॥
7.64.e: Kings, guards of rrtighty everlasting Order, come hitherward, ye Princes, Lords of Rivers.  Send us from heaven, O Varuṇa and Mitra, rain and sweet food, ye who pour down your bounties.

7.64.d: मित्रस्तन्नो वरुणो देवो अर्यः प्र साधिष्ठेभिः पथिभिर्नयन्तु । ब्रवद्यथा न आदरिः सुदास इषा मदेम सह देवगोपाः ॥
7.64.e: May the dear God, and Varuṇa and Mitra conduct us by the most effective pathways,  That foes may say unto Sudās our chieftain, May, we, too, joy in food with Gods to guard us.

7.64.d: यो वां गर्तं मनसा तक्षदेतमूर्ध्वां धीतिं कृणवद्धारयच्च । उक्षेथां मित्रावरुणा घृतेन ता राजाना सुक्षितीस्तर्पयेथाम् ॥
7.64.e: Him who hath wrought for you this car in spirit, who makes the song rise upward and sustains it,  Bedew with fatness, Varuṇa nd Mitra ye Kings, make glad the pleasant dwelling-places.

7.64.d: एष स्तोमो वरुण मित्र तुभ्यं सोमः शुक्रो न वायवेऽयामि । अविष्टं धियो जिगृतं पुरंधीर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.64.e: To you this laud, O Varuṇa and Mitra is offered like bright Soma juice to Vāyu.  Favour our songs of praise, wake thought and spirit. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.65.d: प्रति वां सूर उदिते सूक्तैर्मित्रं हुवे वरुणं पूतदक्षम् । ययोरसुर्य१मक्षितं ज्येष्ठं विश्वस्य यामन्नाचिता जिगत्नु ॥
7.65.e: WITH hymns I call you, when the Sun hath risen, Mitra, and Varuṇa whose thoughts are holy,  Whose Power Divine, supreme and everlasting, comes with good heed at each man's supplication.

7.65.d: ता हि देवानामसुरा तावर्या ता नः क्षितीः करतमूर्जयन्तीः । अश्याम मित्रावरुणा वयं वां द्यावा च यत्र पीपयन्नहा च ॥
7.65.e: For they are Asuras of Gods, the friendly make, both of you, our lands exceeding fruitful.  May we obtain you, Varuṇa and Mitra, wherever Heaven and Earth and days may bless us.

7.65.d: ता भूरिपाशावनृतस्य सेतू दुरत्येतू रिपवे मर्त्याय । ऋतस्य मित्रावरुणा पथा वामपो न नावा दुरिता तरेम ॥
7.65.e: Bonds of the sinner, they bear many nooses: the wicked mortal hardly may escape them.  Varuṇa-Mitra, may your path of Order bear us o’er trouble as a boat o’er waters.

7.65.d: आ नो मित्रावरुणा हव्यजुष्टिं घृतैर्गव्यूतिमुक्षतमिळाभिः । प्रति वामत्र वरमा जनाय पृणीतमुद्नो दिव्यस्य चारोः ॥
7.65.e: Come, taste our offering, Varuṇa and Mitra: bedew our pasture wil sweet food and fatness.  Pour down in plenty here upon the people the choicest of your fair celestial water.

7.65.d: एष स्तोमो वरुण मित्र तुभ्यं सोमः शुक्रो न वायवेऽयामि । अविष्टं धियो जिगृतं पुरंधीर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.65.e: To you this laud, O Varuṇa and Mitra, is offered, like bright Soma juice to Vāyu.  Favour our songs of praise, wake thought and spirit. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.66.d: प्र मित्रयोर्वरुणयोः स्तोमो न एतु शूष्यः । नमस्वान्तुविजातयोः ॥
7.66.e: LET our strong hymn of praise go forth, the laud of Mitra-Varuṇa,  With homage to that high-born Pair;

7.66.d: या धारयन्त देवाः सुदक्षा दक्षपितरा । असुर्याय प्रमहसा ॥
7.66.e: The Two exceeding wise, the Sons of Dakṣa, whom the gods ordained  For lordship, excellently great.

7.66.d: ता नः स्तिपा तनूपा वरुण जरितॄणाम् । मित्र साधयतं धियः ॥
7.66.e: Such, Guardians of our homes and us, O Mitra-Varuṇa, fulfil  The thoughts of those who sing your praise.

7.66.d: यदद्य सूर उदितेऽनागा मित्रो अर्यमा । सुवाति सविता भगः ॥
7.66.e: So when the Sun hath risen to-day, may sinless Mitra, Aryaman,  Bhaga, and Savitar sendus forth.

7.66.d: सुप्रावीरस्तु स क्षयः प्र नु यामन्त्सुदानवः । ये नो अंहोऽतिपिप्रति ॥
7.66.e: May this our home be guarded well forward, ye Bounteous, on the way,  Who bear us safely o’er distress.

7.66.d: उत स्वराजो अदितिरदब्धस्य व्रतस्य ये । महो राजान ईशते ॥
7.66.e: And those Self-reigning, Aditi, whose statute is inviolate,  The Kings who rule a vast domain.

7.66.d: प्रति वां सूर उदिते मित्रं गृणीषे वरुणम् । अर्यमणं रिशादसम् ॥
7.66.e: Soon as the Sun hath risen, to you, to Mitra-Varuṇa, I sing,  And Aryarnan who slays the foe.

7.66.d: राया हिरण्यया मतिरियमवृकाय शवसे । इयं विप्रा मेधसातये ॥
7.66.e: With wealth of gold may this my song bring unmolested power and might,  And, Brahmans, gain the sacrifice.

7.66.d: ते स्याम देव वरुण ते मित्र सूरिभिः सह । इषं स्वश्च धीमहि ॥
7.66.e: May we be thine, God Varuṇa, and with our princes, Mitra, thine.  Food and Heaven's light will we obtain.

7.66.d: बहवः सूरचक्षसोऽग्निजिह्वा ऋतावृधः । त्रीणि ये येमुर्विदथानि धीतिभिर्विश्वानि परिभूतिभिः ॥
7.66.e: Many are they who strengthen Law, Sun-eyed, with Agni for their tongue,  They who direct the three great gatherings with their thoughts, yea, all things with surpassing might.

7.66.d: वि ये दधुः शरदं मासमादहर्यज्ञमक्तुं चादृचम् । अनाप्यं वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा क्षत्रं राजान आशत ॥
7.66.e: They who have stablished year and month and then the day, night, sacrifice and holy verse,  Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryarnan, the Kings, have won dominion which none else may gain.

7.66.d: तद्वो अद्य मनामहे सूक्तैः सूर उदिते । यदोहते वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा यूयमृतस्य रथ्यः ॥
7.66.e: So at the rising of the Sun we think of you with hymns to-day,  Even as Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman deserve: ye are the charioteers of Law.

7.66.d: ऋतावान ऋतजाता ऋतावृधो घोरासो अनृतद्विषः । तेषां वः सुम्ने सुच्छर्दिष्टमे नरः स्याम ये च सूरयः ॥
7.66.e: True to Law, born in Law the strengtheners of Law, terrible, haters of the false,  In their felicity which gives the best defence may we men and our princes dwell.

7.66.d: उदु त्यद्दर्शतं वपुर्दिव एति प्रतिह्वरे । यदीमाशुर्वहति देव एतशो विश्वस्मै चक्षसे अरम् ॥
7.66.e: Uprises, on the slope of heaven, that marvel that attracts die sight  As swift celestial Etaśa bears it away, prepared for every eye to see.

7.66.d: शीर्ष्णःशीर्ष्णो जगतस्तस्थुषस्पतिं समया विश्वमा रजः । सप्त स्वसारः सुविताय सूर्यं वहन्ति हरितो रथे ॥
7.66.e: Lord of each single head, of fixt and moving things, equally through the whole expanse,  The Seven sister Bays bear Sūrya on his car, to bring us wealth and happiness.

7.66.d: तच्चक्षुर्देवहितं शुक्रमुच्चरत् । पश्येम शरदः शतं जीवेम शरदः शतम् ॥
7.66.e: A hundred autumns may we see that bright Eye, God-ordained, arise  A hundred autumns may we live.

7.66.d: काव्येभिरदाभ्या यातं वरुण द्युमत् । मित्रश्च सोमपीतये ॥
7.66.e: Infallible through your wisdom, come hither, resplendent Varuṇa,  And Mitra, to the Soma draught.

7.66.d: दिवो धामभिर्वरुण मित्रश्चा यातमद्रुहा । पिबतं सोममातुजी ॥
7.66.e: Come as the laws of Heaven ordain, Varuṇa, Mitra, void of guile:  Press near and drink the Soma juice.

7.66.d: आ यातं मित्रावरुणा जुषाणावाहुतिं नरा । पातं सोममृतावृधा ॥
7.66.e: Come, Mitra, Varuṇa, accept, Heroes, our sacrificial gift:  Drink Soma, ye who strengthen Law.

7.67.d: प्रति वां रथं नृपती जरध्यै हविष्मता मनसा यज्ञियेन । यो वां दूतो न धिष्ण्यावजीगरच्छा सूनुर्न पितरा विवक्मि ॥
7.67.e: I WITH a holy heart that brings oblation will sing forth praise to meet your car, ye Princes,  Which, Much-desired! hath wakened as your envoy. I call you hither as a son his parents.

7.67.d: अशोच्यग्निः समिधानो अस्मे उपो अदृश्रन्तमसश्चिदन्ताः । अचेति केतुरुषसः पुरस्ताच्छ्रिये दिवो दुहितुर्जायमानः ॥
7.67.e: Brightly hath Agni shone by us enkindled: the limits even of darkness were apparent.  Eastward is seen the Banner of the Morning, the Banner born to give Heaven's Daughter glory.

7.67.d: अभि वां नूनमश्विना सुहोता स्तोमैः सिषक्ति नासत्या विवक्वान् । पूर्वीभिर्यातं पथ्याभिरर्वाक्स्वर्विदा वसुमता रथेन ॥
7.67.e: With hymns the deft priest is about you, Aśvins, the eloquent priest attends you now, Nāsatyas.  Come by the paths that ye are wont to travel, on car that finds the light, laden with treasure.

7.67.d: अवोर्वां नूनमश्विना युवाकुर्हुवे यद्वां सुते माध्वी वसूयुः । आ वां वहन्तु स्थविरासो अश्वाः पिबाथो अस्मे सुषुता मधूनि ॥
7.67.e: When, suppliant for your help, Lovers of Sweetness! I seeking wealth call you to our libation,  Hitherward let your vigorous horses bear you: drink ye with us the well-pressed Soma juices.

7.67.d: प्राचीमु देवाश्विना धियं मेऽमृध्रां सातये कृतं वसूयुम् । विश्वा अविष्टं वाज आ पुरंधीस्ता नः शक्तं शचीपती शचीभिः ॥
7.67.e: Bring forward, Aśvins, Gods, to its fulfilment my never-wearied prayer that asks for riches.  Vouchsafe us all high spirit in the combat, and with your powers, O Lords of Power, assist us.

7.67.d: अविष्टं धीष्वश्विना न आसु प्रजावद्रेतो अह्रयं नो अस्तु । आ वां तोके तनये तूतुजानाः सुरत्नासो देववीतिं गमेम ॥
7.67.e: Favour us in these prayers of ours, O Aśvins. May we have genial vigour, ne’er to fail us.  So may we, strong in children and descendants, go, wealthy, to the banquet that awaits you.

7.67.d: एष स्य वां पूर्वगत्वेव सख्ये निधिर्हितो माध्वी रातो अस्मे । अहेळता मनसा यातमर्वागश्नन्ता हव्यं मानुषीषु विक्षु ॥
7.67.e: Lovers of Sweetness, we have brought this treasure to you as ’twere an envoy sent for friendship.  Come unto us with spirits free from anger, in homes of men enjoying our oblation.

7.67.d: एकस्मिन्योगे भुरणा समाने परि वां सप्त स्रवतो रथो गात् । न वायन्ति सुभ्वो देवयुक्ता ये वां धूर्षु तरणयो वहन्ति ॥
7.67.e: With one, the same, intention, ye swift movers, o’er the Seven Rivers hath your chariot travelled.  Yoked by the Gods, your strong steeds never weary while speeding forward at the pole they bear you.

7.67.d: असश्चता मघवद्भ्यो हि भूतं ये राया मघदेयं जुनन्ति । प्र ये बन्धुं सूनृताभिस्तिरन्ते गव्या पृञ्चन्तो अश्व्या मघानि ॥
7.67.e: Exhaustless be your bounty to our princes who with their wealth incite the gift of riches,  Who further friendship with their noble natures, combining wealth in kine with wealth in herses.

7.67.d: नू मे हवमा शृणुतं युवाना यासिष्टं वर्तिरश्विनाविरावत् । धत्तं रत्नानि जरतं च सूरीन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.67.e: Now hear, O Youthful Twain, mine invocation: come, Aśvins, to the home where food aboundeth.  Vouchsafe us wealth, do honour to our nobles. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.68.d: आ शुभ्रा यातमश्विना स्वश्वा गिरो दस्रा जुजुषाणा युवाकोः । हव्यानि च प्रतिभृता वीतं नः ॥
7.68.e: COME, radiant Aśvins, with your noble horses: accept your servant's hymns, ye Wonder-Workers:  Enjoy oblations which we bring to greet you.

7.68.d: प्र वामन्धांसि मद्यान्यस्थुररं गन्तं हविषो वीतये मे । तिरो अर्यो हवनानि श्रुतं नः ॥
7.68.e: The gladdening juices stand prepared before you: come quickly and partake of mine oblation.  Pass by the calling of our foe and bear us.

7.68.d: प्र वां रथो मनोजवा इयर्ति तिरो रजांस्यश्विना शतोतिः । अस्मभ्यं सूर्यावसू इयानः ॥
7.68.e: Your chariot with a hundred aids, O Aśvins, beareth you swift as thought across the regions,  Speeding to us, O ye whose wealth is Sūrya.

7.68.d: अयं ह यद्वां देवया उ अद्रिरूर्ध्वो विवक्ति सोमसुद्युवभ्याम् । आ वल्गू विप्रो ववृतीत हव्यैः ॥
7.68.e: What time this stone of yours, the Gods’ adorer, upraised, sounds forth for you as Soma-presser,  Let the priest bring you, Fair Ones, through oblations.

7.68.d: चित्रं ह यद्वां भोजनं न्वस्ति न्यत्रये महिष्वन्तं युयोतम् । यो वामोमानं दधते प्रियः सन् ॥
7.68.e: The nourishment ye have is, truly, wondrous: ye gave thereof a quickening store to Atri,  Who being dear to you, receives your favour.

7.68.d: उत त्यद्वां जुरते अश्विना भूच्च्यवानाय प्रतीत्यं हविर्दे । अधि यद्वर्प इतऊति धत्थः ॥
7.68.e: That gift, which all may gain, ye gave Cyavāna, when he grew old, who offered you oblations,  When ye bestowed on him enduring beauty.

7.68.d: उत त्यं भुज्युमश्विना सखायो मध्ये जहुर्दुरेवासः समुद्रे । निरीं पर्षदरावा यो युवाकुः ॥
7.68.e: What time his wicked friends abandoned Bhujyu, O Aśvins, in the middle of the ocean,  Your horse delivered him, your faithful servant.

7.68.d: वृकाय चिज्जसमानाय शक्तमुत श्रुतं शयवे हूयमाना । यावघ्न्यामपिन्वतमपो न स्तर्यं चिच्छक्त्यश्विना शचीभिः ॥
7.68.e: Ye lent your aid to Vrka when exhausted, and listened when invoked to Śayu's calling.  Ye made the cow pour forth her milk like water, and, Aśvins, strengthened with your strength the barren.

7.68.d: एष स्य कारुर्जरते सूक्तैरग्रे बुधान उषसां सुमन्मा । इषा तं वर्धदघ्न्या पयोभिर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.68.e: With his fair hymns this singer, too, extols you, waking with glad thoughts at the break of morning.  May the cow nourish him with milk to feed llim. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.69.d: आ वां रथो रोदसी बद्बधानो हिरण्ययो वृषभिर्यात्वश्वैः । घृतवर्तनिः पविभी रुचान इषां वोळ्हा नृपतिर्वाजिनीवान् ॥
7.69.e: MAY your gold chariot, drawn by vigorous horses, come to us, blocking up the earth  and heaven,  Bright with its fellies while its way drops fatness, food-laden, rich in coursers, man's protector.

7.69.d: स पप्रथानो अभि पञ्च भूमा त्रिवन्धुरो मनसा यातु युक्तः । विशो येन गच्छथो देवयन्तीः कुत्रा चिद्याममश्विना दधाना ॥
7.69.e: Let it approach, yoked by thewill, three-seated, extending far and wide o’er fivefold beings,  Whereon ye visit God-adoring races, bending your course whither ye will, O Aśvins.

7.69.d: स्वश्वा यशसा यातमर्वाग्दस्रा निधिं मधुमन्तं पिबाथः । वि वां रथो वध्वा३ यादमानोऽन्तान्दिवो बाधते वर्तनिभ्याम् ॥
7.69.e: Renowned, with noble horses, come ye hither: drink, Wondrous Pair, the cup that holds sweet juices.  Your car whereon your Spouse is wont to travel marks with its track the farthest ends of heaven.

7.69.d: युवोः श्रियं परि योषावृणीत सूरो दुहिता परितक्म्यायाम् । यद्देवयन्तमवथः शचीभिः परि घ्रंसमोमना वां वयो गात् ॥
7.69.e: When night was turning to the grey of morning the Maiden, Sūrya's Daughter, chose your splendour.  When with your power and might ye aid the pious he comes through heat to life by your assistance.

7.69.d: यो ह स्य वां रथिरा वस्त उस्रा रथो युजानः परियाति वर्तिः । तेन नः शं योरुषसो व्युष्टौ न्यश्विना वहतं यज्ञे अस्मिन् ॥
7.69.e: O Chariot-borne, this car of yours invested with rays of light comes harnessed to our dwelling.  Herewith, O Aśvins, while the dawn is breaking, to this our sacrifice bring peace and blessing.

7.69.d: नरा गौरेव विद्युतं तृषाणास्माकमद्य सवनोप यातम् । पुरुत्रा हि वां मतिभिर्हवन्ते मा वामन्ये नि यमन्देवयन्तः ॥
7.69.e: Like the wild cattle thirsty for the lightning, Heroes, come nigh this day to our libations.  Men call on you with hymns in many places, but let not other worshippers detain you.

7.69.d: युवं भुज्युमवविद्धं समुद्र उदूहथुरर्णसो अस्रिधानैः । पतत्रिभिरश्रमैरव्यथिभिर्दंसनाभिरश्विना पारयन्ता ॥
7.69.e: Bhujyu, abandoned in the midst of ocean, ye raised from out the water with your horses,  Uninjured, winged, flagging not, undaunted, with deeds of wonder saving him, O Aśvins.

7.69.d: नू मे हवमा शृणुतं युवाना यासिष्टं वर्तिरश्विनाविरावत् । धत्तं रत्नानि जरतं च सूरीन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.69.e: Now hear, O Youthful Twain, mine invocation: come, Aśvins, to the home where food aboundeth.  Vouchsafe us wealth, do honour to our nobles. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.70.d: आ विश्ववाराश्विना गतं नः प्र तत्स्थानमवाचि वां पृथिव्याम् । अश्वो न वाजी शुनपृष्ठो अस्थादा यत्सेदथुर्ध्रुवसे न योनिम् ॥
7.70.e: RICH in all blessings, Aśvins come ye hither: this place on earth is called your own possession,  Like a strong horse with a fair back it standeth, whereon, as in a lap, ye seat you firmly.

7.70.d: सिषक्ति सा वां सुमतिश्चनिष्ठातापि घर्मो मनुषो दुरोणे । यो वां समुद्रान्त्सरितः पिपर्त्येतग्वा चिन्न सुयुजा युजानः ॥
7.70.e: This most delightful eulogy awaits you in the man's house drink-offering hath been heated,  Which bringeth you over the seas and rivers, yoking as’twere two well-matched shining horses.

7.70.d: यानि स्थानान्यश्विना दधाथे दिवो यह्वीष्वोषधीषु विक्षु । नि पर्वतस्य मूर्धनि सदन्तेषं जनाय दाशुषे वहन्ता ॥
7.70.e: Whatever dwellings ye possess, O Aśvins, in fields of men or in the streams of heaven,  Resting upon the summit of the mountain, or bringing food to him who gives oblation,

7.70.d: चनिष्टं देवा ओषधीष्वप्सु यद्योग्या अश्नवैथे ऋषीणाम् । पुरूणि रत्ना दधतौ न्य१स्मे अनु पूर्वाणि चख्यथुर्युगानि ॥
7.70.e: Delight yourselves, ye Gods, in plants and waters when Ṛṣis give them and ye find they suit You.  Enriching us with treasures in abundance ye have looked back to former generations.

7.70.d: शुश्रुवांसा चिदश्विना पुरूण्यभि ब्रह्माणि चक्षाथे ऋषीणाम् । प्रति प्र यातं वरमा जनायास्मे वामस्तु सुमतिश्चनिष्ठा ॥
7.70.e: Aśvins, though ye have heard them oft aforetime, regard the many prayers which Ṛṣis offer.  Come to the man even as his heart desireth: may we enjoy your most delightful favour.

7.70.d: यो वां यज्ञो नासत्या हविष्मान्कृतब्रह्मा समर्यो३ भवाति । उप प्र यातं वरमा वसिष्ठमिमा ब्रह्माण्यृच्यन्ते युवभ्याम् ॥
7.70.e: Come to the sacrifice offered you, Nāsatyas, with men, oblations, and prayer duly uttered.  Come to Vasiṣṭha as his heart desireth, for unto you these holy hymns are chanted.

7.70.d: इयं मनीषा इयमश्विना गीरिमां सुवृक्तिं वृषणा जुषेथाम् । इमा ब्रह्माणि युवयून्यग्मन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.70.e: This is the thought, this is the song, O Aśvins: accept this hymn of ours, ye Steers, with favour.  May these our prayers addressed to you come nigh you. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.71.d: अप स्वसुरुषसो नग्जिहीते रिणक्ति कृष्णीररुषाय पन्थाम् । अश्वामघा गोमघा वां हुवेम दिवा नक्तं शरुमस्मद्युयोतम् ॥
7.71.e: THE Night retireth from the Dawn her Sister; the Dark one yieldeth to the Red her pathway.  Let us invoke you rich in steeds and cattle - by day and night keep far from us the arrow.

7.71.d: उपायातं दाशुषे मर्त्याय रथेन वाममश्विना वहन्ता । युयुतमस्मदनिराममीवां दिवा नक्तं माध्वी त्रासीथां नः ॥
7.71.e: Bearing rich treasure in your car, O Aśvins, come to the mortal who presents oblation.  Keep at a distance penury and sickness; Lovers of Sweetness, day and night preserve us.

7.71.d: आ वां रथमवमस्यां व्युष्टौ सुम्नायवो वृषणो वर्तयन्तु । स्यूमगभस्तिमृतयुग्भिरश्वैराश्विना वसुमन्तं वहेथाम् ॥
7.71.e: May your strong horses, seeking bliss, bring hither your chariot at the earliest flush of morning.  With coursers yoked by Law drive hither, Aśvins, your car whose reins are light, laden with treasure.

7.71.d: यो वां रथो नृपती अस्ति वोळ्हा त्रिवन्धुरो वसुमाँ उस्रयामा । आ न एना नासत्योप यातमभि यद्वां विश्वप्स्न्यो जिगाति ॥
7.71.e: The chariot, Princes, that conveys you, moving at daylight, triple-seated, fraught with riches,  Even with this come unto us, Nāsatyas, that laden with all food it may approach us.

7.71.d: युवं च्यवानं जरसोऽमुमुक्तं नि पेदव ऊहथुराशुमश्वम् । निरंहसस्तमसः स्पर्तमत्रिं नि जाहुषं शिथिरे धातमन्तः ॥
7.71.e: Ye freed Cyavāna from old age and weakness: ye brought the courser fleet of food to Pedu.  Ye rescued Atri from distress and darkness, and loosed for Jāhuṣa the bonds that bound him.

7.71.d: इयं मनीषा इयमश्विना गीरिमां सुवृक्तिं वृषणा जुषेथाम् । इमा ब्रह्माणि युवयून्यग्मन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.71.e: This is the thought, this is the song, O Aśvins: accept this hymn of ours, ye Steers, With favour.  May these our prayers addressed to you come nigh you. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.72.d: आ गोमता नासत्या रथेनाश्वावता पुरुश्चन्द्रेण यातम् । अभि वां विश्वा नियुतः सचन्ते स्पार्हया श्रिया तन्वा शुभाना ॥
7.72.e: COME, O Nāsatyas, on your car resplendent, rich in abundant wealth of kine and horses.  As harnessed steeds, all our laudations follow you whose forms shine with most delightful beauty.

7.72.d: आ नो देवेभिरुप यातमर्वाक्सजोषसा नासत्या रथेन । युवोर्हि नः सख्या पित्र्याणि समानो बन्धुरुत तस्य वित्तम् ॥
7.72.e: Come with the Gods associate, come ye hither to us, Nāsatyas, with your car accordant.  'Twixt you and us there is ancestral friendship and common kin: remember and regard it.

7.72.d: उदु स्तोमासो अश्विनोरबुध्रञ्जामि ब्रह्माण्युषसश्च देवीः । आविवासन्रोदसी धिष्ण्येमे अच्छा विप्रो नासत्या विवक्ति ॥
7.72.e: Awakened are the songs that praise the Aśvins, the kindred prayers and the Celestial Mornings.  Inviting those we long for, Earth and Heaven, the singer calleth these Nāsatyas hither.

7.72.d: वि चेदुच्छन्त्यश्विना उषासः प्र वां ब्रह्माणि कारवो भरन्ते । ऊर्ध्वं भानुं सविता देवो अश्रेद्बृहदग्नयः समिधा जरन्ते ॥
7.72.e: What time the Dawns break forth in light, O Aśvins, to you the poets offer their devotions.  God Savitar hath sent aloft his splendour, and fires sing praises with the kindled fuel.

7.72.d: आ पश्चातान्नासत्या पुरस्तादाश्विना यातमधरादुदक्तात् । आ विश्वतः पाञ्चजन्येन राया यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.72.e: Come from the west, come from the cast, Nāsatyas, come, Aśvins, from below and from above us.  Bring wealth from all sides for the Fivefold People. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.73.d: अतारिष्म तमसस्पारमस्य प्रति स्तोमं देवयन्तो दधानाः । पुरुदंसा पुरुतमा पुराजामर्त्या हवते अश्विना गीः ॥
7.73.e: WE have o’erpassed the limit of this darkness while, worshipping the Gods, we sang their praises.  The song invoketh both Immortal Aśvins far-reaching, born of old, great WonderWorkers.

7.73.d: न्यु प्रियो मनुषः सादि होता नासत्या यो यजते वन्दते च । अश्नीतं मध्वो अश्विना उपाक आ वां वोचे विदथेषु प्रयस्वान् ॥
7.73.e: And, O Nāsatyas, man's dear Priest is seated, who brings to sacrifice and offers worship,  Be near and taste the pleasant juice, O Aśvins: with food, I call you to the sacrifices.

7.73.d: अहेम यज्ञं पथामुराणा इमां सुवृक्तिं वृषणा जुषेथाम् । श्रुष्टीवेव प्रेषितो वामबोधि प्रति स्तोमैर्जरमाणो वसिष्ठः ॥
7.73.e: We choosing you, have let our worship follow its course: ye Steers, accept this hymn with favour.  Obeying you as your appointed servant, Vasiṣṭha singing hath with lauds aroused you.

7.73.d: उप त्या वह्नी गमतो विशं नो रक्षोहणा सम्भृता वीळुपाणी । समन्धांस्यग्मत मत्सराणि मा नो मर्धिष्टमा गतं शिवेन ॥
7.73.e: And these Two Priests come nigh unto our people, united, demon-slayers, mighty-handed.  The juices that exhilarate are mingled. Injure us not, but come with happy fortune.

7.73.d: आ पश्चातान्नासत्या पुरस्तादाश्विना यातमधरादुदक्तात् । आ विश्वतः पाञ्चजन्येन राया यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.73.e: Come from the west, come from the cast, Nāsatyas, come, Aśvins, from below and from above us.  Bring wealth from all sides for the Fivefold People. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.74.d: इमा उ वां दिविष्टय उस्रा हवन्ते अश्विना । अयं वामह्वेऽवसे शचीवसू विशंविशं हि गच्छथः ॥
7.74.e: THESE morning sacrifices call you, Aśvins, at the break of day.  For help have I invoked you rich in power and might: for, house by house ye visit all.

7.74.d: युवं चित्रं ददथुर्भोजनं नरा चोदेथां सूनृतावते । अर्वाग्रथं समनसा नि यच्छतं पिबतं सोम्यं मधु ॥
7.74.e: O Heroes, ye bestow wonderful nourishment. send it to him whose songs are sweet  Accordant, both of you, drive your car down to us, and drink the savoury Soma juice.

7.74.d: आ यातमुप भूषतं मध्वः पिबतमश्विना । दुग्धं पयो वृषणा जेन्यावसू मा नो मर्धिष्टमा गतम् ॥
7.74.e: Approach ye and be near to us. drink, O ye Aśvins, of the meath.  Draw forth the milk, ye Mighty, rich in genuine wealth: injure us not, and come to us.

7.74.d: अश्वासो ये वामुप दाशुषो गृहं युवां दीयन्ति बिभ्रतः । मक्षूयुभिर्नरा हयेभिरश्विना देवा यातमस्मयू ॥
7.74.e: The horses that convey you in their rapid flight down to the worshipper's abode,  With these your speedy coursers, Heroes, Aśvins, come, ye Gods, come well-inclined to us.

7.74.d: अधा ह यन्तो अश्विना पृक्षः सचन्त सूरयः । ता यंसतो मघवद्भ्यो ध्रुवं यशश्छर्दिरस्मभ्यं नासत्या ॥
7.74.e: Yea, verily, our princes seek the Aśvins in pursuit of food.  These shall give lasting glory to our liberal lords, and, both Nāsatyas, shelter us.

7.74.d: प्र ये ययुरवृकासो रथा इव नृपातारो जनानाम् । उत स्वेन शवसा शूशुवुर्नर उत क्षियन्ति सुक्षितिम् ॥
7.74.e: Those who have led the way, like cars, offending none, those who are guardians of the men-  Also through their own might the heroes have grown strong, and dwell in safe and happy homes.

7.75.d: व्यु१षा आवो दिविजा ऋतेनाविष्कृण्वाना महिमानमागात् । अप द्रुहस्तम आवरजुष्टमङ्गिरस्तमा पथ्या अजीगः ॥
7.75.e: BORN in the heavens the Dawn hath flushed, and showing her majesty is come as Law ordaineth.  She hath uncovered fiends and hateful darkness; best of Aṅgirases, hath waked the pathways.

7.75.d: महे नो अद्य सुविताय बोध्युषो महे सौभगाय प्र यन्धि । चित्रं रयिं यशसं धेह्यस्मे देवि मर्तेषु मानुषि श्रवस्युम् ॥
7.75.e: Rouse us this day to high and happy fortune: to great felicity, O Dawn, promote us.  Vouchsafe us manifold and splendid riches, famed among mortals, man-befriending Goddess!

7.75.d: एते त्ये भानवो दर्शतायाश्चित्रा उषसो अमृतास आगुः । जनयन्तो दैव्यानि व्रतान्यापृणन्तो अन्तरिक्षा व्यस्थुः ॥
7.75.e: See, lovely Morning's everlasting splendours, bright with their varied colours, have approached us.  Filling the region of mid-air, producing the rites of holy worship, they have mounted.

7.75.d: एषा स्या युजाना पराकात्पञ्च क्षितीः परि सद्यो जिगाति । अभिपश्यन्ती वयुना जनानां दिवो दुहिता भुवनस्य पत्नी ॥
7.75.e: She yokes her chariot far away, and swiftly visits the lands where the Five Tribes are settled,  Looking upon the works and ways of mortals, Daughter of Heaven, the world's Imperial Lady.

7.75.d: वाजिनीवती सूर्यस्य योषा चित्रामघा राय ईशे वसूनाम् । ऋषिष्टुता जरयन्ती मघोन्युषा उच्छति वह्निभिर्गृणाना ॥
7.75.e: She who is rich in spoil, the Spouse of Sūrya, wondrously opulent, rules all wealth and treasures.  Consumer of our youth, the seers extol her: lauded by priests rich Dawn shines out refulgent.

7.75.d: प्रति द्युतानामरुषासो अश्वाश्चित्रा अदृश्रन्नुषसं वहन्तः । याति शुभ्रा विश्वपिशा रथेन दधाति रत्नं विधते जनाय ॥
7.75.e: Apparent are the steeds of varied colour, the red steeds carrying resplendent Morning.  On her all-lovely car she comes, the Fair One, and brings rich treasure for her faithful servant.

7.75.d: सत्या सत्येभिर्महती महद्भिर्देवी देवेभिर्यजता यजत्रैः । रुजद्दृळ्हानि दददुस्रियाणां प्रति गाव उषसं वावशन्त ॥
7.75.e: True with the True and Mighty with the Mighty, with Gods a Goddess, Holy with the Holy,  She brake strong fences down and gave the cattle: the kine were lowing as they greeted Morning.

7.75.d: नू नो गोमद्वीरवद्धेहि रत्नमुषो अश्वावत्पुरुभोजो अस्मे । मा नो बर्हिः पुरुषता निदे कर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.75.e: O Dawn, now give us wealth in kine and heroes, and horses, fraught with manifold enjoyment.  Protect our sacred grass from man's reproaches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.76.d: उदु ज्योतिरमृतं विश्वजन्यं विश्वानरः सविता देवो अश्रेत् । क्रत्वा देवानामजनिष्ट चक्षुराविरकर्भुवनं विश्वमुषाः ॥
7.76.e: SAVITAR God of all men hath sent upward his light, designed for all mankind, immortal.  Through the Gods’ power that Eye was first created. Dawn hath made all the universe apparent.

7.76.d: प्र मे पन्था देवयाना अदृश्रन्नमर्धन्तो वसुभिरिष्कृतासः । अभूदु केतुरुषसः पुरस्तात्प्रतीच्यागादधि हर्म्येभ्यः ॥
7.76.e: I see the paths which Gods are wont to travel, innocuous paths made ready by the Vasus.  Eastward the flag of Dawn hath been uplifted; she hath come hither o’er the tops of houses.

7.76.d: तानीदहानि बहुलान्यासन्या प्राचीनमुदिता सूर्यस्य । यतः परि जार इवाचरन्त्युषो ददृक्षे न पुनर्यतीव ॥
7.76.e: Great is, in truth, the number of the Mornings which were aforetime at the Sun's uprising.  Since thou, O Dawn, hast been beheld repairing as to thy love, as one no more to leave him.

7.76.d: त इद्देवानां सधमाद आसन्नृतावानः कवयः पूर्व्यासः । गूळ्हं ज्योतिः पितरो अन्वविन्दन्त्सत्यमन्त्रा अजनयन्नुषासम् ॥
7.76.e: They were the Gods’ companions at the banquet, the ancient sages true to Law Eternal.  The Fathers found the light that lay in darkness, and with effectual words begat the Morning.

7.76.d: समान ऊर्वे अधि संगतासः सं जानते न यतन्ते मिथस्ते । ते देवानां न मिनन्ति व्रतान्यमर्धन्तो वसुभिर्यादमानाः ॥
7.76.e: Meeting together in the same enclosure, they strive not, ofone mind, one with another.  They never break the Gods’ eternal statutes, and injure none, in rivalry with Vasus.

7.76.d: प्रति त्वा स्तोमैरीळते वसिष्ठा उषर्बुधः सुभगे तुष्टुवांसः । गवां नेत्री वाजपत्नी न उच्छोषः सुजाते प्रथमा जरस्व ॥
7.76.e: Extolling thee, Blest Goddess, the Vasisthas, awake at early mom, with lauds implore thee.  Leader of kine and Queen of all that strengthens, shine, come as first to us, O high-born Morning.

7.76.d: एषा नेत्री राधसः सूनृतानामुषा उच्छन्ती रिभ्यते वसिष्ठैः । दीर्घश्रुतं रयिमस्मे दधाना यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.76.e: She bringeth bounty and sweet charm of voices. The flushing Dawn is sung by the Vasisthas,  Giving us riches famed to distant places. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.77.d: उपो रुरुचे युवतिर्न योषा विश्वं जीवं प्रसुवन्ती चरायै । अभूदग्निः समिधे मानुषाणामकर्ज्योतिर्बाधमाना तमांसि ॥
7.77.e: SHE hath shone brightly like a youthful woman, stirring to motion every living creature.  Agni hath come to feed on mortal? fuel. She hath made light and chased away the darkness.

7.77.d: विश्वं प्रतीची सप्रथा उदस्थाद्रुशद्वासो बिभ्रती शुक्रमश्वैत् । हिरण्यवर्णा सुदृशीकसंदृग्गवां माता नेत्र्यह्नामरोचि ॥
7.77.e: Turned to this All, far-spreading, she hath risen and shone in brightness with white robes about her.  She hath beamed forth lovely with golden colours, Mother of kine, Guide of the days she bringeth.

7.77.d: देवानां चक्षुः सुभगा वहन्ती श्वेतं नयन्ती सुदृशीकमश्वम् । उषा अदर्शि रश्मिभिर्व्यक्ता चित्रामघा विश्वमनु प्रभूता ॥
7.77.e: Bearing the Gods’ own Eye, auspicious Lady, leading her Courser white and fair to look on,  Distinguished by her bean-is Dawn shines apparent, come forth to all the world with wondrous treasure.

7.77.d: अन्तिवामा दूरे अमित्रमुच्छोर्वीं गव्यूतिमभयं कृधी नः । यावय द्वेष आ भरा वसूनि चोदय राधो गृणते मघोनि ॥
7.77.e: Draw nigh with wealth and dawn away the foeman: prepare for us wide pasture free from danger.  Drive away those who hate us, bring us riches: pour bounty, opulent Lady, on the singer.

7.77.d: अस्मे श्रेष्ठेभिर्भानुभिर्वि भाह्युषो देवि प्रतिरन्ती न आयुः । इषं च नो दधती विश्ववारे गोमदश्वावद्रथवच्च राधः ॥
7.77.e: Send thy most excellent beams to shine and light us, giving us lengthened days, O Dawn, O Goddess,  Granting us food, thou who hast all things precious, and bounty rich in chariots, kine, and horses.

7.77.d: यां त्वा दिवो दुहितर्वर्धयन्त्युषः सुजाते मतिभिर्वसिष्ठाः । सास्मासु धा रयिमृष्वं बृहन्तं यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.77.e: O Uṣas, nobly-born, Daughter of Heaven, whom the Vasisthas with their hymns make mighty,  Bestow thou on us vast and glorious riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.78.d: प्रति केतवः प्रथमा अदृश्रन्नूर्ध्वा अस्या अञ्जयो वि श्रयन्ते । उषो अर्वाचा बृहता रथेन ज्योतिष्मता वाममस्मभ्यं वक्षि ॥
7.78.e: WE have beheld her earliest lights approaching: her many glories part, on high, asunder.  On car sublime, refulgent, wending hither, O Uṣas, bring the Wealth that makes us happy.

7.78.d: प्रति षीमग्निर्जरते समिद्धः प्रति विप्रासो मतिभिर्गृणन्तः । उषा याति ज्योतिषा बाधमाना विश्वा तमांसि दुरिताप देवी ॥
7.78.e: The fire well-kindIed sings aloud to greet her, and with their hymns the priests are chaming welcome.  Uṣas approaches in her splendour, driving all evil darkness far away, the Goddess.

7.78.d: एता उ त्याः प्रत्यदृश्रन्पुरस्ताज्ज्योतिर्यच्छन्तीरुषसो विभातीः । अजीजनन्त्सूर्यं यज्ञमग्निमपाचीनं तमो अगादजुष्टम् ॥
7.78.e: Apparent eastward are those lights of Morning, sending out lustre, as they rise, around them.  She hath brought forth Sun, sacrifice, and Agni, and far away hath fled detested darkness.

7.78.d: अचेति दिवो दुहिता मघोनी विश्वे पश्यन्त्युषसं विभातीम् । आस्थाद्रथं स्वधया युज्यमानमा यमश्वासः सुयुजो वहन्ति ॥
7.78.e: Rich Daughter of the Sky, we all behold her, yea, all men look on Dawn as she is breaking.  fler car that moves self-harnessed hath she mounted, the car drawn onward by her well-yoked horses.

7.78.d: प्रति त्वाद्य सुमनसो बुधन्तास्माकासो मघवानो वयं च । तिल्विलायध्वमुषसो विभातीर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.78.e: Inspired with loving thoughts this day to greet thee, we and our wealthy nobles have awakened.  Show yourselves fruitful, Dawns, as ye are rising. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.79.d: व्यु१षा आवः पथ्या३ जनानां पञ्च क्षितीर्मानुषीर्बोधयन्ती । सुसंदृग्भिरुक्षभिर्भानुमश्रेद्वि सूर्यो रोदसी चक्षसावः ॥
7.79.e: ROUSING the lands where men's Five Tribes are settled, Dawn hath disclosed the pathways of the people.  She hath sent out her sheen with beauteous oxen. The Sun with light hath opened earth and heaven.

7.79.d: व्यञ्जते दिवो अन्तेष्वक्तून्विशो न युक्ता उषसो यतन्ते । सं ते गावस्तम आ वर्तयन्ति ज्योतिर्यच्छन्ति सवितेव बाहू ॥
7.79.e: They paint their bright rays on the sky's far limits. the Dawns come on like tribes arrayed for battle.  Thy cattle, closely shutting up the darkness, as Savitar spreads his arms, give forth their lustre.

7.79.d: अभूदुषा इन्द्रतमा मघोन्यजीजनत्सुविताय श्रवांसि । वि दिवो देवी दुहिता दधात्यङ्गिरस्तमा सुकृते वसूनि ॥
7.79.e: Wealthy, most like to Indra, Dawn hath risen, and brought forth lauds that shall promote our welfare.  Daughter of Heaven, a Goddess, she distributes, best of Aṅgirases, treasures to the pious.

7.79.d: तावदुषो राधो अस्मभ्यं रास्व यावत्स्तोतृभ्यो अरदो गृणाना । यां त्वा जज्ञुर्वृषभस्या रवेण वि दृळ्हस्य दुरो अद्रेरौर्णोः ॥
7.79.e: Bestow on us, O Dawn, that ample bounty which thou didst send to those who sang thy praises;  Thou whom with bellowings of a bull they quickened: thou didst unbar the firm-set mountain's portals.

7.79.d: देवंदेवं राधसे चोदयन्त्यस्मद्र्यक्सूनृता ईरयन्ती । व्युच्छन्ती नः सनये धियो धा यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.79.e: Impelling every God to grant his bounty sending to us the charm of pleasant voices,  Vouchsafe us thoughts, for profit, as thou breakest. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.80.d: प्रति स्तोमेभिरुषसं वसिष्ठा गीर्भिर्विप्रासः प्रथमा अबुध्रन् । विवर्तयन्तीं रजसी समन्ते आविष्कृण्वतीं भुवनानि विश्वा ॥
7.80.e: THE priests, Vasisthas, are the first awakened to welcome Uṣas with their songs and praises,  Who makes surrounding regions part asunder,and shows apparent all existing creatures.

7.80.d: एषा स्या नव्यमायुर्दधाना गूढ्वी तमो ज्योतिषोषा अबोधि । अग्र एति युवतिरह्रयाणा प्राचिकितत्सूर्यं यज्ञमग्निम् ॥
7.80.e: Giving fresh life when she hath hid the darkness, this Dawn hath wakened there with new-born lustre.  Youthful and unrestrained she cometh forward: she hath turned thoughts to Sun and fire and worship.

7.80.d: अश्वावतीर्गोमतीर्न उषासो वीरवतीः सदमुच्छन्तु भद्राः । घृतं दुहाना विश्वतः प्रपीता यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.80.e: May blessed Mornings shine on us for ever, with wealth of kine, of horses, and of heroes,  Streaming with all abundance, pouring fatness. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.81.d: प्रत्यु अदर्श्यायत्यु१च्छन्ती दुहिता दिवः । अपो महि व्ययति चक्षसे तमो ज्योतिष्कृणोति सूनरी ॥
7.81.e: ADVANCING, sending forth her rays, the Daughter of the Sky is seen.  Uncovering, that we may see, the mighty gloom, the friendly Lady makes the light.

7.81.d: उदुस्रियाः सृजते सूर्यः सचाँ उद्यन्नक्षत्रमर्चिवत् । तवेदुषो व्युषि सूर्यस्य च सं भक्तेन गमेमहि ॥
7.81.e: The Sun ascending, the refulgent Star, pours down his beams together with the Dawn.  O Dawn, at thine arising, and the Sun's, may we attain the share allotted us.

7.81.d: प्रति त्वा दुहितर्दिव उषो जीरा अभुत्स्महि । या वहसि पुरु स्पार्हं वनन्वति रत्नं न दाशुषे मयः ॥
7.81.e: Promptly we woke to welcome thee, O Uṣas, Daughter of the Sky,  Thee, Bounteous One, who bringest all we long to have, and to the offerer health and wealth.

7.81.d: उच्छन्ती या कृणोषि मंहना महि प्रख्यै देवि स्वर्दृशे । तस्यास्ते रत्नभाज ईमहे वयं स्याम मातुर्न सूनवः ॥
7.81.e: Thou, dawning, workest fain to light the great world, yea, heaven, Goddess! that it may be seen.  We yearn to be thine own, Dealer of Wealth: may we be to this Mother like her sons.

7.81.d: तच्चित्रं राध आ भरोषो यद्दीर्घश्रुत्तमम् । यत्ते दिवो दुहितर्मर्तभोजनं तद्रास्व भुनजामहै ॥
7.81.e: Bring us that wondrous bounty, Dawn, that shall be famed most far away.  What, Child of Heaven, thou hast of nourishment for man, bestow thou on us to enjoy.

7.81.d: श्रवः सूरिभ्यो अमृतं वसुत्वनं वाजाँ अस्मभ्यं गोमतः । चोदयित्री मघोनः सूनृतावत्युषा उच्छदप स्रिधः ॥
7.81.e: Give to our princes opulence and immortal fame, and strength in herds of kine to us.  May she who prompts the wealthy, Lady of sweet strains, may Uṣas dawn our foes away.

7.82.d: इन्द्रावरुणा युवमध्वराय नो विशे जनाय महि शर्म यच्छतम् । दीर्घप्रयज्युमति यो वनुष्यति वयं जयेम पृतनासु दूढ्यः ॥
7.82.e: GRANT us your strong protection, IndraVaruṇa, our people, and our family, for sacrifice.  May we subdue in fight our evil-hearted foes, him who attacks the man steadfast in lengthened rites.

7.82.d: सम्राळन्यः स्वराळन्य उच्यते वां महान्ताविन्द्रावरुणा महावसू । विश्वे देवासः परमे व्योमनि सं वामोजो वृषणा सं बलं दधुः ॥
7.82.e: O Indra-Varuṇa, mighty and very rich One of you is called Monarch and One Autocrat.  All Gods in the most lofty region of the air have, O ye Steers, combined all power and might in you.

7.82.d: अन्वपां खान्यतृन्तमोजसा सूर्यमैरयतं दिवि प्रभुम् । इन्द्रावरुणा मदे अस्य मायिनोऽपिन्वतमपितः पिन्वतं धियः ॥
7.82.e: Ye with your strength have pierced the fountains of the floods: the Sun have ye brought forward as the Lord in heaven.  Cheered by this magic draught ye, Indra-Varuṇa, made the dry places stream, made songs of praise flow forth.

7.82.d: युवामिद्युत्सु पृतनासु वह्नयो युवां क्षेमस्य प्रसवे मितज्ञवः । ईशाना वस्व उभयस्य कारव इन्द्रावरुणा सुहवा हवामहे ॥
7.82.e: In battels and in frays we ministering priests, kneeling upon our knees for furtherance of our weal,  Invoke you, only you, the Lords of twofold wealth, you prompt to hear, we bards, O Indra-Varuṇa.

7.82.d: इन्द्रावरुणा यदिमानि चक्रथुर्विश्वा जातानि भुवनस्य मज्मना । क्षेमेण मित्रो वरुणं दुवस्यति मरुद्भिरुग्रः शुभमन्य ईयते ॥
7.82.e: O Indra-Varuṇa, as ye created all these creatures of the world by your surpassing might,  In peace and quiet Mitra waits on Varuṇa, the Other, awful, with the Maruis seeks renown.

7.82.d: महे शुल्काय वरुणस्य नु त्विष ओजो मिमाते ध्रुवमस्य यत्स्वम् । अजामिमन्यः श्नथयन्तमातिरद्दभ्रेभिरन्यः प्र वृणोति भूयसः ॥
7.82.e: That Varuṇa's high worth may shine preeminent, these Twain have measured each his proper power and might.  The One subdueth the destructive enemy; the Other with a few furthereth many a man.

7.82.d: न तमंहो न दुरितानि मर्त्यमिन्द्रावरुणा न तपः कुतश्चन । यस्य देवा गच्छथो वीथो अध्वरं न तं मर्तस्य नशते परिह्वृतिः ॥
7.82.e: No trouble, no misfortune, Indra-Varuṇa, no woe from any side assails the mortal man  Whose sacrifice, O Gods, ye visit and enjoy: ne’er doth the crafty guile of mortal injure him.

7.82.d: अर्वाङ्नरा दैव्येनावसा गतं शृणुतं हवं यदि मे जुजोषथः । युवोर्हि सख्यमुत वा यदाप्यं मार्डीकमिन्द्रावरुणा नि यच्छतम् ॥
7.82.e: With your divine protection, Heroes, come to us: mine invncation hear, if ye be pleased therewith.  Bestow ye upon us, O Indra-Varuṇa, your friendship and your kinship and your favouring grace.

7.82.d: अस्माकमिन्द्रावरुणा भरेभरे पुरोयोधा भवतं कृष्ट्योजसा । यद्वां हवन्त उभये अध स्पृधि नरस्तोकस्य तनयस्य सातिषु ॥
7.82.e: In battle after battle, Indra-Varuṇa, be ye our Champions, ye who are the peoples' strength,  When both opposing bands invoke you for the fight, and men that they may gain offspring and progeny.

7.82.d: अस्मे इन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा द्युम्नं यच्छन्तु महि शर्म सप्रथः । अवध्रं ज्योतिरदितेर्ऋतावृधो देवस्य श्लोकं सवितुर्मनामहे ॥
7.82.e: May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman vouchsafe us glory and great shelter spreading far.  We think of the beneficent light of Aditi, and Savitar's song of praise, the God who strengthens Law.

7.83.d: युवां नरा पश्यमानास आप्यं प्राचा गव्यन्तः पृथुपर्शवो ययुः । दासा च वृत्रा हतमार्याणि च सुदासमिन्द्रावरुणावसावतम् ॥
7.83.e: LOOKING to you and your alliance, O ye Men, armed with broad axes they went forward, fain for spoil.  Ye smote and slew his Dāsa and his Āryan enemies, and helped Sudās with favour, Indra-Varuṇa.

7.83.d: यत्रा नरः समयन्ते कृतध्वजो यस्मिन्नाजा भवति किं चन प्रियम् । यत्रा भयन्ते भुवना स्वर्दृशस्तत्रा न इन्द्रावरुणाधि वोचतम् ॥
7.83.e: Where heroes come together with their banners raised, in the encounter where is naught for us to love,  Where all things that behold the light are terrified, there did ye comfort us, O Indra-Varuṇa.

7.83.d: सं भूम्या अन्ता ध्वसिरा अदृक्षतेन्द्रावरुणा दिवि घोष आरुहत् । अस्थुर्जनानामुप मामरातयोऽर्वागवसा हवनश्रुता गतम् ॥
7.83.e: The boundaries of earth were seen all dark with dust: O Indra-Varuṇa, the shout went up to heaven.  The enmities of the people compassed me about. Ye heard my calling and ye came to me with help.

7.83.d: इन्द्रावरुणा वधनाभिरप्रति भेदं वन्वन्ता प्र सुदासमावतम् । ब्रह्माण्येषां शृणुतं हवीमनि सत्या तृत्सूनामभवत्पुरोहितिः ॥
7.83.e: With your resistless weapons, Indra-Varuṇa, ye conquered Bheda and ye gave Sudās your aid.  Ye heard the prayers of these amid the cries of war: effectual was the service of the Trtsus' priest.

7.83.d: इन्द्रावरुणावभ्या तपन्ति माघान्यर्यो वनुषामरातयः । युवं हि वस्व उभयस्य राजथोऽध स्मा नोऽवतं पार्ये दिवि ॥
7.83.e: O Indra-Varuṇa, the wickedness of foes and mine assailants' hatred sorely trouble me.  Ye Twain are Lords of riches both of earth and heaven: so grant to us your aid on the decisive day.

7.83.d: युवां हवन्त उभयास आजिष्विन्द्रं च वस्वो वरुणं च सातये । यत्र राजभिर्दशभिर्निबाधितं प्र सुदासमावतं तृत्सुभिः सह ॥
7.83.e: The men of both the hosts invoked you in the fight, Indra and Varuṇa, that they might win the wealth,  What time ye helped Sudās, with all the Trtsu folk, when the Ten Kings had pressed him down in their attack.

7.83.d: दश राजानः समिता अयज्यवः सुदासमिन्द्रावरुणा न युयुधुः । सत्या नृणामद्मसदामुपस्तुतिर्देवा एषामभवन्देवहूतिषु ॥
7.83.e: Ten Kings who worshipped not, O Indra-Varuṇa, confederate, in war prevailed not o’er Sudās.  True was the boast of heroes sitting at the feast: so at their invocations Gods were on their side.

7.83.d: दाशराज्ञे परियत्ताय विश्वतः सुदास इन्द्रावरुणावशिक्षतम् । श्वित्यञ्चो यत्र नमसा कपर्दिनो धिया धीवन्तो असपन्त तृत्सवः ॥
7.83.e: O Indra-Varuṇa, ye gave Sudās your aid when the Ten Kings in battle compassed him about,  There where the white-robed Trtsus with their braided hair, skilled in song worshipped you with homage and with hymn.

7.83.d: वृत्राण्यन्यः समिथेषु जिघ्नते व्रतान्यन्यो अभि रक्षते सदा । हवामहे वां वृषणा सुवृक्तिभिरस्मे इन्द्रावरुणा शर्म यच्छतम् ॥
7.83.e: One of you Twain destroys the Vṛtras in the fight, the Other evermore maintains his holy Laws.  We call on you, ye Mighty, with our hymns of praise. Vouchsafe us your protection, Indra-Varuṇa.

7.83.d: अस्मे इन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा द्युम्नं यच्छन्तु महि शर्म सप्रथः । अवध्रं ज्योतिरदितेर्ऋतावृधो देवस्य श्लोकं सवितुर्मनामहे ॥
7.83.e: May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman vouchsafe us glory and great shelter spreading far.  We think of the beneficent light of Aditi, and Savitar's song of praise, the God who strengthens Law.

7.84.d: आ वां राजानावध्वरे ववृत्यां हव्येभिरिन्द्रावरुणा नमोभिः । प्र वां घृताची बाह्वोर्दधाना परि त्मना विषुरूपा जिगाति ॥
7.84.e: KINGS, Indra-Varuṇa, I would turn you hither to this our sacrifice with gifts and homage.  Held in both arms the ladle, dropping fatness, goes of itself to you whose forms are varied.

7.84.d: युवो राष्ट्रं बृहदिन्वति द्यौर्यौ सेतृभिररज्जुभिः सिनीथः । परि नो हेळो वरुणस्य वृज्या उरुं न इन्द्रः कृणवदु लोकम् ॥
7.84.e: Dyaus quickens and promotes your high dominion who bind with bonds not wrought of rope or cordage.  Far from us still be Varuṇa's displeasure may Indra give us spacious room to dwell in.

7.84.d: कृतं नो यज्ञं विदथेषु चारुं कृतं ब्रह्माणि सूरिषु प्रशस्ता । उपो रयिर्देवजूतो न एतु प्र णः स्पार्हाभिरूतिभिस्तिरेतम् ॥
7.84.e: Make ye our sacrifice fair amid the assemblies: make ye our prayers approved among our princes.  May God-sent riches come for our possession: further ye us with your delightful succours.

7.84.d: अस्मे इन्द्रावरुणा विश्ववारं रयिं धत्तं वसुमन्तं पुरुक्षुम् । प्र य आदित्यो अनृता मिनात्यमिता शूरो दयते वसूनि ॥
7.84.e: O Indra-Varuṇa, vouchsafe us riches with store of treasure, food, and every blessing;  For the Āditya, banisher of falsehood, the Hero, dealeth wealth in boundless plenty.

7.84.d: इयमिन्द्रं वरुणमष्ट मे गीः प्रावत्तोके तनये तूतुजाना । सुरत्नासो देववीतिं गमेम यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.84.e: May this my song reach Varuṇa and Indra, and, strongly urging, win me sons and offspring.  To the Gods’ banquet may we go with riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.85.d: पुनीषे वामरक्षसं मनीषां सोममिन्द्राय वरुणाय जुह्वत् । घृतप्रतीकामुषसं न देवीं ता नो यामन्नुरुष्यतामभीके ॥
7.85.e: FOR you I deck a harmless hymn, presenting the Soma juice to Varuṇa and Indra-  A hymn that shines like heavenly Dawn with fatness. May they be near us on the march and guard us.

7.85.d: स्पर्धन्ते वा उ देवहूये अत्र येषु ध्वजेषु दिद्यवः पतन्ति । युवं ताँ इन्द्रावरुणावमित्रान्हतं पराचः शर्वा विषूचः ॥
7.85.e: Here where the arrows fall amid the banners both hosts invoke the Gods in emulation.  O Indra-Varuṇa, smite back those-our foemen,yea, smite them withyour shaft to every quarter.

7.85.d: आपश्चिद्धि स्वयशसः सदःसु देवीरिन्द्रं वरुणं देवता धुः । कृष्टीरन्यो धारयति प्रविक्ता वृत्राण्यन्यो अप्रतीनि हन्ति ॥
7.85.e: Self-lucid in their seats, e’en heavenly Waters endowed with Godhead Varuṇa and Indra.  One of these holds the folk distinct and sundered, the Other smites and slays resistless foemen.

7.85.d: स सुक्रतुर्ऋतचिदस्तु होता य आदित्य शवसा वां नमस्वान् । आववर्तदवसे वां हविष्मानसदित्स सुविताय प्रयस्वान् ॥
7.85.e: Wise be the priest and skilled in Law Eternal, who with his sacred gifts and oration.  Brings you to aid us with your might, Ādityas: let him have viands to promote his welfare.

7.85.d: इयमिन्द्रं वरुणमष्ट मे गीः प्रावत्तोके तनये तूतुजाना । सुरत्नासो देववीतिं गमेम यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.85.e: May this my song reach Varuṇa and Indra, and, strongly urging, win me sons and offspring.  To the Gods’ banquet may we go with riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods with blessings.

7.86.d: धीरा त्वस्य महिना जनूंषि वि यस्तस्तम्भ रोदसी चिदुर्वी । प्र नाकमृष्वं नुनुदे बृहन्तं द्विता नक्षत्रं पप्रथच्च भूम ॥
7.86.e: WISE, verily, are creatures through his greatness who stayed ever, spacious heaven and earth asunder;  Who urged the high and mighty sky to motion, the Star of old, and spread the earth before him.

7.86.d: उत स्वया तन्वा३ सं वदे तत्कदा न्व१न्तर्वरुणे भुवानि । किं मे हव्यमहृणानो जुषेत कदा मृळीकं सुमना अभि ख्यम् ॥
7.86.e: With mine own heart I commune on the question how Varuṇa and I may be united.  What gift of mine will he accept unangered? When may I calmly look and find him gracious?

7.86.d: पृच्छे तदेनो वरुण दिदृक्षूपो एमि चिकितुषो विपृच्छम् । समानमिन्मे कवयश्चिदाहुरयं ह तुभ्यं वरुणो हृणीते ॥
7.86.e: Fain to know this is my sin I question others: I seek the wise, O Varuṇa, and ask them.  This one same answer even the sages gave me, "Surely this Varuṇa is angry with thee."

7.86.d: किमाग आस वरुण ज्येष्ठं यत्स्तोतारं जिघांससि सखायम् । प्र तन्मे वोचो दूळभ स्वधावोऽव त्वानेना नमसा तुर इयाम् ॥
7.86.e: What, Varuṇa, hath been my chief transgression, that thou wouldst slay the friend who sings thy praises?  Tell me, Unconquerable Lord, and quickly sinless will I approach thee with mine homage.

7.86.d: अव द्रुग्धानि पित्र्या सृजा नोऽव या वयं चकृमा तनूभिः । अव राजन्पशुतृपं न तायुं सृजा वत्सं न दाम्नो वसिष्ठम् ॥
7.86.e: Free us from sins committed by our fathers, from those wherein we have ourselves offended.  O King, loose, like a thief who feeds the cattle, as from the cord a calf, set free Vasiṣṭha.

7.86.d: न स स्वो दक्षो वरुण ध्रुतिः सा सुरा मन्युर्विभीदको अचित्तिः । अस्ति ज्यायान्कनीयस उपारे स्वप्नश्चनेदनृतस्य प्रयोता ॥
7.86.e: Not our own will betrayed us, but seduction, thoughtlessness, Varuṇa wine, dice, or anger.  The old is near to lead astray the younger: even sleep removeth not all evil-doing.

7.86.d: अरं दासो न मीळ्हुषे कराण्यहं देवाय भूर्णयेऽनागाः । अचेतयदचितो देवो अर्यो गृत्सं राये कवितरो जुनाति ॥
7.86.e: Slavelike may I do service to the Bounteous, serve, free from sin, the God inclined to anger.  This gentle Lord gives wisdom to the simple: the wiser God leads on the wise to riches.

7.86.d: अयं सु तुभ्यं वरुण स्वधावो हृदि स्तोम उपश्रितश्चिदस्तु । शं नः क्षेमे शमु योगे नो अस्तु यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.86.e: O Lord, O Varuṇa, may this laudation come close to thee and lie within thy spirit.  May it be well with us in rest and labour. Preserve us ever-more, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.87.d: रदत्पथो वरुणः सूर्याय प्रार्णांसि समुद्रिया नदीनाम् । सर्गो न सृष्टो अर्वतीर्ऋतायञ्चकार महीरवनीरहभ्यः ॥
7.87.e: VARUNA cut a pathway out for Sūrya, and led the watery floods of rivers onward.  The Mares, as in a race, speed on in order. He made great channels for the days to follow.

7.87.d: आत्मा ते वातो रज आ नवीनोत्पशुर्न भूर्णिर्यवसे ससवान् । अन्तर्मही बृहती रोदसीमे विश्वा ते धाम वरुण प्रियाणि ॥
7.87.e: The wind, thy breath, hath sounded through the region like a wild beast that seeks his food in pastures.  Within these two, exalted Earth and Heaven, O Varuṇa, are all the forms thou lovest.

7.87.d: परि स्पशो वरुणस्य स्मदिष्टा उभे पश्यन्ति रोदसी सुमेके । ऋतावानः कवयो यज्ञधीराः प्रचेतसो य इषयन्त मन्म ॥
7.87.e: Varuṇa's spies, sent forth upon their errand, survey the two world-halves well formed and fashioned.  Wise are they, holy, skilled in sacrifices, the furtherers of the praise-songs of the prudent.

7.87.d: उवाच मे वरुणो मेधिराय त्रिः सप्त नामाघ्न्या बिभर्ति । विद्वान्पदस्य गुह्या न वोचद्युगाय विप्र उपराय शिक्षन् ॥
7.87.e: To me who understand hath Varuṇa spoken, the names borne by the Cow are three times seven.  The sapient God, knowing the place's secret, shall speak as ’twere to teach the race that cometh.

7.87.d: तिस्रो द्यावो निहिता अन्तरस्मिन्तिस्रो भूमीरुपराः षड्विधानाः । गृत्सो राजा वरुणश्चक्र एतं दिवि प्रेङ्खं हिरण्ययं शुभे कम् ॥
7.87.e: On him three heavens rest and are supported, and the three earths are there in sixfold order.  The wise King Varuṇa hath made in heaven that Golden Swing to cover it with glory.

7.87.d: अव सिन्धुं वरुणो द्यौरिव स्थाद्द्रप्सो न श्वेतो मृगस्तुविष्मान् । गम्भीरशंसो रजसो विमानः सुपारक्षत्रः सतो अस्य राजा ॥
7.87.e: Like Varuṇa from heaven he sinks in Sindhu, like a white-shining spark, a strong wild creature.  Ruling in depths and meting out the region, great saving power hath he, this world's Controller.

7.87.d: यो मृळयाति चक्रुषे चिदागो वयं स्याम वरुणे अनागाः । अनु व्रतान्यदितेर्ऋधन्तो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.87.e: Before this Varuṇa may we be sinless him who shows mercy even to the sinner-  While we are keeping Aditi's ordinances. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.88.d: प्र शुन्ध्युवं वरुणाय प्रेष्ठां मतिं वसिष्ठ मीळ्हुषे भरस्व । य ईमर्वाञ्चं करते यजत्रं सहस्रामघं वृषणं बृहन्तम् ॥
7.88.e: PRESENT to Varuṇa thine hymn, Vasiṣṭha, bright, most delightful to the Bounteous Giver,  Who bringeth on to us the Bull, the lofty, the Holy, laden with a thousand treasures.

7.88.d: अधा न्वस्य संदृशं जगन्वानग्नेरनीकं वरुणस्य मंसि । स्व१र्यदश्मन्नधिपा उ अन्धोऽभि मा वपुर्दृशये निनीयात् ॥
7.88.e: And now, as I am come before his presence, I take the face of Varuṇa for Agni's.  So might he bring-Lord also of the darkness-the light in heaven that I may see its beauty!

7.88.d: आ यद्रुहाव वरुणश्च नावं प्र यत्समुद्रमीरयाव मध्यम् । अधि यदपां स्नुभिश्चराव प्र प्रेङ्ख ईङ्खयावहै शुभे कम् ॥
7.88.e: When Varuṇa and I embark together and urge our boat into the midst of ocean,  We, when we ride o’er ridges of the waters, will swing within that swing and there be happy.

7.88.d: वसिष्ठं ह वरुणो नाव्याधादृषिं चकार स्वपा महोभिः । स्तोतारं विप्रः सुदिनत्वे अह्नां यान्नु द्यावस्ततनन्यादुषासः ॥
7.88.e: Varuṇa placed Vasiṣṭha in the vessel, and deftly with his niight made him a Ṛṣi.  When days shone bright the Sage made him a singer, while the heavens broadened and the Dawns were lengthened.

7.88.d: क्व१ त्यानि नौ सख्या बभूवुः सचावहे यदवृकं पुरा चित् । बृहन्तं मानं वरुण स्वधावः सहस्रद्वारं जगमा गृहं ते ॥
7.88.e: What hath become of those our ancient friendships, when without enmity we walked together?  I, Varuṇa, thou glorious Lord, have entered thy lofty home, thine house with thousand portals.

7.88.d: य आपिर्नित्यो वरुण प्रियः सन्त्वामागांसि कृणवत्सखा ते । मा त एनस्वन्तो यक्षिन्भुजेम यन्धि ष्मा विप्रः स्तुवते वरूथम् ॥
7.88.e: If he, thy true ally, hath sinned against thee, still, Varuṇa, he is the friend thou lovedst.  Let us not, Living One, as sinners I know thee: give shelter, as a Sage, to him who lauds thee.

7.88.d: ध्रुवासु त्वासु क्षितिषु क्षियन्तो व्य१स्मत्पाशं वरुणो मुमोचत् । अवो वन्वाना अदितेरुपस्थाद्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.88.e: While we abide in these fixed habitations, and from the lap of Aditi win favour,  May Varuṇa untie the bond that binds us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.89.d: मो षु वरुण मृन्मयं गृहं राजन्नहं गमम् । मृळा सुक्षत्र मृळय ॥
7.89.e: LET me not yet, King Varuṇa, enter into the house of clay:  Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.

7.89.d: यदेमि प्रस्फुरन्निव दृतिर्न ध्मातो अद्रिवः । मृळा सुक्षत्र मृळय ॥
7.89.e: When, Thunderer! I move along tremulous like a wind-blown skin,  Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.

7.89.d: क्रत्वः समह दीनता प्रतीपं जगमा शुचे । मृळा सुक्षत्र मृळय ॥
7.89.e: O Bright and Powerful God, through want of strength I erred and went astray  Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.

7.89.d: अपां मध्ये तस्थिवांसं तृष्णाविदज्जरितारम् । मृळा सुक्षत्र मृळय ॥
7.89.e: Thirst found thy worshipper though he stood in the midst of water-fijods:  Have mercy, spare me, Mighty Lord.

7.89.d: यत्किं चेदं वरुण दैव्ये जनेऽभिद्रोहं मनुष्या३श्चरामसि । अचित्ती यत्तव धर्मा युयोपिम मा नस्तस्मादेनसो देव रीरिषः ॥
7.89.e: O Varuṇa, whatever the offence may be which we as men commit against the heavenly host,  When through our want of thought we violate thy laws, punish us not, O God, for that iniquity.

7.90.d: प्र वीरया शुचयो दद्रिरे वामध्वर्युभिर्मधुमन्तः सुतासः । वह वायो नियुतो याह्यच्छा पिबा सुतस्यान्धसो मदाय ॥
7.90.e: To you pure juice, rich in meath, are offered by priest: through longing for the Pair of Heroes.  Drive, Vāyu, bring thine harnessed horses hither: drink the pressed Soma till it make thee joyful.

7.90.d: ईशानाय प्रहुतिं यस्त आनट् छुचिं सोमं शुचिपास्तुभ्यं वायो । कृणोषि तं मर्त्येषु प्रशस्तं जातोजातो जायते वाज्यस्य ॥
7.90.e: Whoso to thee, the Mighty, brings oblation, pure Soma unto thee, pure-drinking Vāyu,  That man thou makest famous among mortals: to him strong sons are born in quick succession.

7.90.d: राये नु यं जज्ञतू रोदसीमे राये देवी धिषणा धाति देवम् । अध वायुं नियुतः सश्चत स्वा उत श्वेतं वसुधितिं निरेके ॥
7.90.e: The God whom both these worlds brought forth for riches, whom heavenly Dhiṣaṇā for our wealth appointeth,  His team of harnessed horses waits on Vāyu, and, foremost, on the radiant Treasure-bearer.

7.90.d: उच्छन्नुषसः सुदिना अरिप्रा उरु ज्योतिर्विविदुर्दीध्यानाः । गव्यं चिदूर्वमुशिजो वि वव्रुस्तेषामनु प्रदिवः सस्रुरापः ॥
7.90.e: The spotless Dawns with fair bright days have broken; they found the spacious light when they were shining.  Eagerly they disclosed the stall of cattle: floods streamed for them as in the days aforetime.

7.90.d: ते सत्येन मनसा दीध्यानाः स्वेन युक्तासः क्रतुना वहन्ति । इन्द्रवायू वीरवाहं रथं वामीशानयोरभि पृक्षः सचन्ते ॥
7.90.e: These with their truthful spirit, shining brightly, move on provided with their natural insight.  Viands attend the car that beareth Heroes, your car, ye Sovran Pair, Indra and Vāyu.

7.90.d: ईशानासो ये दधते स्वर्णो गोभिरश्वेभिर्वसुभिर्हिरण्यैः । इन्द्रवायू सूरयो विश्वमायुरर्वद्भिर्वीरैः पृतनासु सह्युः ॥
7.90.e: May these who give us heavenly light, these rulers, with gifts of kine and horses, gold and treasures.  These princes, through full life, Indra and Vāyu! o’ercome in battle with their steeds and heroes.

7.90.d: अर्वन्तो न श्रवसो भिक्षमाणा इन्द्रवायू सुष्टुतिभिर्वसिष्ठाः । वाजयन्तः स्ववसे हुवेम यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.90.e: Like coursers seeking fame will we Vasisthas, O Indra-Vāyu, with our fair laudations.  Exerting all our power call you to aid us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.91.d: कुविदङ्ग नमसा ये वृधासः पुरा देवा अनवद्यास आसन् । ते वायवे मनवे बाधितायावासयन्नुषसं सूर्येण ॥
7.91.e: WERE not in sooth, the Gods aforetime blameless, whose pleasure was increased by adoration?  For Vāyu and for man in his affliction they caused the Morning to arise with Sūrya.

7.91.d: उशन्ता दूता न दभाय गोपा मासश्च पाथः शरदश्च पूर्वीः । इन्द्रवायू सुष्टुतिर्वामियाना मार्डीकमीट्टे सुवितं च नव्यम् ॥
7.91.e: Guardians infallible, eager as envoys' preserve us safe through many months and autumns.  Addressed to you, our fair praise, Indra-Vāyu, implores your favour and renewed well-being.

7.91.d: पीवोअन्नाँ रयिवृधः सुमेधाः श्वेतः सिषक्ति नियुतामभिश्रीः । ते वायवे समनसो वि तस्थुर्विश्वेन्नरः स्वपत्यानि चक्रुः ॥
7.91.e: Wise, bright, arranger of his teams, he. seeketh men with rich food whose treasures are abundant.  They have arranged them of one mind with Vāyu: the men have wrought all noble operations.

7.91.d: यावत्तरस्तन्वो३ यावदोजो यावन्नरश्चक्षसा दीध्यानाः । शुचिं सोमं शुचिपा पातमस्मे इन्द्रवायू सदतं बर्हिरेदम् ॥
7.91.e: So far as native power and strength permit you, so far as men behold whose eyes have vision,  O ye pure-drinkers, drink with us pure Soma: sit on this sacred grass, Indra and Vāyu.

7.91.d: नियुवाना नियुतः स्पार्हवीरा इन्द्रवायू सरथं यातमर्वाक् । इदं हि वां प्रभृतं मध्वो अग्रमध प्रीणाना वि मुमुक्तमस्मे ॥
7.91.e: Driving down teams that bear the lovely Heroes, hitherward, Indra-Vāyu, come together.  To you this prime of savoury juice is offered: here loose your horses and be friendly-minded.

7.91.d: या वां शतं नियुतो याः सहस्रमिन्द्रवायू विश्ववाराः सचन्ते । आभिर्यातं सुविदत्राभिरर्वाक्पातं नरा प्रतिभृतस्य मध्वः ॥
7.91.e: Your hundred and your thousand teams, O Indra and Vāyu, all-munificent, which attend you,  With these most gracious-minded come ye hither, and drink, O Heroes of the meath we offer.

7.91.d: अर्वन्तो न श्रवसो भिक्षमाणा इन्द्रवायू सुष्टुतिभिर्वसिष्ठाः । वाजयन्तः स्ववसे हुवेम यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.91.e: Like coursers seeking fame will we Vasisthas, O Indra-Vāyu, with our fair laudations,  Exerting all our powe-,, call you to aid us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.92.d: आ वायो भूष शुचिपा उप नः सहस्रं ते नियुतो विश्ववार । उपो ते अन्धो मद्यमयामि यस्य देव दधिषे पूर्वपेयम् ॥
7.92.e: O VĀYU, drinker of the pure, be near us: a thousand teams are thine, Allbounteous Giver.  To thee the rapture-bringing juice is offered, whose first draught, God, thou takest as thy portion.

7.92.d: प्र सोता जीरो अध्वरेष्वस्थात्सोममिन्द्राय वायवे पिबध्यै । प्र यद्वां मध्वो अग्रियं भरन्त्यध्वर्यवो देवयन्तः शचीभिः ॥
7.92.e: Prompt at the holy rites forth came the presser with Soma-draughts for Indra and for Vāyu,  When ministering priests with strong devotion bring to you Twain the first taste of the Soma.

7.92.d: प्र याभिर्यासि दाश्वांसमच्छा नियुद्भिर्वायविष्टये दुरोणे । नि नो रयिं सुभोजसं युवस्व नि वीरं गव्यमश्व्यं च राधः ॥
7.92.e: The teams wherewith thou seekest him who offers, within his home, O Viyu, to direct him,  Therewith send wealth: to us with full enjoyment, a hero son and gifts of kine and horses.

7.92.d: ये वायव इन्द्रमादनास आदेवासो नितोशनासो अर्यः । घ्नन्तो वृत्राणि सूरिभिः ष्याम सासह्वांसो युधा नृभिरमित्रान् ॥
7.92.e: Near to the Gods and making Indra joyful, devout and ofFering precious gifts to Vāyu,  Allied with princes, smiting down the hostile, may we with heroes conquer foes in battle.

7.92.d: आ नो नियुद्भिः शतिनीभिरध्वरं सहस्रिणीभिरुप याहि यज्ञम् । वायो अस्मिन्त्सवने मादयस्व यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.92.e: With thy yoked teams in hundreds and in thousands come to our sacrifice and solemn worship.  Come, Vāyu, make thee glad at this libation. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.93.d: शुचिं नु स्तोमं नवजातमद्येन्द्राग्नी वृत्रहणा जुषेथाम् । उभा हि वां सुहवा जोहवीमि ता वाजं सद्य उशते धेष्ठा ॥
7.93.e: SLAYERS of enemies, Indra and Agni, accept this day our new-born pure laudation.  Again, again I call you prompt to listen, best to give quickly strength to him who craves it.

7.93.d: ता सानसी शवसाना हि भूतं साकंवृधा शवसा शूशुवांसा । क्षयन्तौ रायो यवसस्य भूरेः पृङ्क्तं वाजस्य स्थविरस्य घृष्वेः ॥
7.93.e: For ye were strong to gain, exceeding mighty, growing together, waxing in your vigour.  Lords of the pasture filled with ample riches, bestow upon us strength both fresh and lasting.

7.93.d: उपो ह यद्विदथं वाजिनो गुर्धीभिर्विप्राः प्रमतिमिच्छमानाः । अर्वन्तो न काष्ठां नक्षमाणा इन्द्राग्नी जोहुवतो नरस्ते ॥
7.93.e: Yea when the strong have entered our assembly, and singers seeking with their hymns your favour,  They are like steeds who come into the race-course, those men who call aloud on Indra-Agni.

7.93.d: गीर्भिर्विप्रः प्रमतिमिच्छमान ईट्टे रयिं यशसं पूर्वभाजम् । इन्द्राग्नी वृत्रहणा सुवज्रा प्र नो नव्येभिस्तिरतं देष्णैः ॥
7.93.e: The singer, seeking with his hymns your favour, begs splendid riches of their first possessor.  Further us with new bounties, Indra-Agni, armed with strong thunder, slayers of the foeman.

7.93.d: सं यन्मही मिथती स्पर्धमाने तनूरुचा शूरसाता यतैते । अदेवयुं विदथे देवयुभिः सत्रा हतं सोमसुता जनेन ॥
7.93.e: When two great hosts, arrayed against each other, meet clothed with brightness, in the fierce encounter  Stand ye beside the godly, smite the godless; and still assist the men who press the Soma.

7.93.d: इमामु षु सोमसुतिमुप न एन्द्राग्नी सौमनसाय यातम् । नू चिद्धि परिमम्नाथे अस्माना वां शश्वद्भिर्ववृतीय वाजैः ॥
7.93.e: To this our Soma-pressing, Indra-Agni, come ye prepared to show your loving-kindness,  For not at any time have ye despised us. So may I draw you with all strengthenings hither.

7.93.d: सो अग्न एना नमसा समिद्धोऽच्छा मित्रं वरुणमिन्द्रं वोचेः । यत्सीमागश्चकृमा तत्सु मृळ तदर्यमादितिः शिश्रथन्तु ॥
7.93.e: So Agni, kindled mid this adoration, invite thou Mitra, Varuṇa, and Indra.  Forgive whatever sin we have committed may Aryaman and Aditi remove it.

7.93.d: एता अग्न आशुषाणास इष्टीर्युवोः सचाभ्यश्याम वाजान् । मेन्द्रो नो विष्णुर्मरुतः परि ख्यन्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.93.e: While we accelerate these our sacrifices, may we win strength from both of you, O Agni:  Ne’er may the Maruts, Indra, Viṣṇu slight us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.94.d: इयं वामस्य मन्मन इन्द्राग्नी पूर्व्यस्तुतिः । अभ्राद्वृष्टिरिवाजनि ॥
7.94.e: As rain from out the cloud, for you, Indra and Agni, from my soul  This noblest praise hath been produced.

7.94.d: शृणुतं जरितुर्हवमिन्द्राग्नी वनतं गिरः । ईशाना पिप्यतं धियः ॥
7.94.e: Do ye, O Indra-Agni, hear the singer's call: accept his songs.  Ye Rulers, grant his heart's desire.

7.94.d: मा पापत्वाय नो नरेन्द्राग्नी माभिशस्तये । मा नो रीरधतं निदे ॥
7.94.e: Give us not up to poverty, ye Heroes, Indra-Agni, nor  To slander and reproach of men.

7.94.d: इन्द्रे अग्ना नमो बृहत्सुवृक्तिमेरयामहे । धिया धेना अवस्यवः ॥
7.94.e: To Indra and to Agni we bring reverence, high and holy hymn,  And, craving help, softwords with prayer.

7.94.d: ता हि शश्वन्त ईळत इत्था विप्रास ऊतये । सबाधो वाजसातये ॥
7.94.e: For all these holy singers here implore these Twain to succour them,  And priests that they may win them strength.

7.94.d: ता वां गीर्भिर्विपन्यवः प्रयस्वन्तो हवामहे । मेधसाता सनिष्यवः ॥
7.94.e: Eager to laudyou, we with songs invoke you, bearing sacred food,  Fain for success in sacrifice.

7.94.d: इन्द्राग्नी अवसा गतमस्मभ्यं चर्षणीसहा । मा नो दुःशंस ईशत ॥
7.94.e: Indra and Agni, come to us with favour, ye who conquer men:  Let not the wicked master us.

7.94.d: मा कस्य नो अररुषो धूर्तिः प्रणङ्मर्त्यस्य । इन्द्राग्नी शर्म यच्छतम् ॥
7.94.e: At no time let the injurious blow of hostile mortal fall on us:  O Indra-Agni, shelter us.
Whatever wealth we crave of you, in gold, in cattle, or in steeds,  That, Indra-Agni, let us gain;

7.94.d: यत्सोम आ सुते नर इन्द्राग्नी अजोहवुः । सप्तीवन्ता सपर्यवः ॥
7.94.e: When heroes prompt in worship call Indra and Agni, Lords of steeds,  Beside the Soma juice effused.

7.94.d: उक्थेभिर्वृत्रहन्तमा या मन्दाना चिदा गिरा । आङ्गूषैराविवासतः ॥
7.94.e: Call hither with the song and lauds those who best slay the foemen, those  Who take delight in hymns of praise.

7.94.d: ताविद्दुःशंसं मर्त्यं दुर्विद्वांसं रक्षस्विनम् । आभोगं हन्मना हतमुदधिं हन्मना हतम् ॥
7.94.e: Slay ye the wicked man whose thought is evil of the demon kind.  Slay him who stays the waters, slay the Serpent with your deadly dart.

7.95.d: प्र क्षोदसा धायसा सस्र एषा सरस्वती धरुणमायसी पूः । प्रबाबधाना रथ्येव याति विश्वा अपो महिना सिन्धुरन्याः ॥
7.95.e: THIS stream Sarasvatī with fostering current comes forth, our sure defence, our fort of iron.  As on a car, the flood flows on, surpassing in majesty and might all other waters.

7.95.d: एकाचेतत्सरस्वती नदीनां शुचिर्यती गिरिभ्य आ समुद्रात् । रायश्चेतन्ती भुवनस्य भूरेर्घृतं पयो दुदुहे नाहुषाय ॥
7.95.e: Pure in her course from mountains to the ocean, alone of streams Sarasvatī hath listened.  Thinking of wealth and the great world of creatures, she poured for Nahuṣa her milk and fatness.

7.95.d: स वावृधे नर्यो योषणासु वृषा शिशुर्वृषभो यज्ञियासु । स वाजिनं मघवद्भ्यो दधाति वि सातये तन्वं मामृजीत ॥
7.95.e: Friendly to man he grew among the women, a strong young Steer amid the Holy Ladies.  He gives the fleet steed to our wealthy princes, and decks their bodies for success in battle.

7.95.d: उत स्या नः सरस्वती जुषाणोप श्रवत्सुभगा यज्णे अस्मिन् । मितज्ञुभिर्नमस्यैरियाना राया युजा चिदुत्तरा सखिभ्यः ॥
7.95.e: May this Sarasvatī be pleased and listen at this our sacrifice, auspicious Lady,  When we with reverence, on our knees, implore her close-knit to wealth, most kind to those she loveth.

7.95.d: इमा जुह्वाना युष्मदा नमोभिः प्रति स्तोमं सरस्वति जुषस्व । तव शर्मन्प्रियतमे दधाना उप स्थेयाम शरणं न वृक्षम् ॥
7.95.e: These offerings have ye made with adoration: say this, Sarasvatī, and accept our praises;  And, placing us under thy dear protection, may we approach thee, as a tree, for shelter.

7.95.d: अयमु ते सरस्वति वसिष्ठो द्वारावृतस्य सुभगे व्यावः । वर्ध शुभ्रे स्तुवते रासि वाजान्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥
7.95.e: For thee, O Blest Sarasvatī, Vasiṣṭha hath here unbarred the doors d sacred Order.  Wax, Bright One, and give strength to him who lauds thee. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
